title: AchievementManager::Update indexes _completed/_updateTimes by the save's instance count: heap OOB read+write when a save stores more instances than the achievement list
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (count mismatch between two arrays)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail ?Update@AchievementManager (0x18009e6c0) loops `while (uVar11 < *(int*)(this+0x20))` (the _instances size) over `*(char*)(uVar9 + *(this+8))` (_completed) and `*(this+0x30) + uVar9*8 += time` (_updateTimes). Retail ?Persist (0x18009e910) does `SerializeInt(&count)` then `Collection_Array_SetSize_InternalPtr_AchievementInstance(this+0x18, count)` with no comparison against the achievement list count. The port is identical.
reachability: Loading any save file (shared or downloaded) whose achievement block stores an instance count larger than the installed achievement list. Update runs every game tick whenever no user pack files are enabled, which is the unmodded default.
proof: Repro scratchpad/p8/src_engine_math_volume_pathfinding_picki_ub/ach_update_count.cpp (fz target p8ub_ach, built with achievement_manager.cpp, goal.cpp, goal_list.cpp, achievement_vtable.cpp, batchc_goallist_dtor.cpp). It builds the state Persist leaves after a save with instance count 2 against a 1-entry list (_completed and _updateTimes size 1, _instances size 2), with no user pack files, and calls Update. ASan: `heap-buffer-overflow achievement_manager.cpp:199:14 in Achievement::AchievementManager::Update ... located 0 bytes after 1-byte region` (_completed[1]). The same iteration then does `_updateTimes._data[1]._ticks += time` (an 8-byte heap write past the end). Later, _lastAchievementUpdate (never reset by Persist or RemoveAll) can index _instances out of range and dispatch through a garbage vtable.
root_cause: _completed and _updateTimes are sized from _achievements->_count in SetAchievements. _instances is sized from an untrusted int read from the save in Persist (gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:691). Update iterates count = _instances._size over all three arrays.
minimal_fix: fix.* row: in AchievementManager::Persist on read, reject the load or clamp it when count != _achievements->_count (or call Reset() instead), and reset _lastAchievementUpdate to 0. Alternatively, bound Update's loops by min(_instances._size, _completed._size).
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: AchievementManager::Persist sizes _instances from the save's count with no tie to _completed/_updateTimes; the next Update reads and writes those arrays out of bounds
bug_class: save-supplied count trusted across parallel arrays -> heap out-of-bounds read/write
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Persist 0x18009e910 (Ghidra): `if (stream->dir == 0) RemoveAll(this); count = *(int*)(this+0x20); rw->SerializeInt(&count); if (reading) Collection_Array_SetSize_InternalPtr_AchievementInstance(this+0x18, count); Object_InternalPtrArray_Serialize(...)`. There is no compare with _achievements->_count. Retail Update 0x18009e6c0 loops `0 < i < *(int*)(this+0x20)` (the _instances size) and writes `*(this+0x30)[i] += time` (_updateTimes) and reads `*(this+8)[i]` (_completed). Both arrays are sized by SetAchievements from the achievement list. The port is identical.
reachability: Loading a save: gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:691 calls AchievementManager::_singleton->Persist(stream) with no check on the count. A corrupted or crafted save, or one written against a different achievement list, with count > the list size gives an OOB write into _updateTimes on the first Update tick. This needs no pack files loaded, because Update returns early when there are. A count smaller than the list size lets _lastAchievementUpdate (not persisted, kept from the previous game) index _instances past its end.
proof: Repro achv_count_oob.cpp builds the state Persist leaves after a save whose count (4) exceeds a 1-entry achievement list: _completed and _updateTimes each hold 1 element, _instances holds 4. It then calls the real AchievementManager::Update. ASan result: `heap-buffer-overflow ... 0x502000000031 is located 0 bytes after 1-byte region` and `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow src/engine/achievement/achievement_manager.cpp:199:14 in Achievement::AchievementManager::Update(System::Time const&)`. That is the _completed[i] read. The same loop writes _updateTimes._data[i]._ticks one statement later. Build: fz.sh build p8_achv_count_oob plus all src/engine/achievement/*.cpp except the type records, with link stubs for serializer and persistence bodies that Update never reaches.
root_cause: Three arrays that must stay the same length are sized from two sources: _completed and _updateTimes from the achievement list (SetAchievements), and _instances from the save stream (Persist). Nothing reconciles them, and Update indexes all three with _instances._size.
minimal_fix: In Persist's read arm, reject the stream when count != _achievements->_count (or clamp it and Reset() the instances so the arrays match). Also clamp _lastAchievementUpdate to the new size. Because retail shares the behaviour, this would be a fix.* row.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: AchievementManager::Persist takes the instance count from the save without checking it against the achievement count; Update then writes past _updateTimes and reads past _completed, or indexes _instances with a cursor left over from the old array
bug_class: stale cursor / unchecked serialized count -> heap out-of-bounds write (save-file controlled)
label: retail
label_evidence: The port matches retail Persist 0x18009e910 and Update 0x18009e6c0 instruction for instruction; neither caps the count or resets the cursor at +0x40.
reachability: Every save load: GameUpdateLoop::Serialize (gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:691) calls Persist unconditionally. A save whose achievement-instance count is larger than the installed achievement list (36), for example a hand-edited save or one written under a different achievement list, with each persisted pointer null, makes the next Update with no user pack files write 8-byte values past the _updateTimes heap block. A count smaller than the old cursor _lastAchievementUpdate (Persist does not reset it) makes Update read _instances past its end and make a virtual call through that value.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (no diff: retail has the same defect). Retail Persist 0x18009e910, decompiled: `if (dir==0) RemoveAll(this); local=*(int*)(this+0x20); rw->vtbl[0xa0](rw,&local,0); if (dir==0) Array_SetSize_InternalPtr(this+0x18, local); InternalPtrArray_Serialize(ser, local, *(this+0x18));`. There is no comparison with _achievements->_count (*(*this)+0x28), which is what sized _completed (+0x08) and _updateTimes (+0x30) in SetAchievements. Retail Update 0x18009e6c0:
  18009e6e8: CMP dword ptr [RCX + 0x20],R8D      ; bound = _instances._size (from the save)
  18009e6f0: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]       ; _completed
  18009e6f4: CMP byte ptr [R8 + RAX*0x1],R15B    ; read _completed[i]
  18009e6f8: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x30]      ; _updateTimes
  18009e705: ADD qword ptr [RCX],RAX             ; _updateTimes[i] += time  (WRITE)
  18009e70a: MOV qword ptr [RAX + R8*0x8],R15    ; or _updateTimes[i] = 0  (WRITE)
  18009e714: CMP R9D,dword ptr [RBX + 0x20]
  18009e756: MOVSXD RAX,dword ptr [RBX + 0x40]   ; cursor, never reset by Persist
  18009e76c: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x18]
  18009e779: MOV RDI,qword ptr [RCX + RAX*0x1]   ; _instances[cursor], then virtual calls through it
Port lines that match: achievement_serialize.cpp:169-175 (count from the stream, then `_instances.SetSize(count)`, no cap) and achievement_manager.cpp:199-200 (`_updateTimes._data[i]._ticks += / = 0` for i < _instances._size), 213 (`_instances._data[index]->Update(...)` with index = _lastAchievementUpdate).
root_cause: Persist sizes _instances from the stream but leaves _completed and _updateTimes at _achievements->_count, and it does not reset _lastAchievementUpdate. Update uses _instances._size as the bound for all three arrays and trusts the cursor.
minimal_fix: In Persist on the read path, reject or clamp `count` to `_achievements->_count` (a save with a different count is treated as having no instances, or Reset() rebuilds them), and set `_lastAchievementUpdate = 0` after RemoveAll. As a retail-divergent hardening this would be a fix.* row.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: Scene::Update indexes Channel::channelFlags[8] / platformChannel[8] with the SoundEffect's sample index, unbounded: a SoundEffect with more than 8 samples writes past the Channel record
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (out-of-bounds write)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800df91c 'CMP dword ptr [RDI+0x38],0x0 ; JLE' (loop over effect->_samples._size) ; 0x1800df926 'LEA RBX,[R12+0x60] ; ADD RBX,R13' (channelFlags base) ; 0x1800df938 'LEA RDX,[R12+0x20] ; ADD RDX,R13' (platformChannel base). Both pointers step once per sample with no cap at 8. The port's `for (i = 0; i < effect->_samples._size; ++i) { uint8_t* flag = &ch->channelFlags[i]; Device::AudioChannel** pchan = &ch->platformChannel[i]; ...}` is a faithful transcription.
reachability: A SoundEffect resource (.rsc in a mod or package) that declares 9 or more samples, played as a 2D effect (PlayEffect) or a 3D one that gets a channel. _samples._size comes straight from SoundEffect::Serialize (SerializeInt + SetSize) with no cap.
proof: Repro scene_update_samples.cpp: Scene built by RtAudio_Scene_Ctor, 256 PlayEffect calls with a SoundEffect of 24 samples (startSeconds 0, one variant each), then Scene::Update(delta=1 tick). UBSan: 'audio_scene_update.cpp:455:38: runtime error: index 9 out of bounds for type uint8_t[8]'. Each started sample also stores `*pchan = placed; *flag |= 1`. For samples 8..15 this lands on handleTag / started and the following bytes; from sample 10 on, platformChannel[i] (+0x20+8i) lands in the next Channel (0x70 stride), and for channel 255 past the 0x7000-byte channel table.
root_cause: The Channel holds 8 per-sample slots, but the sample count comes from data and is never clamped (in the resource loader or in Update).
minimal_fix: Clamp the loop to 8 (`i < effect->_samples._size && i < 8`), or reject more than 8 samples in SoundEffect::Serialize. A fix.* row, because retail shares the overflow.
also: Scene::Update indexes Channel::platformChannel[8] / channelFlags[8] by sample index with no bound: a SoundEffect with more than 8 samples writes past the Channel and the channel table

title: Streamed music: Stream::Run reads 16 fixed 0x8b6-byte packets per block, but XwmaDecoder::DecodeChunk strides by the format's nBlockAlign, so any streamed track with nBlockAlign > 0x8b6 reads past Block::packets (heap over-read)
bug_class: out-of-bounds read (index/size from data without a bound)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail has no decoder: it hands the block to XAudio2 with AudioBytes = nPackets*0x8b6 (0x1800a1194 MOV EAX,R15D ; 0x1800a1197 IMUL EAX,EAX,0x8b6 ; 0x1800a119d MOV [RBP+0x70],EAX, the same count ReadFile at 0x1800a11e7 fills). XAudio2 never reads beyond AudioBytes. The port-only XwmaDecoder (Phase D.4 SDL-4 A5) reads packetCount * _blockAlign bytes, where _blockAlign comes from the WAVEFORMATEX (xwma_decode.cpp:172/185/309-310). Open accepts any non-zero blockAlign and, in the stream form (packets == nullptr), skips the bytes/blockAlign check (line 176).
reachability: Any streamed SoundBuffer (_streamed=1: the music player) whose xWMA format has nBlockAlign > 2230, for example a mod's music track encoded at a higher bitrate (4459, 8917 and so on are standard xWMA block sizes). Slot 3's read runs past the 4*0x8ba0 _buffers allocation. With nBlockAlign < 0x8b6 the decoder silently decodes the wrong byte ranges.
proof: Repro stream_blockalign.cpp (p8/src_engine_engine_src_engine_audio_ub). It does exactly what Run does: XwmaDecoder::Open(fmt{tag 0x161, 2ch, 44100, avg 12000, nBlockAlign 4459 (a standard xWMA block size)}, nullptr, 0, seek, 64), then DecodeChunk(0, 16, packets, pcm, MaxSamplesFor(16)) on a heap buffer of 16*0x8b6 = 35680 bytes (Block::packets). ASan: 'ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 4459 at 0x52d000008f60 ... #1 wmav2_decode_packet #2 Audio::XwmaDecoder::DecodeRange xwma_decode.cpp:310:13 ... located 0 bytes after 35680-byte region'. Retail side (Ghidra 0x1800a1170..0x1800a11e7): 'IMUL EDX,EDX,0x8b6 ; MOV R15D,0x10 ; ... IMUL EAX,EAX,0x8b6 ; MOV [RBP+0x70],EAX ; ... MOV R8D,[RBP+0x70] ; CALL 0x1800ace00' (ReadFile of nPackets*0x8b6 bytes into _buffers[slot]+0x40). Port line: 'const size_t pcmSamples = decoder.DecodeChunk(curSeg32, nPackets, block->packets, pcm, pcmSlotSamples);'
root_cause: The streaming loop keeps retail's fixed 0x8b6 packet stride and buffer size. The port's decoder that replaces XAudio2 reads packets at the format's nBlockAlign, and nothing checks that the two agree.
minimal_fix: In Stream::Run, treat the track as undecodable unless the format's nBlockAlign == kPacketBytes (or make XwmaDecoder::DecodeChunk take the chunk's byte count and refuse packetCount*_blockAlign > bytes), e.g. `const bool decodable = decoder.Open(...) && ReadU16(buf->_format + 12) == kPacketBytes;`

title: Stream::Run hands the decoder a ring slot of 16 fixed 0x8b6-byte packets, but the decoder copies each packet by the format's blockAlign (heap over-read past the slot / ring)
bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow read (stream size mismatch, port-only)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail Run (Runtime 0x1800a0f60) never strides by blockAlign. It reads nPackets*0x8b6 bytes into block+0x40 and hands XAudio2 exactly that byte count with the cumulative table. The port added XwmaDecoder::DecodeChunk (no retail counterpart), which reads packet i at chunk + i*_blockAlign and memcpys _blockAlign bytes (wmadec_glue.c:130).
reachability: Any streamed SoundBuffer (music) whose serialized WAVEFORMATEX has blockAlign > 0x8b6, e.g. from a mod's .rsc. Stream::Play starts Run on the stream thread, and the last ring slot (index 3) reads past the 4*0x8ba0 _buffers allocation.
proof: Repro stream_blockalign.cpp (scratchpad/p8/src_engine_engine_src_engine_audio_errors/): format tag 0x161, stereo, blockAlign 0x1000, Block ring new Block[4], then DecodeChunk(0,16,ring[3].packets,...), which is what Run line 386 does. ASan: 'heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 4096 at 0x7a88e4cab680 ... #0 memcpy #1 wmav2_decode_packet #2 Audio::XwmaDecoder::DecodeRange xwma_decode.cpp:310 ... 0 bytes after 142976-byte region' (142976 = 4*0x8ba0). Retail for contrast (0x1800a0f60): 1800a1172 IMUL EDX,EDX,0x8b6 ; 1800a1197 IMUL EAX,EAX,0x8b6 (byteCount) ; 1800a11c0 IMUL RCX,RCX,0x8ba0 ; 1800a11d0 ADD RCX,0x40 ; 1800a11e7 CALL ReadFile(byteCount) ; 1800a12ff MOV [RBP-0x2c],EAX (AudioBytes = byteCount) ; 1800a130b LEA RAX,[RCX+0x40] (pAudioData) ; 1800a1361 CALL [RAX+0xa8] SubmitSourceBuffer. Retail never reads blockAlign-sized strides from the slot.
root_cause: The port replaced XAudio2's xWMA consumer with XwmaDecoder. Run keeps retail's fixed 0x8b6 packet size for reading and slot layout, but XwmaDecoder::Open takes blockAlign from the resource's format with no check that it matches 0x8b6, and DecodeRange copies blockAlign bytes per packet.
minimal_fix: In Stream::Run, treat the track as undecodable unless the format's blockAlign == kPacketBytes (0x8b6); the existing !decodable path then skips the loop. Alternatively, have DecodeChunk take the chunk's byte length and refuse when packetCount*blockAlign > bytes.

title: Save-supplied animation layer handle indexes AnimationManager::_instances without a bound (heap overflow write in ResetAnimationState; reads in UpdateRootOnly / StaticRootVector / mesh skinning)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800fd930: 1800fd964 MOV ECX,[RAX+RBP+0xc] ; 1800fd968 TEST ECX,ECX ; 1800fd96a JS skip ; 1800fd96c SAR ECX,0x8 ; 1800fd96f MOVZX EAX,CL ; 1800fd972 LEA RBX,[RAX+RAX*2] ; 1800fd976 SHL RBX,4 ; 1800fd97a MOV RAX,[0x1801fe7b0] ; 1800fd981 ADD RBX,[RAX] ; 1800fd984 DEC dword [RBX+0xc]. The only test is the sign; there is no compare against _instances._size. The port matches line for line.
reachability: Loading a crafted or corrupted save (.sav). The first ResetAnimationState (model change or removal) or the first animated frame touches the bad index.
proof: Repro file: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_graphics_src_engine_video_ub/anim_handle_oob.cpp, built with the real animationstate.cpp. Inputs: AnimationManager with one Instance (48 bytes), one AnimationState::Layer with _handle = 0x0500 (instance 5, as Array<Layer>::Serialize 0x18005cb40 reads it from a save), then st.ResetAnimationState(). Command: wsl ~/fz.sh run gfxub_anim_handle 30 -runs=1. Output: `0x50400000038c is located 204 bytes after 48-byte region ... SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow animationstate.cpp:455:13 in Graphics::AnimationState::ResetAnimationState()`. The access is the `--inst->_refCount` write; on a zero count the same function also blanks the out-of-range record and SetSizes its two arrays.
root_cause: MeshInstance::Serialize (0x1800ff680, reached from ModelComponent at modelcomponent.cpp:177) reads every layer's _handle and _clipIndex from the save, and AnimationManager::Serialize (gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:692) reads the instance count independently. Nothing checks (handle >> 8) & 0xff against _instances._size, or handle & 0xff against that instance's _states._size, or _clipIndex against the group's clip count. The same unchecked handle is dereferenced by StaticRootVector (wave28_lane_gfxbody.cpp:520-523), meshinstance_draw.cpp:172, mesh.cpp:412/2227 and wave27_lane_gfxbig.cpp:770/881. The _clipIndex reaches AnimationGroup::GetAnimation (imul 0x70, no bound) at animationstate_transforms.cpp:432/456, mesh.cpp:1839 and wave27_lane_gfxbig.cpp:799. These are not the same root cause as known F-025, which is ModelComponent's mesh group/index.
minimal_fix: Validate once after load, where both arrays are known. After the save's AnimationManager and model components are read, set to -1 (or reset) any layer whose instance index >= _instances._size, whose state index >= that instance's _states._size, or whose _clipIndex is outside [0, group clip count). The existing `handle < 0` arms already handle -1 everywhere.

title: Key binding from settings.cfg indexes Device state arrays without a bound: heap OOB read (inputId) or null-base deref (device byte >= 3)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail ?Released@KeyMap@Input@@ (Runtime 0x1800a79b0), decompiled: `pDVar3 = 0; if (bVar1==0) pDVar3 = Device::_singleton + joy*0x1b0; else if (bVar1==1) pDVar3 = _singleton+0x6c0; else if (bVar1==2) pDVar3 = _singleton+0x1098; if (pDVar3[(ulonglong)pbVar2[lVar4+0x12]*0x18+7] != 0) ...`. This is the same unbounded inputId index and the same null base for device 3..127 as the port's DeviceArrayBase default-nullptr plus base[inputId].
reachability: Any user or tool writing settings.cfg (or the imported retail registry key) with an Input* value >= 0 whose low byte is >= 105 (keyboard), >= 13 (mouse) or >= 18 (joystick), or whose second byte is 3..127. Only exclusive bindings are loaded. The read happens on the next frame's input poll.
proof: Repro scratchpad/p8/src_engine_math_volume_pathfinding_picki_ub/keymap_inputid.cpp (fz target p8ub_keymap, built with src/engine/input/input.cpp). It calls RegisterInput(5,1,0,"CameraForward",true), then SetInput(5,0,1,255), which stores the same bytes KeyMap::Load stores for a settings.cfg value of 511 (device=(v>>8)&0xFF, inputId=v&0xFF), then Pressed(0,5). ASan: `heap-buffer-overflow input.cpp:355:47 in Input::KeyMap::Pressed ... 0x5210000033ae is located 3246 bytes after 4608-byte region` (the 0x1200-byte Device). The read is _keyboard[255] at Device+0x6c0+255*0x18. With a device byte of 3..127 (for example 768), DeviceArrayBase returns nullptr and base[inputId] reads null + k*0x18 + 7.
root_cause: keymap_load.cpp:270-276 accepts any non-negative strtol value from the user-editable settings file (`Input<Name>[Alt]=N`) and splits it into device=(N>>8)&0xFF and inputId=N&0xFF without checking either. ReadBoundState (GetValue/Pressed/Released) then indexes _keyboard[105], _mouse[13] or _joystick[j][18] by inputId and dereferences the nullptr DeviceArrayBase returns for device >= 3. This runs every frame.
minimal_fix: fix.* row (retail shares it): in KeyMap::Load, treat a value whose device is not in 0..2 or whose inputId is >= the device's input count (18/105/13) as absent (-2), so the RegisterInput default is kept. Alternatively, skip the slot in ReadBoundState when DeviceArrayBase returns null or inputId is out of range.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: KeyMap::Load trusts any settings.cfg Input* value: device/inputId bytes are stored unchecked and later index Input::Device past its 0x1200-byte object (or through null)
bug_class: unchecked file input -> heap out-of-bounds read / null deref
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Input::KeyMap::Load 0x1800a7190 (Ghidra decompile): `iVar5 = Crt_ParseInt10(value); ... if (iVar5 < 0) { if (iVar5 == -1) {dev=0xff; id=0} } else { *(char*)(node+0x10+slot) = (char)((uint)iVar5 >> 8); *(char*)(node+0x12+slot) = (char)iVar5; }`. There is no range check, and the port matches it. In retail the store was the registry, and the port reads the user-editable text file <SaveDirectory>/settings.cfg (persistence_settings.cpp).
reachability: Any 'Input<description>[Alt]=<n>' line in settings.cfg (hand-edited, corrupted, or written by another build) with n >= 0 whose high byte is not 0/1/2, or whose low byte is past that device's input count (keyboard 0x69, mouse 13, joystick 18). Configuration::Startup -> KeyMap::Load at boot. The first per-frame KeyMap::GetValue/Pressed/Released on that binding then reads out of bounds.
proof: Repro keymap_load_oob.cpp: the settings map holds the one pair 'InputTest'='511' (0x1FF), and an exclusive binding 'Test' has both slots unbound. KeyMap::Load() stores device[0]=1 (keyboard) and inputId[0]=0xFF. KeyMap::GetValue(0,5) then reads Device::_keyboard[255] (the array has 105 entries). ASan result: `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... 0x5210000033ac is located 3244 bytes after 4608-byte region` and `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow src/engine/input/input.cpp:348:50 in Input::KeyMap::GetValue(int,int) const`. Build: fz.sh build p8_keymap_load_oob src/engine/input/input.cpp src/engine/input/keymap_load.cpp. Other values: device byte 3..0x7F makes DeviceArrayBase return nullptr, so GetValue/Pressed/Released read null + inputId*0x18. Device 0 with a large inputId runs past the joystick blocks.
root_cause: Load splits the parsed integer into device = (v>>8)&0xFF and inputId = v&0xFF and stores both with no check that device is in {0,1,2} or that inputId is below that device's input count. The readers (ReadBoundState / DeviceArrayBase) trust the stored bytes as array indices.
minimal_fix: In KeyMap::Load, accept value >= 0 only when device is 0..2 and inputId is below that device's count (kJoystickInputCount / kKeyboardInputCount / kMouseInputCount). Otherwise treat the value like the absent sentinel (-2) and keep the RegisterInput default. Because retail shares the behaviour, this would be a fix.* row (src/ext) rather than a change to the faithful body.

title: ~PersistenceWorker frees the job's block tables and filename before ~Thread joins the worker: an in-flight save/load job reads (LoadJob: writes through) freed memory
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads: join after free (use-after-free on the worker thread)
label: retail
label_evidence: Ghidra Runtime-x64.dll 0x1800b7740: the member releases come BEFORE the SetEvent/WaitForSingleObject: `1800b7760 ADD RCX,0x70 / CALL 0x18002ac40` (_saves), `1800b776a LEA RCX,[RBX+0x60] / CALL 0x180024aa0` (_blockPtrs), `1800b7774 LEA RCX,[RBX+0x50] / CALL 0x18002a930` (_blockDescs), `1800b777e..1800b7799` String release of +0x30 (_pendingFilename), then `1800b77a8 LEA RAX,[0x180155f20]` (base vtable), `1800b77b6 CALL [0x18014b368]` SetEvent(hStop), `1800b77c3 CALL [0x18014b3c0]` WaitForSingleObject(hThread, INFINITE). The port reproduces this with C++ member-then-base order (Persistence.h members, System::Thread::ReleaseFields in ~Thread), so it is faithful; it is a finding because it is a use-after-free.
reachability: ~Persistence runs from the engine teardown (engine_lifecycle.cpp:877). A quit while the worker is still running a job reaches it, for example App::Quit from the pause menu while an autosave (AutoSaveDialog::Autosave, which does not pause the game) or a manual save is writing. SaveJob loops over the cached descs/blockPtrs for the whole write. LoadJob (UpdateList metadata) writes through the cached ptrs[i], which makes it a write-after-free. ext/background_save/background_save.cpp:311-327 already waits for the persistence write before teardown on its own path, so the window is known; the faithful (synchronous) path has no such wait.
proof:
ASan repro persist_worker_dtor_uaf.cpp, which uses the real IO::PersistenceWorker, System::Thread (thread.cpp) and the posix platform thread/event layer. A probe Run() caches _blockDescs._data, _blockPtrs._data and _size the way SaveJob does at persistence_worker.cpp:593-602, sleeps (standing in for the CRC + WriteFile of a large save), then reads descs[i].size. The main thread calls Start() and then deletes the worker. Output:
[probe] job started, descs=0x503000000160
[probe] destroying the worker
[probe] job reads descs[0].size now
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x503000000168 ... READ of size 4 ... thread T2
  #0 Probe::Run() persist_worker_dtor_uaf.cpp:47
  #1 System::Thread::ThreadFunc thread.cpp:206
freed by thread T0 here:
  #1 rtcoll::ArrayDtorImpl Collection.h:480
  #4 Collection::Array<RtIo::BlockDesc>::~Array Collection.h:564
  #5 IO::PersistenceWorker::~PersistenceWorker
The worker is joined only after this free, in System::Thread::ReleaseFields.
root_cause: The worker's shared job state (_blockDescs, _blockPtrs, _saves, _pendingFilename) lives in the derived PersistenceWorker. The thread is stopped and joined in the base System::Thread destructor, which C++ (and MSVC in retail) runs after the derived members are destroyed. Nothing waits for an in-flight job before those members are freed.
minimal_fix: In IO::PersistenceWorker::~PersistenceWorker(), stop and join the thread before the members die. Either call WaitForFinish() (hFinished is manual-reset and is reset by every enqueue, so this waits for the current job), or signal hStop and join there, leaving the base ReleaseFields join as a no-op. Plain hardening: it does not change any retail-visible state.

title: MemoryAllocator::Allocate wraps (size+7) and (total+8) for requests near 2^64: a huge request returns a small block, and 2^64-8 returns a block that stays on the free list
bug_class: integer wrap -> heap corruption
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800c6e60 does the same arithmetic with no overflow check: LEA R8,[RDX+0x7] / AND R8,-0x8 / LEA EAX,[RDI-0x8] / CDQE / ADD RAX,R8 / CMP RAX,8 / CMOVC RAX,RCX / LEA RBP,[RAX+0x8] / CALL GetFreeTagForSize(RBP). The port (allocator.cpp:425-431) is the same.
reachability: Any MemAlloc whose size comes from a negative or sign-extended int count. In the tree: package blob lengths (F-033, package_file_read.cpp:465), negative capacity from SetSizeCore's 32-bit treble, RtMemAlloc(n*8) / (n*2) helpers fed from stream counts. Crafted .pkg/.pkm mods and saves.
proof: Repro alloc_wrap.cpp: install a mmap platform seam, Construct + Startup(1,0), then call a.Allocate(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF8, 8) followed by a.Allocate(64, 8). Run in the ASan/UBSan fuzz tree with ~/fz.sh repro p8sys_alloc_wrap, it prints 'HEAP CORRUPTION: the 2^64-8 byte block and the next 64-byte block overlap' and aborts. Why: want = total + 8 wraps to 0, so GetFreeTagForSize(0) returns the first free block. The split arm then sets the handed-out tag's size to 0, so rem == tag; it rewrites the tag as a free block of the full size and calls LinkFreeTag. The caller gets tag+8 while the same block is still on the free list, and the next allocation returns the same memory. A request of 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (an int -1 sign-extended, the F-033 shape) gives size+7 -> 6 & ~7 = 0 -> total = 8, so a 16-byte block comes back instead of FatalOutOfMemory.
root_cause: Allocate turns size into want with unchecked uint64 adds. The caller-side sign extensions (MemAlloc((uint64_t)(int64_t)n * stride), the F-033 blobLen) all count on a huge request failing, but here it wraps to a tiny or zero-size request and succeeds.
minimal_fix: In Allocate (and the ASan seat is already fine): if (size > kMaxRequest /* e.g. 1ull<<42, the tag size field's range */) FatalOutOfMemory(..., true); before computing total. Equivalently, reject when size + 7 + align8 + 8 overflows.

title: Stale hFinished: Start() issued between the worker's `_runFlags &= ~1` and its SetEvent(hFinished) leaves hFinished signalled, so WaitForFinish returns while the next job is still running (Map::~Map then frees the PathfinderThread under a live A* job)
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads / lost hand-off (stale event)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800ca440 has the same order. 1800ca495 MOV RCX,[RBX+0x28] (hFinished); 1800ca499 AND dword ptr [RBX+0x8],0xfffffffe; 1800ca49d CALL [0x18014b368] (SetEvent). Start 0x1800ca610 is ResetEvent(hFinished) then SetEvent(hStart). The port's thread.cpp:209-211 matches this byte for byte.
reachability: Map::~Map (leave to menu, or load a save) while the pathfinder has a stranded command. A stranded command needs the lost-wake-up window: an enqueue while bit 0 is still set after the worker's last queueCount read. DrainQueue must also hit the clear/SetEvent window. Both windows are narrow, but the unit run shows the second one is hit easily once the first holds. The Loader is not exposed, because LoaderLoop::Shutdown waits on hFinished before the next Load.
proof: runflags_tsan.cpp is built at -O2 without a sanitizer against the real src/engine/system/thread.cpp, src/platform/posix/{thread,sync}_posix.cpp and src/platform/common/event_std.cpp. Each loop iteration does this: job 1 (trivial) Start(); poll `_runFlags & 1` until it is clear (the poll DrainQueue / the enqueuers use); at once job 2 (Run sleeps 20 ms, then stores done=2) Start(); WaitForFinish(); check done. Output: `STALE hFinished at iteration 12: WaitForFinish returned while job 2 still running`. It reproduces within a few dozen iterations. Interleaving: worker clears bit 0 (thread.cpp:210) -> main sees it clear and calls Start() (ResetEvent(hFinished), SetEvent(hStart)) -> worker runs EventSet(finished) for the OLD job (thread.cpp:211) -> main's WaitForFinish returns at once -> the worker wakes on hStart and runs the new job. In game: PathfinderThread::DrainQueue (keystone_a_gamedtor.cpp:238-253) does `if ((_runFlags&1)==0) Start();`, loops until queueCount==0 and then calls WaitForFinish(). The worker's Run pops the last command under the lock (queueCount -> 0) and then runs ApplyCommand/A* unlocked. With a stale hFinished, Map::~Map (keystone_a_gamedtor.cpp:266-270) runs ~PathfinderThread and MemFree(pathfinder) while the worker is still inside A*, using grid, results and the lock CriticalSection. The base ~Thread join comes only after the members are destroyed.
root_cause: ThreadFunc publishes 'not running' (bit 0 clear) before it signals hFinished. A caller that trusts the bit can therefore Start a new job whose hFinished the previous job's SetEvent then sets.
minimal_fix: A fix row (retail shares this). In ThreadFunc, signal hFinished before clearing bit 0 (EventSet(finished) then `_runFlags &= ~1`), with the clear as a release store. Alternatively, have Start() wait on hFinished when bit 0 is clear but the previous SetEvent is still pending. Either way a Start() issued after the bit clears comes after the old SetEvent.

title: UpdateEvents caches _events._data/_size before the drain: an event posted by a handler is a heap-use-after-free (after a realloc) or is silently dropped; retail re-reads both every iteration
bug_class: stale pointer across a callback that can reallocate (use-after-free) / lost events
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x18011fc60 reloads the array base [RBX+0x48] at the top of every iteration and compares against [RBX+0x50] after every call. The port hoists both into locals (`const int32_t count = _events._size; Event* const data = _events._data;`) and iterates `data[i]` for i < count.
reachability: Any event appended to UserInterface::_events while UpdateEvents is draining. The in-tree producer reachable from a handler is CloseDialog: when a handler closes the current drag-drop dialog, CloseDialog appends the 0xd drag-cancel event (userinterface_close.cpp:326) and calls EndDragDrop. Its own nested UpdateEvents call is a no-op under the +0x88 guard, so the event lands in the array being drained. Any exe-side dialog or controller that queues a UI event from OnElementEvent does the same. With the array at capacity the append reallocates and frees the old buffer. The port's next iteration then reads the freed buffer and calls a virtual through a pointer loaded from freed memory. Below capacity the event is dropped where retail delivers it, a behaviour divergence.
proof:
ASan repro (built and run): C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_ui_errors/update_events_stale.cpp plus stubs.cpp in the same folder (link stubs only), with real sources src/engine/ui/userinterface.cpp and src/engine/io/encoding.cpp. Built with fz.sh build ui_update_events_stale. The repro queues six events, so the size equals the capacity of 6 (1, then 6 by the 3x rule). The DialogInstance subclass's OnElementEvent posts one more event through RtColl_ArraySetSizeFill_180033690 on its first call, the same helper CloseDialog's drag-cancel arm uses. Result: `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free src/engine/ui/userinterface.cpp:1058:50 in UI::UserInterface::UpdateEvents()`; the freed block was allocated by rtcoll::SetSizeCore (array.cpp:2269). GHIDRA-DIFF retail 0x18011fc60:
18011fc90: MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x48]   ; base re-read EVERY iteration
18011fc94: ADD RDX,RSI
18011fc9b: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RDX]
18011fcd1: CALL qword ptr [R10 + 0x40]      ; OnElementEvent
18011fcd5: INC EDI
18011fcd7: ADD RSI,0x30
18011fcdb: CMP EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0x50]   ; size re-read EVERY iteration
18011fcde: JL 0x18011fc90
18011fce9: CALL 0x180079df0                 ; clear
Port (userinterface.cpp:1051-1058): `const int32_t count = _events._size; Event* const data = _events._data; for (int32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) { const Event& ev = data[i]; ... ev.dialog->OnElementEvent(...); } _events._size = 0;`. Without a realloc, retail still dispatches an event appended during the drain. The port never visits it, then `_size = 0` discards it.
root_cause: The transcription hoisted `_events._data` and `_events._size` out of the dispatch loop. Retail treats both as live across the virtual OnElementEvent call, which can append to `_events` and reallocate it.
minimal_fix: Match retail: `for (int32_t i = 0; i < _events._size; ++i) { const Event ev = _events._data[i]; Object::InternalPtr<UI::Element> elem(ev.element); ev.dialog->OnElementEvent(&elem, ev.eventId, ev.arg14, ev.arg18, ev.arg1C, ev.arg20, ev.userData); }`. Re-read the base and the bound on every iteration and copy the record out before the call.

title: CompleteRoad's saved roadTileIndex indexes Map::cells unbounded in FinishRoadCell (out-of-bounds write: footprintCount, +0x2A/+0x2B, terrain type)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (OOB write)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400c5880 serializes +0x20 as a plain int. Retail 0x14009c640 indexes the cell array with it and has no bound. The port is the same.
reachability: A save holding a CompleteRoad action (a builder carrying a road tile) with roadTileIndex < 0 or >= size*size. The action's AbstractImpl runs on the first tick after the load and writes 1-2 bytes at cells + idx*0x30, plus the terrain sidecar and height grid writes inside SetTerrainType / ResetTerrainHeights.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (identical, faithful): retail 0x14009c640: 'MOVSXD RBX,EDX / LEA RDX,[RBX + RBX*0x2] / SHL RDX,0x4 / ADD RDX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x80] / CMP R9D,0x2 / JNZ 0x14009c67a / DEC byte ptr [RDX + 0x28] / MOV word ptr [RDX + 0x2a],0xff / ... 14009c67a: MOV byte ptr [RDX + 0x2b],R8B / ... CALL 0x14009f2f0'. Retail 0x1400c5880 (CompleteRoad_Persist): 'IO::Serializer::Serialize(local_30,(int *)(param_1 + 0x20),(char *)0x0)'. Port: completeroad.cpp:36 'ser.Serialize(roadTileIndex, nullptr);' then completeroad.cpp:49 'm_game->FinishRoadCell(roadTileIndex, roadDirection, roadType)', then action_pf_roots_road.cpp:212 'lVar4 = &cells.GetData()[param_2];' and writes through lVar4 (footprintCount - 1, field_0x2A / 0x2B, or field_0x2B), then SetTerrainType(param_2, ...) and ResetTerrainHeights on row/col derived from it.

label: retail

title: MoveTo::Persist reads pathCount from the save and serializes that many ints into the fixed path[0x100]: heap overflow of the 0x480-byte MoveTo
bug_class: array index / count from data without a bound (heap-buffer-overflow write)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400c8ec0 does the same three calls with no clamp: Serialize(int*)(+0x64); Serialize(int*)(+0x60); Serialize(*(int*)(this+0x64), (int*)(this+0x68)). The port matches it line for line (moveto.cpp:161-165).

WRITE of size 4 ... #1 IO::MemoryStream::Read memory_stream.cpp:74 #2 IO::BinaryReader::SerializeInt #3 IO::BinaryReader::SerializeIntArray(int,int*,const char*) #4 LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput moveto_pathcount.cpp:50', located 0 bytes after the 1152-byte region.   14011b692: MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSI + 0x28]      ; desc->_materials

title: Save path frees entities marked this frame without the deferred drain's dialog-close, tool-clear and scene-unlink nets (UAF on pinned info panels and Graphics::Scene nodes)
bug_class: C1 side table / cached pointer outlives the entity (use after free)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail EntityList::Update 0x1400c4090 drains removalList at its own tail (0x1400c434f..0x1400c43c4), so the list is empty when the UI's save runs later in the frame, and retail's info dialogs hold a strong data-source ref. The port moved the drain to the top of the NEXT Update (UpdateImpl step 0, 'SA DEVIATION', KPI row 792). It added the nets that make that deferral safe (EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities, EntityList_ClearToolSelectionForDyingEntities, AuditDyingEntity) only to DrainRemovals. FlushForSerialize, the other removal path, never got them.
reachability: Any save (the autosave timer or a pause-menu save) taken after a sim frame that marked an entity: a tree felled, food eaten, a citizen dying, a demolish. Marks happen in almost every frame of a running town. A crash needs one of the following too: a pinned info panel on the marked entity, the EditTool selection on it, or the mark-before-registration model/particle case that the net measured at 40% of frees.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail EntityList::Update 0x1400c4090 tail (end of the same Update, after the bucket loop):
1400c434f: MOVSXD RDI,dword ptr [R12 + 0xd8]   ; removalList._size
1400c4357: TEST EDI,EDI
1400c435e: CALL 0x1400c3bd0                    ; PreUpdate
1400c4366: CALL 0x1400c3ab0                    ; PostUpdateStaging
1400c438e: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + RBX*0x8]
1400c439d: CALL 0x1400c38e0                    ; RemoveEntity
1400c43c4: JMP 0x1400032e0                     ; removalList.SetSize(0)
Retail's head (0x1400c40a5..0x1400c40b1) runs only time += and PreUpdate, with no drain.
Port: UpdateImpl calls DrainRemovals() at the TOP of the next Update (entitylist.cpp:819). That leaves removalList holding every entity marked during this frame's sim when GameUpdateLoop runs m_userInterface->Update (gameupdateloop.cpp:1162; the autosave timer and the pause-menu save run there). When paused, no Update runs at all, so the list holds the marks of the last sim frame. The save then runs FlushForSerialize (entitylist.cpp:1519-1535):
    for (...) { ComponentEntity* localIBP = removalList._data[i]; RemoveEntity(&localIBP); }   // delete, no nets
    removalList.SetSize(0);
The port's DrainRemovals (entitylist.cpp:1202-1224) does CloseDialogs + ClearToolSelection + AuditDyingEntity before each RemoveEntity. Its own comments say each net exists because the port frees while weak refs remain: a pinned ResidenceUI panel crashed in Slot7 on 2026-07-22, the EditTool outline-follow crashed in Sub7080 on 2026-07-23, and a scene model or particle registered after the mark caused the Graphics::Scene::Clean fault in 44 of 109 freed entities (2026-08-14). After the save frees the entities, the next DrainRemovals finds removalList empty, so none of the three nets ever runs for them.
root_cause: The one-frame drain deferral (a port-only SA DEVIATION) moved retail's end-of-Update drain, and the port made that move safe only inside DrainRemovals. FlushForSerialize (retail Serialize steps 2-3, faithful) relies on retail's invariants: the list is nearly empty after Update, and dialogs keep the entity's memory alive. Neither holds in the port, so the save path deletes entities that pinned dialogs, the EditTool selection and Graphics::Scene still reference.
minimal_fix: Put the deferral's nets on every removal path: before FlushForSerialize's RemoveEntity loop (and Shutdown's), call EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities() and EntityList_ClearToolSelectionForDyingEntities(), and run AuditDyingEntity(entity) per entity. The cleanest form is one helper used by DrainRemovals, FlushForSerialize and Shutdown. The alternative is ending the deferral: drain at the end of Update, as retail does at 0x1400c434f, once EntityUI holds the strong ref (KPI row 792's stated exit).

title: PlayerToolManager::Serialize walks the camera-view array with an unsigned loop: a negative saved count runs ~4G iterations of wild writes; retail skips the loop
bug_class: index bounds / signedness divergence (serialized count)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x140102920 tests the count as signed (TEST EAX,EAX / JLE) before the loop; the port compares i < (uint32_t)count.
reachability: Loading a save file (GameUpdateLoop serializer -> PlayerToolManager::Serialize, version 2). The count is a raw int32 from the save stream.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x140102920 (Application-x64.exe):
140102a08: MOV EDX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x50]
140102a0c: LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x70]
140102a10: CALL 0x14002e000          ; SetSize(count)
140102a15: MOV RBX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x70]
140102a19: MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x50]
140102a1d: TEST EAX,EAX
140102a1f: JLE 0x140102a8f            ; count <= 0: no element loop
140102a25: MOV EDI,EAX                ; loop counter = count
Port gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:448: `for (uint32_t i = 0; i < (uint32_t)count; i++) { PlayerCameraView& e = cameraViews[i]; e.position.Serialize(ser); ... ser.Serialize(e.used, nullptr); }`. A save whose camera-view count is negative (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFF) is skipped by retail. The port runs 4294967295 iterations, and Array::operator[](int) turns i into an int index. Each iteration writes 0x1C deserialized bytes per element past the 5-element (0x8C-byte) block that Load sized: a heap overflow WRITE. Once i passes INT_MAX the index goes negative and the writes land before the block.

title: WorldGeometry::Serialize sizes the height bytes as int32 gridSize*gridSize*4 (signed overflow), and when the result is <= 0 leaves _heightBytes uninitialised; retail always stores MemAlloc((int64)(g*g) << 2)
bug_class: signed overflow / 32-bit size truncation / uninitialised field read
label: port
label_evidence: Retail sign-extends g*g and then shifts in 64 bits for the allocation, and stores the result unconditionally. The port does the whole multiply in int32 and skips both the allocation and the store when the product is <= 0. The WorldGeometry ctor (retail 0x1400b00e0 and the port) never initialises +0x140.
reachability: Loading a save: GameUpdateLoop serializer -> WorldGeometry::Serialize. _gridSize (+0xC0) is a raw int32 from the save.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400b04d0:
1400b05ed: CALL 0x1400ac1e0           ; BuildTerrainMesh
1400b05f2: MOV EAX,dword ptr [R12]     ; gridSize
1400b05f6: IMUL EAX,EAX
1400b05f9: MOVSXD RCX,EAX
1400b05fc: SHL RCX,0x2                 ; 64-bit byte count
1400b0605: CALL qword ptr [0x140152b60] ; MemAlloc
1400b060b: MOV qword ptr [R14 + 0x140],RAX ; stored unconditionally
Port: `int byteCount = gridSize * gridSize * 4;` then `if (System::MemoryAllocator::_singleton && byteCount > 0) { heightBuf = MemAlloc(byteCount, 4); _heightBytes = heightBuf; }`. The retail ctor 0x1400b00e0 zeroes +0xc0..+0xf8 and +0x150.. but not +0x140, and the port ctor matches it. Cases:
- gridSize = 0x8000: g*g*4 = 2^32. That is signed-overflow UB; it wraps to 0, so the port leaves _heightBytes as heap garbage. UploadHeightImage then calls CopyToTexture(garbage, 0x8000, 0x8000), and ~WorldGeometry calls InternalMemFree on the garbage pointer.
- gridSize = 0x8080: wraps to 0x02010000. The port allocates 32 MB where retail asks for 4.03 GB, and UploadHeightImage then reads 0x8080*0x8080*4 bytes from it.
- gridSize = 0: retail stores MemAlloc(0); the port leaves the field uninitialised, and the dtor frees it.
root_cause: The allocation size was folded into a single int32 expression, and a port-only `byteCount > 0` gate also skips the store of +0x140, which only the load path ever initialises.
minimal_fix: Compute the size in 64 bits as retail does (`int64_t bytes = (int64_t)(gridSize * gridSize) << 2`; better still, reject gridSize outside [1, 0xB504]) and always assign `_heightBytes` on load (null on failure).

title: BuildTerrainMesh sizes its vertex scratch from _chunkIndexStride but FillTerrainVertices writes _fieldCC^2 records into it; both are raw save fields (heap overflow write)
bug_class: array index / size from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400ac1e0 does the same: Collection_Array_SetSize_TerrainVertex(&local_40, *(int*)(this+0xd4)), then FillTerrainVertices(this, chunk*col, chunk*row, *(int*)(this+0xcc), *(int*)(this+0xcc), scratch). Retail 0x1400ac880 writes width*height 16-byte records and also indexes the heights at +0xd8 with stride +0xd0, which nothing checks against the array count at +0xe0.
reachability: Loading a save: WorldGeometry::Serialize reads +0xC0, +0xC8, +0xCC, +0xD0, +0xD4 and the +0xD8 height count independently, then calls BuildTerrainMesh on load.
proof: Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_game_Game_ub/terrain_fill.cpp. It sets _gridSize=64, _chunkSize=32, _fieldCC=33, _fieldD0=64, _chunkIndexStride=1, allocates scratch[_chunkIndexStride] exactly as BuildTerrainMesh does, and calls FillTerrainVertices(0,0,33,33,scratch). Run with `fz.sh build gameub_terrainfill src/game/Game/serialize_heightmap_mesh.cpp && fz.sh run gameub_terrainfill 30 -runs=1`. Result: `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow serialize_heightmap_mesh.cpp:208:28 in WorldGeometry::FillTerrainVertices` (0 bytes after the 16-byte region allocated at terrain_fill.cpp:26).
root_cause: The mesh parameters (vertsPerSide, vertsPerChunk, row stride, grid) and the height array count are each read from the save, and nothing checks them against each other (vertsPerChunk == vertsPerSide^2, heights.size >= stride^2).
minimal_fix: Plain hardening in WorldGeometry::Serialize on load: require chunkSize > 0, gridSize % chunkSize == 0, vertsPerSide == chunkSize+1, vertsPerChunk == vertsPerSide^2, rowStride == gridSize+1 and _heights.size >= rowStride^2, and reject the save otherwise.

title: TutorialInstance::LoadNextScenario indexes the scenario list with Tutorial::currentStep without an upper bound
bug_class: OOB-index (array index from resource data without an upper bound)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400E0D70: `MOV RDX,[RCX+0x30]; CMP dword ptr [RDX+0x38],R14D; JL 0x1400e1175` (lower bound only), then `MOV RAX,[0x1401c3de8]; MOV RAX,[RAX+0x8]; MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [RDX+0x38]; MOV RCX,[RAX+0x20]; MOV RBX,[RCX+RDX*0x8]`. The port has the same single `scenIdx < 0` test and then reads `scenarioList->_resources[scenIdx]`.
reachability: Completing the last step of a tutorial whose definition (modded or crafted .rsc) names a scenario index past the GameContainer scenario list.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (faithful, both unbounded): retail `1400e0da6: CMP dword ptr [RDX + 0x38],R14D; 1400e0daa: JL 0x1400e1175; 1400e0dbb: MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [RDX + 0x38]; 1400e0dbf: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x20]; 1400e0dc3: MOV RBX,qword ptr [RCX + RDX*0x8]`. Port: `int scenIdx = tutorial->currentStep; if (scenIdx < 0) return; ... Object::External* resource = scenarioList->_resources[scenIdx];`. The read pointer is then passed to IsDerivedFromNullSafe, i.e. a vtable call through an out-of-bounds pointer.
root_cause: Tutorial::currentStep (+0x38) is a serialized int in the tutorial definition (tutorial.cpp:97) and is used as the next-scenario index. Nothing compares it with the scenario list's size.
minimal_fix: Return when `scenIdx >= scenarioList->_resources size` (alongside the existing `< 0` test). This is a fix.* row.

title: TutorialSetupDialog::OpenHighlightDialog indexes the template bucket's entities with the resource's toolbarIndex, with only an upper test (a negative value reads before the array)
bug_class: OOB-index (array index from resource data, signed lower bound missing)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400E2700: `MOV EAX,dword ptr [RCX+0x10]` (bucket count) `CMP EAX,dword ptr [RDI+0x70]; JLE 0x1400e291c` (signed: count > index only), then `MOVSXD R14,dword ptr [RDI+0x70]` ... `MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDX+0x8]; MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX+R14*0x8]`. The port mirrors it: `if (count > index) ... entities._data[index].Get()`.
reachability: A TutorialSetupDialog in modded or crafted tutorial resource data with a negative toolbarIndex, opened while a building of the toolbarRef template exists.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (no divergence, faithful): retail `1400e2805: CMP EAX,dword ptr [RDI + 0x70]; 1400e2808: JLE 0x1400e291c; ... 1400e2832: MOVSXD R14,dword ptr [RDI + 0x70]; ... 1400e286f: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]; 1400e2877: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX + R14*0x8]`. Port: `int index = toolbarIndex; if (count > index) { ... targetElem = found2->element.entities._data[index].Get(); }`. With a negative toolbarIndex (+0x70, serialized int at tutorialsetupdialog.cpp:134), the read lands before the heap block, and the value read is then used as the highlight dialog's target entity.

title: RefreshStepUI indexes Tutorial::steps with the save-loaded currentStep and no bound (heap OOB read, then virtual calls through the read pointer)
bug_class: OOB-index (array index from save data without a bound)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400E1260 has no bound either: `MOV RAX,[RCX+0x30]; MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [RCX+0x10]; MOV RDI,[RAX+0x28]; MOV RDI,[RDI+RDX*0x8]; CMP dword ptr [RDI+0x58],R13D` and then `CALL [RAX+0x40]` on each setup. StepExecute 0x1400E1DB0 calls 0x1400e1260 (at 0x1400e1e8b) BEFORE its only bound test `CMP EAX,[RBX+0x30]; JGE` at 0x1400e1e98, and that test is signed, so negative values pass it.
reachability: Loading a tutorial save whose TutorialInstance currentStep is >= the step count or negative: a crafted or shared save. Also possible after the last step if the instance is saved and later reloaded with its dialog lookup succeeding.
proof: ASan repro scratchpad/p8/src_game_Goal_src_game_Tutorial_src_game_ub/tut_refresh_oob.cpp (Tutorial with steps._size=1, TutorialInstance currentStep=1, call RefreshStepUI), built with build.sh tutrefresh ... src/game/Tutorial/tutorial_wave.cpp: `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 8 ... #0 TutorialInstance::RefreshStepUI() tutorial_wave.cpp:417:26 ... 0 bytes after 8-byte region`.
root_cause: TutorialInstance::Persist (0x1400e1520) loads currentStep from the save and only rewrites it when 0 < step < steps._size. A saved value >= steps._size or < 0 survives the load. stepDialog is not persisted, so the first StepExecute after a load runs RefreshStepUI before StepExecute's own `stepIndex >= stepCount` test. RefreshStepUI then reads steps._data[currentStep] and calls slot 8 on every entry of that pointer's setups array. A save with currentStep == steps._size (the value set after the last step completes) or a crafted negative value is enough.
minimal_fix: In RefreshStepUI, return when `idx < 0 || idx >= tutorial->steps._size`. Alternatively, clamp currentStep into [0, steps._size) in Persist on load. This is a retail bug, so it needs a fix.* row per AGENTS.md section 2.

title: ConsumeProduceWork_CreateActions allocates 0x38 bytes for a 0x40-byte ConsumeRawMaterial (heap overflow on every read of _field38)
bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (object built in undersized storage)
label: port
reachability: Every ConsumeProduceWork action build whose chosen recipe has inputs: the main production path of every crafting workplace.
proof:
ASan repro crm_alloc38.cpp (scratchpad/p8/src_game_Action_lifetime/). It calls MemAlloc(0x38, 8), exactly what WCP_Alloc(0x38) does, then runs the real 2-arg ctor and CheckEntity from consumerawmaterial.cpp, built with ASan+UBSan on WSL:
  ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... 0x5070000001a8 is located 0 bytes after 56-byte region [0x507000000170,0x5070000001a8)
  allocated by: AsanMemAlloc allocator.cpp:105 <- LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput crm_alloc38.cpp:19
  SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow src/game/Action/consumerawmaterial.cpp:214:10 in ConsumeRawMaterial::CheckEntity()

GHIDRA-DIFF: retail ConsumeProduceWork_CreateActions 0x1400bef70 allocates 0x40:
  1400bf446: MOV EDX,0x8
  1400bf44b: LEA ECX,[RDX + 0x38]      ; 0x40
  1400bf44e: CALL qword ptr [0x140152b60]  ; MemAlloc(0x40, 8)
  1400bf45d: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RDI]
  1400bf46b: CALL 0x1400c6440          ; ConsumeRawMaterial(storage)
Port, work_act_consume.cpp:301:
  obj = WCP_Alloc(0x38);            // LEA ECX,[RDX+0x30] => 0x38   <- wrong; the instruction is +0x38 => 0x40
ConsumeRawMaterial.h asserts sizeof(ConsumeRawMaterial) == 0x40.
root_cause: The comment on the allocation misread retail's `LEA ECX,[RDX+0x38]` as `[RDX+0x30]`. It looks copied from the CompleteTask allocation a few lines above, which really is 0x38. So the object is built in a block 8 bytes too small. Its last qword (+0x38: the reserve/consume flag _field38 and _pad39) lies outside the block. That field is read by AddMaterial (0x1400c64b0, called right after construction for each recipe input), AbstractImpl (0x1400c5f50), CheckEntity (0x1400c5e30, run on every action-stack clear) and Persist (0x1400c6120, on save). Reached whenever a ConsumeProduce workplace (blacksmith, tailor, etc.) builds its action chain for a recipe with inputCount > 0, which is every normal production cycle. Outside ASan builds the read lands in the allocator's slack or the next block, so the consume-mode branch is chosen from foreign heap bytes.
minimal_fix: In src/game/Work/work_act_consume.cpp:301, allocate `WCP_Alloc(0x40)` (or `sizeof(ConsumeRawMaterial)`) and fix the comment to `MOV EDX,8; LEA ECX,[RDX+0x38] => 0x40`.

title: RedecodeRange copies a stored block of up to 64 KB into a 32 KB stack page (stack buffer overflow on a package block whose uncompressedSize > 0x8000)
bug_class: size math / unchecked length (stack buffer overflow write)
label: ext
label_evidence: payload.cpp is ext.create_on_demand (header: 'NOT RETAIL'); retail has no re-decode path. The engine's own window read (compressed_stream_read.cpp:285, retail 0x1800a9755) trusts the same field, but with the row on, the payload's blocks are skipped by the engine (stream_locate.cpp Skip) and decoded only here, so this site is reached on its own.
reachability: ext.create_on_demand on (DX11 lazy_create.cpp:81/156, Vulkan lazy_create.cpp:61/117 -> Redecode -> RedecodeRange) and a package entry (for example a mod .pkg) whose block directory has a stored block (compressedSize 0) with uncompressedSize > 0x8000. RangeInStream only checks pos+len against (n-1)*32768 + last.uncompressedSize, so the oversized value passes it. The same missing bound also lets `last = (pos+len-1)>>15` exceed n-1, so the loop reads block headers past the directory.
proof:
Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_common_layout/redecode_stored.cpp. The entry is n=1, header {sourceOffset=12, compressedSize=0, uncompressedSize=0x9000}, followed by 0x9000 bytes; the call is RedecodeRange(entry, 12+0x9000, pos=0, len=0x9000, dst). ASan+UBSan (fz.sh build/run rc_layout_redecode):
==756==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow on address 0x72de7d708020
WRITE of size 36864 at 0x72de7d708020 thread T0
    #0 __asan_memcpy
    #1 CreateOnDemand::RedecodeRange(...) src/render/common/create_on_demand/payload.cpp:163:13
  This frame has 1 object(s):
    [32, 32800) 'page' (line 150) <== Memory access at offset 32800 overflows this variable
root_cause: `uint8_t page[kBlockBytes]` (0x8000) receives `std::memcpy(page, src, h.uncompressedSize)` with a uint16 size of up to 0xFFFF that is never checked against kBlockBytes. RangeInStream likewise never requires uncompressedSize <= kBlockBytes or block index < n. The later `to = min(h.uncompressedSize, ...)` also reads page past 0x8000.
minimal_fix: In RedecodeRange, return false when `h.uncompressedSize > kBlockBytes` or `b >= n` (n read from the entry). In RangeInStream, reject `last.uncompressedSize > kBlockBytes`, so the stream length and block count stay consistent. SkipIfWithin's copy of the length formula takes the same bound.

title: Device::PlayPlatform: nowTicks % (int64)(_durationSeconds / secondsPerTick) with no zero test (division by zero for a zero-length sound; float-cast overflow for a huge, inf or NaN duration)
bug_class: integer division by zero / out-of-range float->int
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800de856 'MOVSS XMM0,[RCX+0x24]' ; 0x1800de85b 'CVTPS2PD XMM0,XMM0' ; 0x1800de85e 'DIVSD XMM0,[0x1801fe728]' ; 0x1800de869 'CVTTSD2SI R8,XMM0' ; 0x1800de84c 'CQO' ; 0x1800de871 'IDIV R8' (no zero test). The port's ComputePlayPosition transcribes it: `const int64_t loopDurationTicks = static_cast<int64_t>(loopDurationTicksD); const int64_t remainderTicks = nowTicks % loopDurationTicks;`
reachability: Every PlayPlatform call (each sample that starts, 2D or 3D, and each music start) runs ComputePlayPosition. A SoundBuffer whose serialized _durationSeconds is 0 or below one timer tick (1 us), for example an empty or truncated sound in a mod package, crashes the game the first time it plays.
proof: Repro playplatform_zero_duration.cpp (includes audio_play_platform.cpp to reach the anonymous-namespace helper): SoundBuffer with _durationSeconds = 0, ComputePlayPosition(buf, 123456789, ...). UBSan: 'audio_play_platform.cpp:275:45: runtime error: division by zero'. On x86 this is a #DE crash in both retail and the port. In the same function, `static_cast<int32_t>(bytePosF)` (line 287) is a second unchecked float->int: seconds-in-loop times a bytes-per-second figure from the format can exceed INT32_MAX.
root_cause: The loop length in ticks is derived from a data float and used as a divisor and converted without range checks.
minimal_fix: If loopDurationTicks <= 0 (or the double is not in (0, INT64_MAX)), use remainderTicks = 0; clamp bytePosF to [0, INT32_MAX] before the cast. A fix.* row.

title: Save-supplied EffectSlot soundType indexes Scene::paused[5] and the stack array volumes[5] in Scene::Update (wild out-of-bounds read)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (out-of-bounds read)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800df741 'MOVSXD RSI,dword ptr [RBX+0xc]' ; 0x1800df745 'CMP byte ptr [RSI+R15*0x1+0x30],0x0' (paused[soundType], sign-extended, no bound). The soundType is serialized with SerializeUInt in RtAudio_Scene_SerializeEffectSlots (audio_effectslot_serialize.cpp, retail 0x180052683), and GameUpdateLoop serializes m_audioScene in the save (gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:693).
reachability: Loading a corrupted or crafted save: the Audio::Scene block of every save carries a soundType per live effect slot. A negative or large value gives a read up to +-2 GiB away from the Scene (a crash), or garbage pause and volume values.
proof: Repro scene_savetype.cpp: a fresh Scene, effects[0].idTag = 3 and soundType = 0x40000000 (the two fields the save's read arm writes), then Scene::Update. UBSan: 'audio_scene_update.cpp:328:17: runtime error: index 1073741824 out of bounds for type bool[5]'. The same value then reaches PlayEffect -> Channel::soundType -> paused[soundType] (line 424) and the stack read volumes[soundType] (lines 488/528).

title: Scene::Update: a sample with zero variants dereferences variants._data[0] through a null pointer
bug_class: null dereference from data (missing count check)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800df97c 'MOV EBX,[R9+RCX*0x1+0x10]' (variants._size) ; 0x1800df988 'TEST EBX,EBX' ; 0x1800df98a 'JNZ 0x1800df992' ; 0x1800df98c 'XOR EAX,EAX' ; 0x1800df98e 'MOV EDX,EAX' ; 0x1800df990 'JMP 0x1800df9f7' ; 0x1800df9fb 'MOVSXD RAX,EDX' ; 0x1800df9fe 'LEA RBX,[RAX+RAX*0x2]' ; 0x1800dfa02 'MOV R8,[R9+RCX*0x1+0x8]' (variants._data, null when the size is 0), which is then indexed for the variant. Port: `uint32_t pick = 0; if (variantCount != 0) pick = ...; const SoundEffect::Variant* const v = &sample->variants._data[pick]; ... v->pitchLow`.
reachability: A SoundEffect resource with a sample that declares 0 variants (RtAudio_SoundEffect_SerializeBuffers reads that count from the file). It crashes when the sample's start time comes into the window.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: the retail sequence above is identical to the port lines 467-480. Not run: the Array<Variant> of a sample whose serialized variant count is 0 has _data == nullptr (SetSize(0)), so v->pitchLow / v->buffer read through null + 0..0x14.

title: Animation::GetPoseAtTime divides by zero (IDIV) when a clip's loop frame is its end frame; other loop/frame values give an out-of-range float->int and negative key indexes
bug_class: integer division by zero / float->int out of range / unbounded index from resource data
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800faca0 has the same unguarded arithmetic: 1800facef DIVSS XMM2,XMM0 ; 1800facf7 CVTTSS2SI R10D,XMM2 (loopStart, no zero-span test) ; 1800fad2e MOV ECX,R9D ; 1800fad34 SUB ECX,R10D ; 1800fad37 CDQ ; 1800fad38 IDIV ECX ; ... 1800fad55 SUB R9D,R10D ; 1800fad58 CDQ ; 1800fad59 IDIV R9D. There is no test of frameCount - loopStart before either IDIV.
reachability: Any AnimationGroup resource, including a mod's .pkg (crafted or a careless loop point at the end frame), and save-supplied layer times. It is reached each frame through AnimationState::Update / AnimationManager::Update.
proof: Repro file: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_graphics_src_engine_video_ub/anim_pose_div0.cpp. It builds against the real src/engine/graphics/animationstate.cpp, relinked with link.sh in the same folder. Inputs: Animation {_startFrame 0, _endFrame 10, _loopFrame 10, _looping true, _frameRate 30, _boneCount 2, _frameCount 4}, Timer::_secondsPerTick 1e-7, time 1 s. Command: wsl ~/fz.sh run gfxub_anim_div0 30 -runs=1. Output: `animationstate.cpp:528:43: runtime error: division by zero` (SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer). On x86 this is #DE, which kills the process, as in retail.
root_cause: loopStart = (int)((loopFrame - startFrame) / (endFrame - startFrame) * frameCount). Every value comes from the AnimationGroup resource (Animation::Serialize) and none is checked. (1) loopFrame == endFrame gives loopStart == frameCount, so `whole % (frameCount - loopStart)` and `f1 % (frameCount - loopStart)` divide by zero as soon as a looping clip passes its last frame. (2) endFrame == startFrame with loopFrame != 0 gives 0/0 or x/0 (NaN or inf), and the float->int conversion of that is UB in C++. (3) loopFrame outside [start, end] makes the modulus negative or wrong, so f0/f1 leave [0, frameCount) and `keys + boneCount*f0` reads outside _keys. (4) A negative layer _time from a save makes `whole` negative, which indexes keys backwards. Animation::GetRootPoseAtTime (wave29_lane_gfxbody.cpp:715-735, retail 0x1800faaa0) repeats the same loopKey/keyCount arithmetic at a second site.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening at load, not in the hot path. In Animation::Serialize (reading), reject or clamp a clip whose frameCount <= 0, endFrame <= startFrame, loopFrame outside [startFrame, endFrame), or _keys._size != boneCount*frameCount. Then in GetPoseAtTime / GetRootPoseAtTime, treat frameCount - loopStart <= 0 as non-looping (clamp to frameCount-1) and clamp a negative `whole` to 0. That needs a fix.* row if it is to be kept beside the faithful body.

title: External::Load dereferences null on a resource whose serialized type id is not registered; a non-External type leaks the created object (and the port static_casts it to External* before the check)
bug_class: null dereference / invalid downcast from data-controlled type id
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800bc73b `MOV RCX,RBX` (RBX=0) followed by `MOV RAX,[RCX+0x10]`. The port keeps it on purpose through a volatile read (comment: FAITHFUL FAULT). The `static_cast<External*>(created)` at :330, before IsDerivedFrom, is port-only UB, the same shape as the InternalPtr finding.
reachability: Every resource load (FindOrLoad -> External::Load), including third-party mod .pkm packages. A compiled resource whose header type id (after the magic 0x5412a91f) is not in the type tree crashes the loader. One that names a non-External type leaks a factory object and, in the port, runs an invalid downcast.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (faithful): retail 0x1800bc620:
 1800bc705: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x98]   ; SerializeUInt(typeId) from the .rsc
 1800bc722: MOV EDX,dword ptr [RCX]       ; type-tree descent
 1800bc739: JNZ 0x1800bc722
 1800bc73b: MOV RCX,RBX                   ; miss -> RCX = 0
 1800bc73e: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10] ; null read
 1800bc742: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x20]   ; factoryFn
 1800bc751: CALL 0x1800c0390 ; IsDerivedFrom(External)
 1800bc758: JZ 0x1800bc845                ; bad -> created object never freed
Port :325-330: `infoSlot = &n->element.record.info; info = *infoSlot; created = info->factoryFn(); obj = static_cast<External*>(created);`, then the IsDerivedFrom test at :336.
root_cause: The type id read from the file is used for the factory lookup and for the downcast without validating either step.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening as a fix.* row: if the descent misses, set bad=true without calling factoryFn. Keep `created` as Base* until IsDerivedFrom(External::TypeId()) passes, and delete it on the bad arm.

title: InternalFactory::PersistObject dereferences null when the save names a type id that is unregistered or not an Object::Internal
bug_class: null dereference from data-controlled type id
label: retail
label_evidence: The retail disassembly does the same: a descent miss leaves RAX=RSI=0 and loads [RAX+0x10]; an IsDerivedFrom failure keeps RSI=0 (CMOVNZ) and loads [RSI+0x8]. The port comments say both derefs are deliberately unguarded.
reachability: Save load. InternalBasePtr::Serialize reads `type` (uint32) straight from the save and passes it to PersistObject while _persistIds[index] < 0. A type id that is unregistered, or that names a registered non-Internal type (an External resource type, say), faults at 0x10 or 0x8. Separate root cause from F-022 (that one is the index bound).
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (faithful): retail 0x1800bff10:
 1800bff5d: XOR ESI,ESI
 1800bff70: MOV ECX,dword ptr [RAX] ; descent over Factory type tree
 1800bff87: JNZ 0x1800bff70
 1800bff89: MOV RAX,RSI            ; miss -> RAX = 0
 1800bff8c: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]   ; null+0x10 read
 1800bff9f: CALL 0x1800c0390       ; IsDerivedFrom(Internal)
 1800bffa6: CMOVNZ RSI,RBX         ; not Internal -> RSI stays 0
 1800bffad: MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSI + 0x8]    ; null+0x8 read
Port internal_class.cpp:703 `found->element.record.info` (found may be null) and :719 `obj->_factoryIndex` (obj null when !IsDerivedFrom). The object built by factoryFn is also leaked on the non-Internal arm.
root_cause: The save-supplied type id is trusted twice: once for the type-tree lookup and once for the downcast to Internal. Neither result is checked.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening as a fix.* row: if `found == nullptr`, or `created` is not derived from Internal (delete `created`), treat the record as a null pointer. Leave _persistIds[i] unchanged and return nullptr instead of dereferencing.
also: InternalFactory::PersistObject dereferences null when a save names an unregistered type or a type that is not an Internal

title: PointList::Serialize: a negative point count makes PointArraySetSize release Strings before the array (wild ~String)
bug_class: negative serialized count / signed size
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x180071730 (Pathfinding_PointList_PointArray_SetSize): `if (plVar2 == *param_1) { if (param_2 < iVar1) DestroyRange(plVar7, plVar2 + lVar9*3, iVar1 - param_2); }`. There is no negative check, matching the port's `ReleasePointsRange(oldData + newSize, oldSize - newSize)`.
reachability: A Pathfinding::PointList resource (mod package or damaged .rsc) whose point count field is negative.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (identical): 0x180071730 `*(int*)(param_1+1) = param_2; ... if (param_2 < iVar1) DestroyRange(..., plVar2 + (longlong)param_2*3, iVar1 - param_2)` versus port pointlist.cpp PointArraySetSize lines `a->_size = newSize; ... if (newSize < oldSize) ReleasePointsRange(oldData + newSize, oldSize - newSize);`. With a fresh PointList (data null, size 0) and a serialized n = -1, ~String runs on address null-0x18. The size also stays -1, and the destructor later calls ReleasePointsRange(data, -1), which is a no-op. This is a separate local copy of the grow routine, not array.cpp SetSizeCore (F-012), but it has the same shape.
root_cause: The serialized int count is passed to a signed SetSize that has no negative guard.
minimal_fix: fix.* row: in PointList::Serialize, reject n < 0 (return false), or clamp it to 0 before PointArraySetSize.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: String::FormatIndexed takes its vararg count from the format text: a string-table template with '@9' makes it va_arg and dereference up to 10 const char* the caller never passed
bug_class: vararg over-read (UB) / wild pointer deref
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800c8b40: 1800c8b96 CALL 0x1800c8d20 (FormatParamCount on the format) / 1800c8b9b MOVSXD R14,EAX / ... 1800c8bbd LEA RBX,[RBP+0x58] (the vararg home slots) / 1800c8bc9 MOV EDX,R14D / CALL 0x180029a80 (array SetSize(count)), then a loop of R14 iterations, each reading the next qword at RBX. No caller-supplied count exists. The port's FormatIndexedV (string.cpp:742-755) is the same.
reachability: Any string-table (.rsc) text a translation or mod package supplies for the event-log templates. Text-only mods are the most common Banished mod type.
proof: Repro formatindexed.cpp: FormatIndexed("@1 @2 @9", "Spring", "Year 3"), the eventlog.cpp case-0 shape with 2 args. ASan reports: SEGV on unknown address 0x7fffffffff01 (READ) in System::String::Set(char const*) string.cpp:317, called from FormatIndexedV string.cpp:753 and FormatIndexed string.cpp:770.
root_cause: FormatParamCount returns the highest '@n' digit + 1 found in the template, and FormatIndexedV reads that many varargs. The templates come from UI::StringTable text (eventlog.cpp:240 events->GetText(eventType), diseasecomponent.cpp:441 GetText(0xC)), i.e. game data, while the callers pass a fixed 2, 3 or 5 args.
minimal_fix: Add an explicit argument count: FormatIndexedN(fmt, argc, ...) that reads min(FormatParamCount(fmt), argc) varargs and fills the rest with empty Strings. Route the eventlog / disease callers through it. Alternatively, clamp '@n' with n >= argc to an empty substitution in FormatParamList.

title: System::Random::Serialize loads _index from the save with no bound; Rand() then reads _mt[_index] out of bounds (up to 16 GB past the object)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Rand 0x1800c7f90: CMP dword [RCX],0 / JNZ / CALL NextGroup / 1800c7fa3 MOV EDX,dword [RBX] / 1800c7fa5 MOV R8D,dword [RBX+RDX*4+0x4] ... LEA ECX,[RDX+1] / CMP ECX,0x270 / CMOVZ ECX,EAX / MOV [RBX],ECX. There is no range check, and Serialize 0x1800c7cf0 reads the uint straight from the stream. The port is the same.
reachability: Crafted or corrupt save file: the first Rand() after load (weather, AI, the seat shuffle) reads past the 2.5 KB object, then walks memory until it faults.
proof: Repro random_index.cpp: static System::Random g_r(1); g_r._index = 0x270 + 8 (any value >= 624 a save can carry); g_r.Rand(). ASan reports: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in (anonymous namespace)::RandImpl value_types.cpp:119:18, called from System::Random::Rand() value_types.cpp:184.
root_cause: GameUpdateLoop's world Random is deserialized by m_random->Serialize(ser) (gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:666): Serialize(_index) then 624 words. _index only wraps to 0 when it reaches exactly 0x270, so a loaded value > 0x270 indexes past _mt on every draw and keeps counting up to 2^32.
minimal_fix: In Random::Serialize, after the read: if (_index >= 0x270) _index = 0; (as a fix.* row, since retail has the same gap). Alternatively, use `_index % 0x270` in RandImpl.

title: AddController(description, name): a name that matches neither the root nor any subtree leaves `insertion` null, which is then called (IsDerivedFrom) and dereferenced (target->_children); a swallowed lookup miss becomes a crash and member-call-on-null UB
bug_class: swallowed lookup failure turned into a null dereference (member call on null this)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x180113470 does the same thing: on a miss it zeroes RDI and calls IsDerivedFrom with RCX=0, then forms `LEA RCX,[RBX+0xa0]` from the CMOV result, which is null for a null insertion, and reads [RCX+8]. The port is a faithful transcription; its comment says so. It is reported because the user ruled that all UB is a finding (here a C++ member call through a null pointer and a write through null->_children) and because the input that triggers it is user-installable data.
reachability: src/game/Dialog/toolui.cpp:160 (UIDescription::AddControllers) calls this overload for every UIDescription entry whose `entry.name` does not resolve to a TabElement, and moddialog.cpp:424 passes "groupBrowse". The names and the dialog layouts come from .rsc resources (entity UIDescriptions, StandardDialog.rsc, Mod.rsc) that mods override. A mod whose UIDescription names an insertion point its dialog layout lacks, or a layout that renames or drops the group, crashes opening the panel, in retail as well.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (retail matches the port; quoted to show the crash path) Runtime-x64.dll 0x180113470:
1801134f5: MOV R14D,dword ptr [RDI + 0xa8]   ; root->_children._size
1801134ff: JLE 0x180113538
180113518: CALL 0x180115650                 ; child->FindElement(name)
180113522: TEST RDI,RDI / JNZ found
180113538: XOR ESI,ESI
18011353a: MOV EDI,ESI                      ; miss: insertion = 0
180113542: MOV RCX,RDI
180113545: CALL 0x1800c0390                 ; IsDerivedFrom(this = null)
18011354f: CMOVNZ RBX,RDI                   ; target
180113603: LEA RCX,[RBX + 0xa0]
18011360a: MOV EDX,dword ptr [RCX + 0x8]   ; target->_children._size, null deref
Port dialog_create.cpp:497-525: `insertion = hit; /* a miss zeroes RDI */ ... Element* const target = insertion->IsDerivedFrom(UI::GroupElement::TypeId()) ? insertion : nullptr; ... ->SetSizeFill(target->_children._size + 1, &newEl); Element* walk = target; do { walk->_flags |= ...; } while (walk);`
root_cause: The miss result of the root-name test and the child FindElement scan is not checked before use. The code assumes the .rsc always contains the named GroupElement.
minimal_fix: Faithfully this stays a retail crash. Under the project's rules the fix is a fix.* row in src/ext with a hook that skips the insertion when `insertion` is null or not a GroupElement (destroy newEl, or keep it unparented) and still runs the phase-3 controller add. In the engine body, at minimum, do not call a member through the null `insertion`: test it before IsDerivedFrom so the remaining crash is the explicit target deref and not UB.

title: DocumentText ^i/^f/^c/^li slot digits index _sheets/_fonts/_colors/_frameTable with no bound; ModDetails puts raw mod names and package filenames into that markup

bug_class: null-this member call
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x180112180: the search loop falls through to `18011221e XOR EBX,EBX`, then `180112234 MOV EDX,[0x1801fa040] ; 18011223a MOV RCX,RBX ; 18011223d CALL 0x1800c0390 ; ... 18011224f TEST RBX,RBX`.
