title: Video::Device::ValidateConfiguration divides by the unvalidated settings value VideoRefreshD (division by zero / INT_MIN/-1)
bug_class: UB: integer division by zero on unvalidated persisted input
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800f8830 does the same IDIV on the config denominator. 0x1800f89a4: MOV R8D,R10D / TEST R9D,R9D / JLE 0x1800f89e1 / MOV EAX,ESI / CDQ / IDIV R12D (R12D = cfg->refreshDenominator) / ... 0x1800f89c0: MOV EAX,[RCX] / CDQ / IDIV dword ptr [RCX+0x4] (the per-mode denominator). The port transcribes this exactly.
reachability: Configuration::Startup (device.cpp:478) copies "VideoRefreshN" and "VideoRefreshD" from IO::Persistence, which reads the plain-text settings file in the user's documents folder (persistence_settings.cpp ReadSettings), with no range check. Any RefreshD=0 that is not an exact match for an enumerated rate (always the case for 0) reaches the fallback divide at boot (PlatformStartup -> ValidateConfiguration), so the game dies before the window comes up. RefreshN=INT_MIN with RefreshD=-1 also overflows. The second IDIV at device_startup.cpp:248 divides by each enumerated mode's denominator, and DXGI documents a 0/0 refresh rational as legal (devicedata.cpp:1716 copies it unchecked), so a driver that reports one crashes the same way. The same root cause is in the 8-argument Device::ValidateConfiguration (device.cpp:250-251, retail 0x1800f7370), reached from the options dialog.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_graphics_src_engine_video_errors/vcfg_refreshd0.cpp. It sets up one interface, one adapter and one 1920x1080 mode with refresh {60,1}, then sets Configuration{width=1920,height=1080,refreshNumerator=60,refreshDenominator=0} and calls Device::ValidateConfiguration(). It was built with `fz.sh build p8vid_refreshd0 src/engine/video/device_startup.cpp` and run with `-runs=1`. Result: `SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior src/engine/video/device_startup.cpp:246:47`, which is `const int32_t want = refreshN / refreshD;`, then a deadly signal.
root_cause: The refresh-rate fallback compares integer ratios num/den without checking the denominator. Both the persisted denominator and the adapter-reported ones go straight into IDIV.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening at the one site. In both ValidateConfiguration bodies, treat a refreshD <= 0 as "no match" (skip the ratio search and take entry 0), and skip any mode entry whose denominator is 0 inside the loop. A fix.* row is only needed if the maintainer wants the change switchable; the input is invalid either way.

title: Save-supplied negative bucket cursor indexes the bucket array out of bounds in Update; the port zero-extends it to +4G elements where retail MOVSXD reads before the array
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: port
label_evidence: Both builds are out of bounds. Retail sign-extends the cursor (0x1400c419b MOVSXD RSI,R14D, then MOV RCX,[RAX+RSI*8] at 0x1400c41bc). The port keeps it as a uint32_t idx and indexes arrBase[idx], so the address it reads differs from retail's.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400c4090:
1400c417c: MOV R14D,dword ptr [RCX]        ; cursor[bucket] (serialized)
1400c4185: CMP R14D,EAX                     ; signed: only cursor >= count is reset
1400c4190: CMOVGE R14D,R8D
1400c419b: MOVSXD RSI,R14D
1400c41b0: MOV RAX,qword ptr [R13]
1400c41bc: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + RSI*0x8]   ; arr[(int64)cursor]
Port lines 896-909:
  uint32_t cursorVal = cursor[bucket];
  if ((int32_t)cursorVal >= count) cursorVal = 0;   // negative passes
  uint32_t idx = startIdx;
  ComponentEntity* entIBP = arrBase[idx].Get();      // idx = 0xFFFFFFFB -> +32 GB
EntityList::Serialize loads cursor[5] straight from the save (line ~1601, `serializer.Serialize(5, cursor, nullptr)`) with no range check. A save with cursor[b] = -5 and a non-empty bucket b makes the first Update read arrBase[0xFFFFFFFB]. That is about 32 GB past the array: an access violation, then a wild entity pointer dereferenced (->_entityFlags, ->_lastUpdateTime write). Retail reads arr[-5] (heap header bytes) instead, so it is out of bounds as well.
root_cause: The cursor is persisted state, and the loop only resets it when it is >= count. A negative value is never rejected, in the port or in retail.
minimal_fix: Treat the cursor as a signed index and clamp it at load or before use. At line 897: `if ((int32_t)cursorVal < 0 || (int32_t)cursorVal >= count) cursorVal = 0;`. Or reject cursor[i] / processCount[i] outside 0..INT_MAX after Serializer::Serialize in EntityList::Serialize. This is a fix.* hardening, because retail lacks the test.

title: POSIX ThreadResume / ThreadJoin / ThreadClose dereference the null handle a failed pthread_create returns; System::Thread passes it unchecked, as retail does with _beginthreadex
bug_class: error handling of platform calls (null handle after failed thread creation)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail System::Thread ctor 0x1800ca4e0 (Runtime-x64.dll) stores _beginthreadex's result and calls SetThreadPriority and ResumeThread on it with no check: `CALL 0x18007fbfc ; MOV [RBX+0x10],RAX ; MOV RCX,[RBX+0x10] ; CALL [0x18014b188] (SetThreadPriority) ... MOV RCX,[RBX+0x10] ; CALL [0x18014b190] (ResumeThread)`. On Win32 a 0 handle makes both calls fail with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE, and the dtor's WaitForSingleObject(0) and CloseHandle(0) also just fail, so retail does not crash. The POSIX twin returns nullptr on failure (thread_posix.cpp:96) and then dereferences it at :110 (ThreadResume), :119 (ThreadJoin) and :127 (ThreadClose). thread.cpp:146-155 keeps retail's unchecked sequence. parallel_for.cpp:159 and gather_threads.cpp:32 check for null; System::Thread does not.
reachability: Any pthread_create failure (EAGAIN from RLIMIT_NPROC or the kernel thread limit, or ENOMEM) while constructing an engine System::Thread (Engine::Loader, the update and path threads) on Linux, macOS (same thread_posix.cpp; no darwin twin) or Android. Retail and the Windows build survive the same failure.
proof:
Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_platform_posix_src_platform_darwin_s_sdl/thread_create_fail.cpp sets RLIMIT_NPROC=1 and then runs InitFields' Platform call sequence call for call. Output (ASan+UBSan, WSL):
[Platform] pthread_create failed (11)
ThreadCreateSuspended -> (nil)
/home/uspc/openba-review/src/platform/posix/thread_posix.cpp:110:28: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'ThreadObject'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior .../thread_posix.cpp:110:28
Retail sequence, 0x1800ca4e0: 1800ca518 CALL 0x18007fbfc (_beginthreadex) / 1800ca51f MOV [RBX+0x10],RAX / 1800ca523 MOV RCX,[RBX+0x10] / 1800ca527 CALL [0x18014b188] / ... / 1800ca568 MOV RCX,[RBX+0x10] / 1800ca570 CALL [0x18014b190]. These are kernel calls that tolerate a null handle.
root_cause: The POSIX twin copies _beginthreadex's failure value (null) but not the Win32 property that every later call on that handle fails harmlessly. ThreadSetNormalPriority tolerates null; ThreadResume, ThreadJoin and ThreadClose do not.
minimal_fix: Make the twin keep Win32 semantics for a null handle: at the top of ThreadResume return 0xFFFFFFFFu (ResumeThread's failure value) when t == nullptr; ThreadJoin returns 0xFFFFFFFFu (WAIT_FAILED) and ThreadClose returns false for null. This leaves retail's unchecked caller in thread.cpp byte-faithful.
also: POSIX ThreadResume / ThreadJoin / ThreadClose dereference the null handle a failed ThreadCreateSuspended returns; System::Thread passes it unchecked (Win32 fails the call with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE instead)

title: ext.create_on_demand idle sweep can deadlock: UseGate is held across Device::Lock while the frame thread, holding Device::Lock, spins in UseGate::Enter
bug_class: lock-order deadlock (gate vs device lock), hang
label: ext
reachability: ext.create_on_demand on with ext.create_on_demand_idle_min > 0 (a settings key, 0..120, default 0). A SetData or buffer save on a thread other than the frame thread, such as the loader during a load while the loading screen renders, has to collide with the once-per-minute sweep. The result is a permanent hang (watchdog exit 4).
proof: Standalone repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_common_swapchain/gate_deadlock.cpp. It includes the real use_tracker.h and uses a std::recursive_mutex for Video::Device::Lock. Built with clang++-19 -fsanitize=address,undefined on WSL; the watchdog fires after 3 s: "DEADLOCK: frame spins in UseGate::Enter holding the device lock, loader waits for the device lock inside the gate, sweep waits in UseGate::Close for the loader" (exit=1). The interleaving matches the port's call order: (1) ContextData::BeginCommands takes device->Lock() (contextdata.cpp:471) and holds it until Finish; draws call VertexBufferData/IndexBufferData/ImageBufferData::Bind, which open CreateOnDemand::UseScope -> UseGate::Enter (buffers.cpp:620, 715; imagebufferdata.cpp:854). (2) On another thread (buffers.cpp:552 says 'The caller may be the loader thread while the main thread presents'), VertexBufferData::SetData opens UseScope (buffers.cpp:596) and then GpuBuffer_SetData calls VideoDeviceObject()->Lock() (buffers.cpp:537). The GpuBuffer_Serialize save arm does the same: UseScope at :440, Lock at :488. (3) Worker 0's LazyTable::Sweep calls _gate.Close() (lazy_table.cpp Sweep), which sets _closed and spins until _users==0. The loader is inside the gate waiting for the device lock. The frame thread holds the device lock and spins in Enter while _closed is set. The sweep waits for the loader, so all three wait on each other forever.
root_cause: UseGate::Close blocks new users until every current user leaves, but a current user can block on Video::Device::Lock inside its UseScope, and the device-lock holder (the frame thread) needs to Enter the gate before it releases the lock. The gate is effectively a lock taken in both orders relative to the device lock.
minimal_fix: In GpuBuffer_SetData and the GpuBuffer_Serialize save arm, take the UseScope after VideoDeviceObject()->Lock(), so the gate is always taken inside the device lock. Alternatively, make Sweep evict only from the frame thread at a point where it holds the device lock, or make UseGate::Close give up (re-open and retry the next epoch) when users do not drain within a bound.

title: BANISHED_FPS_CAP accepts any positive value (or NaN): out-of-range double->int64 casts and a signed overflow in the frame limiter
bug_class: UB: float-cast-overflow and signed-integer-overflow from unbounded input
label: ext
label_evidence: frame_limiter.cpp is the NOT RETAIL frame cap (frame_limiter.h); the value comes from Opt().fpsCap (options.cpp:209, a harness flag).
reachability: Harness or user environment: BANISHED_FPS_CAP=1e-300, =nan or =0.001 (Linux/macOS/Android), from the first menu frame. ext.fps_cap's integer rate cannot reach it.
proof: Repro scratchpad/p8/src_app_sdl/fpscap_cast.cpp includes the real frame_limiter.cpp with platform stubs and calls FrameLimiter::Tick() once with fpsCap="1e-300". Under UBSan: frame_limiter.cpp:121:68: runtime error: inf is outside the range of representable values of type 'long' (SetCeiling -> Pace -> Tick). Line 133, g_intervalTicks = (int64_t)((double)g_qpcFreq / fps), has the same defect for the same input and for "nan" (v <= 0.0 is false for NaN, so g_harness becomes Fixed with g_harnessFps = NaN). Repro scratchpad/p8/src_app_sdl/fpscap_wait_overflow.cpp uses fpsCap="0.001" with a 1 GHz counter (the POSIX ns clock) and two Ticks. Under UBSan: frame_limiter.cpp:167:50: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 999999748000 * 10000000 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t' (WaitUntil -> Pace -> Tick).
root_cause: Init() accepts any atof result > 0 (and NaN) as the harness ceiling. SetCeiling converts freq/fps and 1e9/fps to int64_t without a range check, and WaitUntil computes sleepTicks * 10000000 in int64. A tiny cap (below about 1e-3 fps on a ns counter, or 1e-5 on a 10 MHz QPC) or NaN makes those expressions undefined.
minimal_fix: In Init, accept the flag only if std::isfinite(v) && v >= some floor (for example 0.01 fps); otherwise treat it as Off. In WaitUntil, compute due100ns without overflow, for example as (double)sleepTicks * 1e7 / g_qpcFreq clamped to INT64_MAX, or with a 128-bit multiply.

title: freopen of the two log files is unchecked: on an unwritable run directory stdout/stderr are left closed and every later printf/fprintf/setvbuf uses a closed FILE (UB, logs silently lost, printf reports success)
bug_class: unchecked return value (file IO) / swallowed failure
label: ext
label_evidence: WinMain's log redirect is OpenBA-only: retail Application-x64.exe opens no standalone_*.log. The same unchecked pattern is at the POSIX entry src/app/main.cpp:1157-1158 and at the post-Startup re-open src/game/Game/game_main.cpp:342-343.
reachability: Any launch whose working directory is not writable: GOG Galaxy's default Program Files install, a shortcut whose 'Start in' points elsewhere, or a read-only network share.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_app_errors/freopen_fail.cpp, built with the pinned toolchain (C:/winlibs-gcc16 g++ -mwindows, UCRT, as OpenBA.exe). It runs WinMain's lines 981-984 against a path that cannot be created, then the crash handler's _get_osfhandle(_fileno(stderr)). Output: 'freopen stdout=0000000000000000 stderr=0000000000000000 fileno(stdout)=-1' / 'printf on closed stdout returned 10' / '_get_osfhandle(_fileno(stderr)) = -1 (survived)'. Both streams are closed (C11 7.21.5.4: freopen closes the old file first), so every later use of stdout/stderr is use of a closed stream (C11 7.21.3p4: indeterminate FILE). The CRT reports success and writes nothing. Reachable: Windows EnterRunDirectory is empty (src/platform/win/app_win.cpp:30), so the logs open in the launch cwd. That cwd is not writable when the game is installed under GOG Galaxy's default C:/Program Files (x86)/GOG Galaxy/Games, because the manifested exe gets no UAC virtualisation, or when the exe is launched with a system-folder cwd. src/app/frame_limiter.cpp:102 already notes 'redirect silently fails, output lost'.
root_cause: The return value of freopen is discarded, and nothing records that stdout/stderr are now closed. The boot goes on writing through them, and the crash handler, boot-state and [AutoStart] diagnostics that the harness and triage rely on (CLAUDE.md: 'read standalone_crash.log first') vanish with no signal.
minimal_fix: Check each freopen. On failure, reopen the stream on a fallback that always works: freopen to the user dir (Platform user folder / BANISHED_USER_DIR) and, failing that, to the null device ("NUL" / "/dev/null"). Emit one line to the fallback naming the failed path. Apply the same change at main.cpp:1157-1158 and game_main.cpp:342-343.

title: Scene::FindFree3DEffect: (int64_t)((_maxLength / 20.0f) / secondsPerTick) overflows for a large serialized _maxLength (float-cast-overflow UB)
bug_class: out-of-range float->int conversion
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800deae5 'MOV RAX,[RDX+0x28]' ; 0x1800deafd 'CVTSI2SS XMM1,RAX' ; 0x1800deb07 'DIVSS XMM1,[0x180161700]' ; 0x1800deb0f 'COMISS XMM1,XMM0' ; 0x1800deb14 'CVTPS2PD XMM0,XMM1' ; 0x1800deb17 'DIVSD XMM0,[0x1801fe728]' ; 0x1800deb1f 'CVTTSD2SI R10,XMM0'. On overflow retail gets 0x8000000000000000 (window negative, harmless); in C++ it is UB. _maxLength is read from the resource by SoundEffect::Serialize (SerializeInt64 for version >= 1).
reachability: Any PlayEffect3D (animation sounds, building sounds) of a SoundEffect whose serialized _maxLength exceeds about 1.8e14 ticks; any 2D or 3D sample whose startSeconds exceeds about 9.2e12 s or is inf. Both come from mod or package data.
proof: Repro findfree3d_maxlength.cpp: _secondsPerTick = 1e-6, SoundEffect _maxLength = INT64_MAX, then Scene::FindFree3DEffect via a real Scene (RtAudio_Scene_Ctor). UBSan: 'audio.cpp:464:43: runtime error: 4.61169e+23 is outside the range of representable values of type long'. The same pattern sits in SoundEffect::Compile (vtbatch7_soundbuffer_soundeffect.cpp:606: `static_cast<int64_t>(static_cast<double>(end) / secondsPerTick)` with end = buffer _durationSeconds + sample startSeconds, both from data, inf included) and in Scene::Update (audio_scene_update.cpp:463: `static_cast<int64_t>(sec / spt)` with the sample's startSeconds).
root_cause: A seconds-to-ticks conversion of data-derived floats with no range clamp (retail's inlined SecondsToTicks).
minimal_fix: Route these through one saturating SecondsToTicks helper (NaN -> 0, clamp to [INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX] before the cast) that returns retail's CVTTSD2SI result (INT64_MIN) on overflow, so behaviour stays byte-identical while the UB goes.

title: Audio::Stream::_stopping (plain uint8_t) and the inherited _runFlags are shared between the main thread (Play / StopPlatform) and the stream worker (Run / ThreadFunc) with no synchronisation: a data race (UB)
bug_class: data-race / plain field as cross-thread flag (C12)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Stream::Play 0x1800a0d10: `TEST byte ptr [RCX+0x8],0x1 ; JZ ; MOV byte ptr [RCX+0x80],0x1 ; MOV RCX,[RCX+0x40] ; CALL [SetEvent] ; ... MOV byte ptr [RBX+0x80],0x0`. Retail StopPlatform 0x1800dea20: `TEST byte ptr [RCX+0xa08],0x1 ; JZ ; MOV byte ptr [RCX+0xa80],0x1 ; CALL [SetEvent]`. Plain loads and stores with no lock, the same as the port's lines.
proof:
Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_engine_src_engine_audio_concurrency/stream_play_race.cpp. It links the real audio_stream.cpp, audio_stream_play.cpp, system/thread.cpp, platform/posix/thread_posix.cpp, sync_posix.cpp and event_std.cpp. Its Run stand-in reads _stopping the way the real Run's loop tail does at audio_stream_run.cpp, `if (_stopping != 0)`, retail 0x1800a13af. TSan report:
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
  Read of size 4 by main thread: #0 Audio::Stream::Play audio_stream_play.cpp:136:27 (`_runFlags & 1u`)
  Previous write of size 4 by thread T1: #0 System::Thread::ThreadFunc thread.cpp:205:25 (`_runFlags |= 1u`)
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
  Write of size 1 by main thread: #0 Audio::Stream::Play audio_stream_play.cpp:139:19 (`_stopping = 1`)
  Previous read of size 1 by thread T1: #0 Audio::Stream::Run (the loop-tail _stopping read)
The same two accesses are made by Device::StopPlatform at audio_device.cpp:277-279.
root_cause: Stream::_stopping is a plain uint8_t written by the main thread (Play :139, StopPlatform :278) and polled by the worker in Run's loop tail, outside the Stream lock. Thread::_runFlags is a plain uint32_t that the worker read-modify-writes in ThreadFunc while Play and StopPlatform read it to decide whether to stop the pass. Neither has atomic or acquire/release semantics. Calls to opaque functions keep GCC from hoisting the loads today, but under the C++ memory model the program has undefined behaviour.
minimal_fix: Make the accesses atomic without changing the layout: use __atomic_store_n / __atomic_load_n (relaxed is enough, because the events order everything else) on _stopping in Play, StopPlatform and Run. Read _runFlags in Play and StopPlatform with __atomic_load_n(&_runFlags, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE). Or wrap both in one small std::atomic_ref helper so the retail byte layout is kept.

title: The Device channel flag word is written by the backend audio thread (OnStreamEnd `flags |= 2`) and read and cleared by the main thread's Device::Update without a lock: a data race (UB)
bug_class: data-race / lock-free cross-thread flag (C12)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Device::Update 0x1800de520: `1800de550 TEST byte ptr [RBX-0x20],0x2 ; JZ ; CALL 0x1800de6f0 (FreeChannelPlatform) ; MOV RAX,[RBX] ; AND dword ptr [RBX-0x20],0xfffffffc`, with no lock. Retail StopPlatform 0x1800dea20 ends `1800dea97 OR dword ptr [RAX],0x2`, also unlocked. Stream.h and platform_audio.h both note that the callback writes the flags 'WITHOUT a lock (retail's design)'. Not listed in known_port_issues.md or retail_bugs.md.
proof:
Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_engine_src_engine_audio_concurrency/channel_flags_race.cpp. It links the real audio_device.cpp and audio_voice_callback.cpp. One thread calls PlatformChannel::OnStreamEnd, as SDL's get callback does in audio_sdl.cpp GetCallback; the main thread runs Device::Update with _xaudio2 null, so FreeChannelPlatform returns at its first test. TSan report:
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
  Read of size 4 by main thread: #0 Audio::Device::Update audio_device.cpp:203:18 (`(ch->flags & 2u) == 0`)
  Previous write of size 4 by thread T1: #0 Audio::Device::PlatformChannel::OnStreamEnd audio_voice_callback.cpp:212:20 (`channel->flags |= kChannelFinished`)
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
  Write of size 4 by main thread: #0 Audio::Device::Update audio_device.cpp:208:19 (`ch->flags &= 0xFFFFFFFCu`)
  Previous write: OnStreamEnd audio_voice_callback.cpp:212:20
In the real program, Update clears the flags only after FreeChannelPlatform has destroyed the voice, and AudioVoiceDestroy waits out any running callback. So the reachable race is the per-frame read at :203 against the callback's read-modify-write. The write-write pair in the repro is an artefact of the test.
root_cause: AudioChannel::flags is a plain uint32_t. The backend's audio thread read-modify-writes it in OnStreamEnd, while the main thread polls it every frame in Device::Update (and Scene code reads bit 0). There is no lock or atomic between the two threads.
minimal_fix: Make the accesses atomic and keep the layout. Use __atomic_fetch_or(&channel->flags, 2u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE) in OnStreamEnd. Use an __atomic_load_n(&ch->flags, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) for the bit test in Device::Update (and Scene's bit-0 scan). Also use atomic and/or for the `&= ~3` / `|= 2` writes in Update, Stop and StopPlatform so the word has a single access discipline.

title: CompressedStream::GetSize: (nHdr << 15) - 0x8000 + last overflows int32 for a 65536-block directory
bug_class: signed-overflow / shift
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800aa860: `MOVSXD R10,[R9+0x48]; ... MOVZX R8D,word [RCX+R10*8-2]; SHL R10D,0xf; LEA ECX,[R10-0x8000]; ADD ECX,R8D; CMP EAX,ECX; CMOVG ECX,EAX`. These are 32-bit SHL/LEA/ADD that wrap; the port line `int32_t total = (nHdr << 15) - RtIo::kCompressedStreamWindowSize + last;` is the same arithmetic in signed int. Faithful behaviour, UB in C++17.
reachability: GetSize on any opened CompressedMemoryStream / CompressedFileStream with a crafted or >2 GiB-uncompressed directory. Live callers on a loaded save: ExtSave_ReadTail (src/game/Game/gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:807) runs on save load, and RoundtripDecompress (:974); also ext/background_save and the stream slot 6 used by the package readers.
proof: Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_io_src_engine_save_ub/getsize_shift.cpp, linked by link_getsize.sh in the same folder with the real compressed_stream_open/write, memory_stream and encoding objects. The blob is {count=65536} followed by 65536 all-zero 8-byte headers (len = 524292). The real CompressedStream::Open accepts it: blockCount*8 <= len, and total == len because every StoredLength is 0. GetSize() then trips UBSan: `__ubsan_handle_sub_overflow_abort` in `IO::CompressedStream::GetSize() const src/engine/io/compressed_stream_write.cpp:678:38`. (65536<<15 is also a C++17 shift into the sign bit, UB before the subtraction.)
root_cause: _headerSize is the block count read from the stream by Open, which only bounds it by blockCount*8 <= len. 65536 or more blocks make nHdr<<15 reach 2^31, and the signed shift and subtract overflow. This is GetSize, a separate function from the DecompressFromSource / SetWindow overflow already known as F-052, but the input (a large directory) is the same.
minimal_fix: Compute in uint32 and convert back to keep retail's wrapped result: `int32_t total = static_cast<int32_t>((static_cast<uint32_t>(nHdr) << 15) - 0x8000u + static_cast<uint32_t>(last));`

title: Port-only counter `++g_fsc.fsDtor` in FileStream::~FileStream is a data race between the Persistence, Audio::Stream and Loader threads
bug_class: data race on shared global (port instrumentation)
label: port
label_evidence: RtIO::g_fsc (file_stream.cpp:202-205) is port-only instrumentation, a counter added during porting. Retail ~FileStream (0x1800aaad0) begins with `if (file.handle != -1) FileSystem::CloseFile(...)` and has no global increment, as the banner above the body lists ('Retail's six steps').
proof:
TSan. fsdtor_counter_tsan.cpp plus abort stubs (fsdtor_stubs.cpp), linked with the REAL file_stream.cpp and file_stream_write.cpp. Two threads each construct and destroy unopened IO::FileStream stack objects, as the Audio::Stream worker (`IO::FileStream st;` in audio_stream_run.cpp) and the Persistence jobs (LoadJob, GetSaveInfoJob, SaveJob) do. TSan output:
`WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 8 at ... by thread T2: #0 IO::FileStream::~FileStream() file_stream.cpp:729:5 ... Previous write of size 8 ... by thread T1: #0 IO::FileStream::~FileStream() file_stream.cpp:729:5 ... Location is global 'RtIO::g_fsc'`.
In the game the overlap is reachable: music streaming runs while a save, load or save-list job runs, and while the Loader thread closes resource streams during world load.
root_cause: A plain uint64_t global is incremented, a non-atomic read-modify-write, on a path that every IO thread executes. g_fsc.create and g_fsc.createTrue (file_stream.cpp:422/446) are hit by the worker's SaveJob as well.
minimal_fix: Delete the investigation counters: AGENTS.md section 3 says investigation lines are deleted when the investigation closes. If they must stay, make the struct fields std::atomic<uint64_t> and use relaxed fetch_add.

title: FileSystem::ReadFile computes the packed read offset as a signed int32 sum, which overflows (UB) for an entry that crosses the 2 GiB mark; this is the seam of fix.large_packages
bug_class: signed integer overflow (UB) on the fix.large_packages seam; inconsistent with its sibling helpers (C7/C8 width)
label: port
label_evidence: The comment cites retail 0x1800ace43/46, a 32-bit ADD that wraps (defined on x86). The port spells it as C++ int32 + int32, which is UB on overflow. Its two siblings written for the same fix (PackedReadOffset line 320, PackedMapOfEntry line 410) already add through uint32 and say 'Retail's int32 sum, wrapping as the 32-bit ADD does'. Only this line kept the signed form.
reachability: Any mod package larger than 2 GiB (docs/retail_bugs.md section 9, fix.large_packages). Every packed read of the entry that straddles offset 0x80000000 reaches it, with the row on or off.
proof: The repro readfile_abs_overflow.cpp (scratchpad/p8/src_ext_fix_rows_default_ON_and_their_se_drift/) links the real src/engine/io/filesystem_openfile.cpp. It calls IO::FileSystem::ReadFile on a packed FileInfo {handle=0x00000001, baseOffset=0x7FFFF000, cursor=0x2000}: an entry 4 KB below 2 GiB, read 8 KB in. fz.sh build fixdrift_readfile + run -runs=1 gives: '#13 __ubsan_handle_add_overflow_abort ... #14 IO::FileSystem::ReadFile(RtIO::FileInfo&, int, void*) src/engine/io/filesystem_openfile.cpp:509:40' and 'SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior .../filesystem_openfile.cpp:509:40'.
root_cause: `const int32_t abs = fi->baseOffset + fi->cursor;`, where both FileInfo fields are int32_t (FileSystem.h:198-199). Any package entry that starts below 2 GiB and runs past it gives a sum above INT32_MAX once the cursor crosses the mark. That happens in every package over 2 GiB, the very input fix.large_packages exists for, and also under the faithful profile. The sum is computed before the `wide` branch, so the UB happens even when the fix's 64-bit offset is the one used.
minimal_fix: Wrap the same way as the siblings: `const int32_t abs = static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<uint32_t>(fi->baseOffset) + static_cast<uint32_t>(fi->cursor));`. Lines 522 and 534 have the same latent issue in `fi->cursor += n` (an entry larger than 2 GiB); they can use the same unsigned add.
module: src/ext fix.* rows (default ON) and their seams into src/engine + src/game

title: BinaryReader::Skip: word24 + word20 is a signed int32 overflow when the record length word comes from the stream
bug_class: signed-overflow
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800a83f0 (Runtime-x64.dll): `MOV RAX,[RCX+0x18]; MOV EDX,[RCX+0x24]; ADD EDX,[RCX+0x20]; MOV R8,[RAX]; MOV RCX,RAX; JMP [R8+0x20]`. That is a 32-bit ADD that wraps, and the port's `const int32_t end = word24 + word20;` transcribes it. The behaviour is faithful; only the C++ spelling is UB.
reachability: Any BinaryReader record with version 0 that a consumer skips, using a length word from the file. Examples: AchievementInstance::Persist (the achievements file in the user's documents), Dialog settings controller records with an unknown id (dialog_settings.cpp:401), GraphicsMesh::Serialize (graphicsmesh_vtable.cpp:403/413, package data), ShaderProgram (shaderprogram.cpp:197), leaves (batchc_gfx_leaves.cpp:566).
proof: Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_io_src_engine_save_ub/skip_overflow.cpp. It builds a BinaryReader over a stream holding the record header {0xaaaaaaaa, 0x7fffffff, version 0}, then calls Skip() when GetVersion()==0, the same path AchievementInstance::Persist and the dialog_settings controller loop take. Built with `wsl -e bash -c "FZ_SRC=... ~/fz.sh build ioub_skip && ~/fz.sh run ioub_skip 30 -runs=1"`. UBSan reports `__ubsan_handle_add_overflow_abort` in `IO::BinaryReader::Skip() src/engine/io/serialize_family.cpp:349:32`, with SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior serialize_family.cpp:349:32.
root_cause: word20 is the record's length word, read raw from the stream by the BinaryReader constructor (Serializer.h:1004, `rw_stream::Read(s, 4, &word20)`). Skip adds it to word24 (the stream position after the length word) in signed int32 with no bound. A length word near INT_MAX overflows.
minimal_fix: Do the add in unsigned and convert back, which keeps retail's wrapped value: `const int32_t end = static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<uint32_t>(word24) + static_cast<uint32_t>(word20));`

title: InternalPtr<T>::Serialize (and ~48 game call sites) static_casts the loaded Internal* to T* BEFORE the IsDerivedFrom check: invalid downcast UB on a mismatched save type
bug_class: invalid downcast (static_cast to wrong dynamic type)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail has no C++ cast: it tests the Internal* with IsDerivedFrom (0x1800c0390) and nulls the slot. The port spells the check as `T* obj = Get(); if (obj && !obj->IsDerivedFrom(T::TypeId()))`, where Get() is `static_cast<T*>(Internal*)` (Internal.h:356). That cast is UB whenever the check is about to fail. The behaviour matches retail; the UB exists only in the port.
reachability: Every save load. InternalBasePtr::Serialize stores whatever PersistObject built from the save's type id. InternalPtr<T>::Serialize(ser) then downcasts before validating. The same shape appears at 48 game sites (`IsDerivedFromNullSafe(field.Get(), ...)`, e.g. completetask.cpp:51/59, charactercomponent_serialize.cpp:80). A save whose persisted object type is a different Internal subclass triggers it.
proof:
Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_object_ub/internalptr_downcast.cpp. Built against libfuzz_tree.a with -fsanitize=vptr (build_vptr.sh in the same folder). It puts a live TypeB (an Internal) into an InternalPtr<TypeA>, which is what InternalBasePtr::Serialize leaves when the save's type id names another Internal type, then runs Serialize's `Get()`:
 Internal.h:356:36: runtime error: downcast of address 0x5030000000d0 which does not point to an object of type '(anonymous namespace)::TypeA'
 note: object is of type '(anonymous namespace)::TypeB'
 #0 Object::InternalPtr<TypeA>::Get() const Internal.h:356:36
 SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior Internal.h:356:36
root_cause: The type test is applied to the already-downcast T* instead of to the Internal* the base class holds.
minimal_fix: Test before the cast: `Internal* raw = InternalBasePtr::Get(); if (raw && !raw->IsDerivedFrom(T::TypeId())) _ptr = nullptr;`. For the game sites, pass `field.InternalBasePtr::Get()` (or add an `InternalPtr::GetRaw()`) to IsDerivedFromNullSafe instead of `field.Get()`.

title: External::Load dereferences a null type node when a .crs header names a typeId the Factory does not hold
bug_class: unchecked lookup result -> null member access (UB) on input
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800bc71d..0x1800bc742: on a miss the descent falls to `1800bc73b MOV RCX,RBX` (RBX=0 since 0x1800bc6a5), then `1800bc73e MOV RAX,[RCX+0x10]` and `1800bc742 CALL [RAX+0x20]`. The port transcribes this on purpose (the volatile read of &n->element.record.info, 'FAITHFUL FAULT ON A MISS'). Not in docs/retail_bugs.md.
reachability: Any compiled resource read through FindOrLoad -> External::Load: a third-party .pkm mod or a loose .crs whose second dword is not a registered type CRC.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_object_errors/create_object_miss.cpp. It drives the identical miss arm in Object::Factory::CreateObject (an empty Factory, CreateObject(0x1234)). Built and run with `fz.sh build objerr_createmiss` and `fz.sh run objerr_createmiss 30 -runs=1`. Result: `SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior src/engine/object/type_reflection.cpp:552:33` (`&n->element.record` with n == nullptr; frame #14 Object::Factory::CreateObject(unsigned int) const). External::Load open-codes the same descent and does `const BaseTypeInfo* const volatile* infoSlot = &n->element.record.info; info = *infoSlot; info->factoryFn();` with n null on a miss. Retail: `1800bc739 JNZ 1800bc722 / 1800bc73b MOV RCX,RBX / 1800bc73e MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX+0x10] / 1800bc742 CALL qword ptr [RAX+0x20]`.
root_cause: The Factory type-tree lookup result is never checked. The typeId comes straight from the resource file (SerUInt after the magic), so any .crs in a mod package with an unregistered typeId is a null member access, then a read at 0x10 and a crash. Factory::CreateObject (type_reflection.cpp:550-558) has the same unchecked Find and is used by goal_list, componententity and toolbardialog with ids from data.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening at the lookup site (a fix.* row if faithfulness is required): when n == nullptr, set bad = true (count it as notAnExternal) so Load takes retail's 0x1800bc845 bad-file exit and returns null. Give Factory::CreateObject the same `if (!n) return nullptr;`.

title: External::Load calls IsDerivedFrom on a null object when the typeId names an abstract type (factoryFn returns null)
bug_class: unchecked Create* return value used before its null test
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800bc742 `CALL [RAX+0x20]` (factoryFn) / 0x1800bc74e `MOV RCX,RAX` / 0x1800bc751 `CALL 0x1800c0390`. The callee's first access is 0x1800c039a `MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]` and then 0x1800c03a6 `CALL [RAX+0x10]`. The `TEST RDI,RDI` at 0x1800bc75e comes too late, so the port's `|| obj == nullptr` is equally dead.
reachability: A mod .crs whose type dword is the CRC of a registered abstract type, or an out-of-memory during factoryFn.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: Runtime-x64.dll
1800bc742: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x20]   ; info->factoryFn()
1800bc745: MOV RDI,RAX
1800bc74e: MOV RCX,RAX
1800bc751: CALL 0x1800c0390             ; Base::IsDerivedFrom(created,...)
  1800c039a: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]     ; vptr of null
  1800c03a6: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x10] ; Type()
1800bc75e: TEST RDI,RDI                  ; null test only afterwards
Port: `::Object::Base* const created = info->factoryFn(); ... const bool isExternal = created->IsDerivedFrom(::Object::External::TypeId()); if (!isExternal || obj == nullptr)`. External::CreateNewObject, CompiledExternal::CreateNewObject, Internal::CreateNewObject, ExternalCompiler/ExtensionCompiler::CreateNewObject all `return nullptr;` (external_class.cpp:99,141; internal_class.cpp:298; external_compilers.cpp:20-23), and ExternalList::CreateNewObject returns null when MemAlloc fails. Under C++ the virtual call on null is UB, so the compiler may also delete the later `obj == nullptr` test.
root_cause: The result of the type's factory function is used, through a virtual call, before it is null-tested. The typeId is file-controlled, so a .crs naming a registered abstract type (the CRC of "External", "CompiledExternal", ...) or an allocation failure leads to a null vptr load.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening: test `created == nullptr` before IsDerivedFrom and treat it as the bad-type exit (bad = true). The same reorder applies at internal_class.cpp:706-713 (PersistObject) and Internal::Clone (internal_class.cpp:425-431).

title: GridFreeEntry copies an uninitialised int (_userValue2) of its stack temporary into the live Entry (indeterminate-value read, UB)
bug_class: uninitialised read (indeterminate value copied by EntryAssign)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x18007b390 builds the temporary at RSP+0x28 and never stores to +0x3c (RSP+0x64); the port's banner documents reproducing this on purpose.
reachability: Every Picking::Scene::RemoveMesh: entity removal through PickingComponent::OnRemove, Map::RemoveFloor, and the edit tools.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (no diff: faithful). Retail RemoveMesh's entry release 0x18007b390, temporary Entry at R11-0x50 == RSP+0x28:
  18007b3af: MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x28],ECX        ; +0x00 _queryStamp
  18007b3b3: MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x2c],0xffffffff ; +0x04 _nextFree
  18007b3bb: MOV qword ptr [R11 + -0x48],RCX       ; +0x08 cellX/Y
  18007b3bf: MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x38],ECX        ; +0x10 cellW/H
  18007b3cb..3d7: MOV qword ptr [R11-0x38..-0x20],RCX ; +0x18 mesh, +0x20/+0x28 transforms, +0x30 userData
  18007b3db: MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x60],ECX        ; +0x38 _userValue
  18007b3df: MOV qword ptr [R11 + -0x10],RCX       ; +0x40 _callback   (no store to RSP+0x64 = +0x3c)
  18007b3fa: CALL 0x18007b590                       ; Entry::operator= copies +0x3c
Port: scene_grid.cpp:983-999 builds `Entry tmp;` without writing tmp._userValue2, then `EntryAssign(&scene->_entries._data[id], &tmp)`, and EntryAssign does `d->_userValue2 = s->_userValue2;` (an lvalue-to-rvalue conversion of an indeterminate int32_t, which is UB under [basic.indet]).
root_cause: The byte-faithful reproduction of retail's partially initialised stack temporary. In C++ the copy of an indeterminate non-char value is undefined, so the optimiser may treat it as poison.
minimal_fix: Initialise `tmp._userValue2 = 0;` (or value-initialise the temporary with `Entry tmp{};`). The value is never read back after RemoveMesh, so nothing observable changes, but the oracle exclusion for +0x3c stays.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: Persistence worker hand-off is an unsynchronised data race: SaveLoad::Update polls _runFlags/_status with plain loads, then reads the job's results with no acquire
bug_class: C11 data race / volatile-as-sync
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail SaveLoad::Update 0x1800c2e40 does the same plain poll: `1800c2e4a MOV RAX,[0x1801fc6b8]; 1800c2e51 TEST byte ptr [RAX+0x18],0x1; 1800c2e55 JNZ 0x1800c2e9b; 1800c2e57 CMP dword ptr [RAX+0x48],0x0; 1800c2e5b JZ 0x1800c2e9b; ... JMP 0x1800c2a80 (UpdateSave)`. On x86 TSO with MSVC this works in practice. The port is shaped like retail but also ships on aarch64 (Android, macOS), where it is not ordered.
proof:
TSan (clang++-19 -fsanitize=thread). The repro persist_handoff_tsan.cpp links the REAL src/engine/system/thread.cpp with the posix thread/sync/event_std layer. It runs a worker whose Run() mirrors GetSaveListJob's tail (fill _saves, then `_status = 1`) against the main-side sequence of UpdateList state 0, then the SaveLoad::Update gate, then GetSaveCount/GetSaveInfo. TSan reports three races:
(1) `Read of size 4 ... by main thread` (the `_runFlags & 1` poll) vs `Previous write ... by thread T1: System::Thread::ThreadFunc thread.cpp:205:25` (`_runFlags &= ~1u`).
(2) The main thread's read of `_status` vs the worker's `_status = 1` store in Run (ThreadFunc thread.cpp:206).
(3) The main thread's read of the result payload (the _saves size and elements) vs the worker's writes in Run.
The worker stores in program order: payload, then `_status = 1`, then `_runFlags &= ~1`, then EventSet. The main thread reads `_runFlags`, then `_status`, then the payload, and never takes the event's mutex in between. So there is no happens-before edge from the job's results to the reads.
root_cause: The cross-thread completion protocol is two plain int fields: `_runFlags`, written by ThreadFunc, and `_status`, written by the jobs. The main thread polls them every frame without atomics or barriers (saveload.cpp:799-800; the same pattern at saveload_update.cpp:999, 1604, 1624 and persistence_saves.cpp:171/184). The job results are then read as plain data: _saves (persistence_savelist_job.cpp), the loaded SavedState buffers (LoadJob) and _blockDescs. Under the C++ memory model this is a data race, which is UB. On aarch64 the main thread can observe status==1 / runFlags==0 before the worker's earlier stores to _saves or the block data, and so read a stale or half-built save list or load buffer.
minimal_fix: Give the completion word release/acquire semantics. The worker publishes with `__atomic_store_n(&_status, v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)` (or the worker side of ThreadFunc clears `_runFlags` with a release store). The pollers in SaveLoad::Update, UpdateList states 3/4 and Persistence::GetSaveCount/GetSaveInfo read `_runFlags` and `_status` with `__atomic_load_n(..., __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)`. Field layout and widths stay retail's; only the access spelling changes. Drop the `volatile` cast at saveload_update.cpp:999 in favour of the same acquire load.

title: System::CRC::Compute builds its table lazily through a non-atomic `static bool built`: two threads making their first CRC call race on the flag and the 1 KB table (retail's table is static data)
bug_class: C12 data race on lazy init
label: port
label_evidence: Retail reads a prebuilt exported table and has no init branch.
reachability: Callers run on different threads. One is the IO::PersistenceWorker save-info job (persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp:254, worker thread, when the save list is built). The other is ext.resources' ProvideSprites -> LogWriterCrc (ext_sprites.cpp:62/116, ExternalFactory load path, Loader or main thread). The race needs both first calls to overlap, which is a narrow window. On ARM64, a thread can see `built==true` before the table stores land, read zero entries and compute a wrong CRC, and the save-info job then marks a good save as corrupt (badFile).
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1800c5490: `TEST EDX,EDX / JLE 0x1800c54c0 / MOV R9D,EDX / LEA R10,[0x1801f9080] / MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RCX] / MOVZX EDX,R8B / ... / MOV R8D,dword ptr [R10 + RDX*0x4]`. The table at 0x1801f9080 is used directly, with no flag and no build. Port crc.cpp:46-57: `static uint32_t table[256]; static bool built = false; if (!built) { ...table[i] = c; built = true; }`. TSan (crc_tsan.cpp, two std::threads calling System::CRC::Compute once each, linked with the real crc.cpp), 5/5 runs: `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race #0 CrcTable() crc.cpp:49:10 ... #0 CrcTable() crc.cpp:55:15` (the flag) and `data race #0 System::CRC::Compute crc.cpp:70:19 ... #0 CrcTable() crc.cpp:53:22` (a table entry read while another thread writes it).
root_cause: The port replaced retail's static data table with a lazily filled function-local array guarded by a plain bool. That is not thread-safe, although the function runs on worker threads.
minimal_fix: Build the table at compile time (a constexpr generator into a `static constexpr std::array<uint32_t,256>`), or use a C++11 magic-static initialiser `static const Table table = Build();`. Either removes the flag. The same pattern exists in io/persistence_worker.cpp, io/persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp and object/type_reflection.cpp (outside this scope), and these copies can share the one constexpr table.

title: String::ToInteger accumulates digits with signed int overflow (UB); the comment's 'retail simply wraps, and so do we' does not hold in C++
bug_class: signed integer overflow
label: retail
label_evidence: The port comment cites retail 0x18003f664..0x18003f670, `EDX = c + 2*(5*EDX - 24)` in 32-bit LEA/ADD, which wraps silently in hardware. The port writes the same expression on a C++ int, which is UB once it passes INT_MAX.
reachability: User text in number edit fields (numbereditelement.cpp:82, spinnerelement.cpp:202/211/225, widgets_input.cpp:390/423/629/638, e.g. the new-game seed) and numbers in UI document text (documenttext.cpp:577).
proof: Repro tointeger.cpp: System::String::ToInteger("99999999999"). UBSan reports: string.cpp:818:29: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 999999999 * 10 cannot be represented in type 'int'.
root_cause: `result = result * 10 + digit` on int32 with unbounded digit runs. The faithful wrap needs unsigned arithmetic.
minimal_fix: Accumulate in uint32_t: `uint32_t r = 0; ... r = r * 10u + uint32_t(d - '0'); ... return static_cast<int>(sign < 0 ? 0u - r : r);`. Same bits as retail's LEA chain, no UB.

title: System::Thread::_runFlags is a plain uint32_t that the worker RMWs and other threads poll as the job-done flag: a data race, and no happens-before for the job's results
bug_class: C11/C12 data race, flag used as sync without ordering
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800ca440: 1800ca483 `OR dword ptr [RBX+0x8],0x1` and 1800ca499 `AND dword ptr [RBX+0x8],0xfffffffe` are plain non-LOCK RMWs. Readers such as LoaderLoopAdvance (`testb $1,0x1801fe7c0`) and the Persistence polls are plain loads. Retail relies on x86 TSO and on MSVC treating the opaque Run call as a barrier.
reachability: Every run. The Loader's bit is polled every loading frame (engine/loops.cpp:750). The Persistence worker's bit is polled at saveload_update.cpp:379/797/1073/1433/1604/1624, persistence_saves.cpp:171-228, savedstate_setupload.cpp:131, and the main thread then reads or frees worker-owned data. Example: saveload_update.cpp:1433 frees `_worker._saves` and 1604 reads `_status` once the bit is clear. The pathfinder bit is read at action_pf_astar.cpp:789, keystone_a_zone.cpp:64/105 and path_query_first.cpp:45. The audio Stream bit is read at audio_device.cpp:277. On the ARM64 builds (Android, Apple silicon) the plain clear can become visible before Run's earlier stores, so the main thread can read a stale `_status`/`_saves`, or free `_saves` while the worker's late stores still land.
proof: runflags_tsan.cpp (TSan, the real thread.cpp + posix platform files) gives two reports. (1) `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 4 at 0x721000000008 by thread T1: #0 System::Thread::ThreadFunc(void*) src/engine/system/thread.cpp:205:25 ... Previous read of size 4 ... by main thread: #0 main runflags_tsan.cpp:36` (the `_runFlags & 1` poll). (2) `data race ... Read of size 4 at 0x721000000034 by main thread (result read after observing bit 0 clear) ... Previous write ... by thread T1: #0 Worker::Run() ... #1 System::Thread::ThreadFunc thread.cpp:206`. So observing the clear bit orders nothing: the job's stores are not guaranteed visible.
root_cause: The completion flag is a non-atomic field written with plain RMWs and read with plain loads on other threads. No release/acquire pairs the worker's job writes with the reader's 'bit clear' observation.
minimal_fix: Access `_runFlags` through `__atomic` builtins (layout unchanged, still uint32_t at +0x08). Make the set a relaxed fetch_or, the clear a `__atomic_fetch_and(&_runFlags, ~1u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)`, and every reader `__atomic_load_n(&t->_runFlags, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)`, through one helper such as `bool Thread::IsRunning() const`. This emits identical code on x86 (plain MOV loads, LOCK AND), so it does not change x86 behaviour.

title: Timer::CurrentTimeTicks overflows int64 after 10.7 days of uptime: (now - _systemInitialTick) * 1e6 is signed overflow (UB)
bug_class: signed integer overflow
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800ca8f0: CALL [QueryPerformanceCounter] / MOV RAX,[RSP+0x30] / SUB RAX,[0x1801fe738] / IMUL RAX,[0x1801fe720] / CQO / IDIV [0x1801fe730]. The 64-bit IMUL wraps in hardware, and the port spells the same expression on int64_t.
reachability: A game session (or a paused game left open) running more than about 10.7 days on a 10 MHz counter. Plausible for idle or server-like sessions. Not input-driven.
proof: Repro timer_ticks.cpp: set System::Timer::_systemInitialTick = now - 11 days * 10 MHz, then call CurrentTimeTicks(). UBSan reports: timer.cpp:293:39: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 9504000000002 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t'.
root_cause: The elapsed counter delta is multiplied by _ticksPerSecond (1e6) before dividing by the counter frequency. At 10 MHz (Windows QPC on most machines, and the posix/darwin PerfCounter by design: time_posix.cpp banner) the product passes INT64_MAX after 9.22e12 counter units, about 10.7 days. After that the engine clock goes negative or jumps, and MainLoop's frame timing reads it every frame (loops.cpp:1133, mainloop_run.cpp:281/314/316 via the same expression in mainloop_frame.cpp, application.cpp:94).
minimal_fix: Split the conversion so it cannot overflow and matches retail's result while retail does not wrap: `d = now - init; return (d / f) * tps + (d % f) * tps / f;`. Apply the same change to mainloop_frame.cpp CurrentTimeTicksViaGlobals and application.cpp:94.

title: DateTime::DateAsString/TimeAsString ignore all three conversion results: a zero (failed-stat) save timestamp formats an uninitialised stack buffer in western time zones
bug_class: unchecked return value -> swallowed failure -> read of uninitialised memory (UB; possible stack over-read in WideStrLen)
label: retail
label_evidence: The disassembly of Runtime 0x1800c56a0 calls FileTimeToLocalFileTime [0x18014b120], then FileTimeToSystemTime [0x18014b128], then GetDateFormatW [0x18014b130] with cch=0x100, and never tests EAX after any of them. It then builds a WideString from [RSP+0x50] (CALL 0x1800caf40) and converts it with AsUTF8 (CALL 0x1800cacd0). The Win32 platform body (src/platform/win/file_win.cpp:126) reproduces this on purpose ('DELIBERATELY UNINITIALISED'). The POSIX twin returns an empty string instead, so only the Windows build has the bug.
reachability: IO::FileSystem::GetFileTimeStamp (filesystem_timestamp.cpp:119) returns DateTime{} (zero) on every failure arm. One example: CreateFileW with FILE_SHARE_READ fails while another process (OneDrive or other cloud sync of Documents, antivirus, a concurrent writer) holds the save open with write access. persistence_savelist_job.cpp:211 stores that zero as entry.sortKey. SaveLoad copies it to row.sortKey (saveload_update.cpp:1501). saveloaddialog.cpp:321 calls saveInfo.sortKey.AsString() for every save whose metadata version is 2. In any time zone west of UTC, FileTimeToLocalFileTime(0) gives a negative FILETIME, so the next two calls fail as shown above.
proof: Retail 0x1800c56a0: `LEA RDX,[RSP+0x270] / CALL [0x18014b120]` (FileTimeToLocalFileTime) ; `LEA RDX,[RSP+0x40] / LEA RCX,[RSP+0x270] / CALL [0x18014b128]` (FileTimeToSystemTime) ; `MOV dword [RSP+0x28],0x100 / LEA RAX,[RSP+0x50] / ... / MOV ECX,0x400 / CALL [0x18014b130]` (GetDateFormatW) ; `LEA RDX,[RSP+0x50] / LEA RCX,[RSP+0x260] / CALL 0x1800caf40` (WideString(buf)). None of the three results is tested. Port: value_types.cpp:412 `Platform::PathChar buf[kDateTimeChars]; // also uninitialised`, then :415 `Platform::FormatLocalDateTime(...)`, then `const System::WideString ws(buf);`. A Windows run of scratchpad/p8/src_engine_system_src_engine_collection_errors/ft.c on this machine (bias=300, UTC-5) printed: `ToLocal ok=1 local=ffffffd61729f800` for FILETIME 0; `ToSystem(neg) ok=0 err=87 st.wYear=cccc`; `GetDateFormatW ret=0 err=87 buf[0]=cccc`. The SYSTEMTIME and the output buffer keep their 0xCC poison, so WideString(buf) then runs WideStrLen over indeterminate stack WCHARs until it happens to find a zero, which can be past the 0x100-WCHAR buffer.
root_cause: The DateTime formatter treats the Win32 conversion chain as infallible: no BOOL or int result is checked, and the output buffer is not pre-initialised. When the chain fails, the buffer is read as a NUL-terminated wide string.
minimal_fix: As a fix.* row (retail shares the behaviour): set buf[0] = 0 before Platform::FormatLocalDateTime, or have the Win32 FormatLocalDateTime write out[0] = 0 when any of the three calls fails. That makes a failed conversion yield the empty string, as the POSIX twin already does.

title: AnimatedImageElement::Update wraps the clock only once: a tick longer than two periods indexes _frames past its end, and an empty frame list converts NaN to int
bug_class: float->int out of range (NaN) and an array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800cb290: `1800cb2fc COMISS XMM1,XMM2 ; 1800cb2ff JC 0x1800cb318 ; 1800cb301 SUBSS XMM1,XMM2` (a single subtract, no loop), then `1800cb320 DIVSS XMM1,XMM2 ; 1800cb324 CVTDQ2PS XMM0,XMM0 ; 1800cb327 MULSS XMM1,XMM0 ; 1800cb32b CVTTSS2SI EAX,XMM1 ; 1800cb32f MOVSXD RCX,EAX ; 1800cb339 ADD RCX,RCX ; 1800cb33c MOVUPS XMM1,[RAX+RCX*8]`. No clamp against _frames._size. The port matches line for line.
reachability: Every input is resource data. AnimatedImageDescription::CreateInstance (animatedimagedescription.cpp:163-172) copies _frameNames._size and _framesPerSecond with no checks. A mod dialog (or a mod override of Dialog/Loading.rsc, which AutoSave.rsc inherits) that declares an AnimatedImage with no frames, or with fps above 60 times the frame count, reaches it on the first UI tick. The as-shipped Loading.rsc (62 frames at 30 fps, fixed 1/60 s step) is safe.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_ui_ub/animimage_frame.cpp: 1 frame, _framesPerSecond 1000, a 1/60 s tick. `fz.sh build ui_animimage src/engine/ui/animatedimageelement.cpp` compiled the objects but its link failed on missing Element/ImageElement symbols, so the binary was relinked by hand with the same sanitizer flags plus -no-pie -Wl,--unresolved-symbols=ignore-all. Output: `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 8 ... #0 UI::AnimatedImageElement::Update animatedimageelement.cpp:118:25` (frame 15 of 1). The same binary with input byte 0x01 (empty frame list): `animatedimageelement.cpp:115:40: runtime error: -nan is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'`.
root_cause: `if (elapsed >= period) elapsed -= period` assumes one tick never exceeds one full cycle. When period is 0 (no frames), (elapsed/0)*0 is NaN and is converted to int.
minimal_fix: fix.* row: wrap with fmod (or loop while elapsed >= period), clamp frame to [0, _frames._size - 1], and return early when _frames._size == 0.

title: Font glyph walks bound the glyph index by the sprite sheet's count, then index the font's own shorter _glyphs table
bug_class: array index bounded against the wrong array (heap OOB read)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail ComputeLineLayout 0x180116c70: `180116d1a MOVSXD RDX,[RAX+RCX*4] ; ... 180116d3b MOV RAX,[RBP+0x60] ; 180116d3f CMP EDX,[RAX+0x28] ; 180116d42 JGE ... ; 180116d52 SHL RBX,0x4 ; 180116d56 ADD RBX,[RBP+0x40]`. The glyph is compared against SpriteSheet+0x28 (sprite count) only, then scaled into Font+0x40 (_glyphs). _glyphs._size at +0x48 is never compared. The same pattern appears at font.cpp:146 (MeasureLiteral), 414, 503 and 654.
reachability: Font::Serialize (font.cpp:332-343) reads the glyph row count from the font resource independently of the sprite sheet's count, which comes from the separate SpriteSheet resource. A mod font, or a mod that replaces the sheet a stock font references, with fewer glyph rows than sprites causes out-of-bounds reads on every text layout that hits a high glyph. Stock fonts are consistent.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_ui_ub/font_glyph.cpp: a sheet with 10 sprites, a font with 8 codepoint entries (identity map) and 1 glyph row, then ComputeCharacterPosition("\x05", 1). Built from src/engine/ui/font.cpp and src/engine/io/text_codec.cpp; `fz.sh build` compiled the objects but its link failed, so the binary was relinked by hand with the same sanitizer flags plus -no-pie --allow-multiple-definition --unresolved-symbols=ignore-all. Output: `ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 4 ... #0 UI::Font::ComputeCharacterPosition font.cpp:503:36`.
root_cause: The glyph validity test checks `glyph < sheet->m_sprites._size` (needed for the sprite read in ComputeLineLayout) but never `glyph < _glyphs._size`, and the kerning row is read from _glyphs.
minimal_fix: fix.* row: also require `glyph < _glyphs._size` in the four walks (MeasureLiteral, ComputeLineLayout, ComputeCharacterPosition, ComputeStringLayout), or validate at load in Font::Serialize that every _charToGlyph entry below 0xffff is less than _glyphs._size.

title: UserInterface::Play shifts the int32 play counter left by 9: signed-shift UB once Scene::playGeneration reaches 2^23 (retail's SHL wraps)
bug_class: signed left-shift overflow
label: port
label_evidence: Retail Play 0x1801223d0: `180122447 INC dword ptr [R10+0x8] ; 18012244b MOV ECX,dword ptr [R10+0x8] ; 18012244f LEA EAX,[R9+R9*1] ; 180122453 SHL ECX,0x9 ; 180122456 OR EAX,ECX ; 180122458 MOV [RDX+0x68],EAX`. That is a 32-bit wrap, which is defined. Port: `const int32_t counter = ++scene->playGeneration; slot.handleTag = static_cast<uint32_t>((index * 2) | (counter << 9));`, a signed shift. The sibling sites userinterface_close.cpp:371 and audio.cpp:388/536 already shift a uint32_t; this one and documenttextelement.cpp:151 (`scene->playGeneration << 9` in PlayInline, the inlined copy at the hover and click sounds) do not.
reachability: Scene::playGeneration is shared by every PlayEffect / PlayEffect3D in the scene (audio.cpp), as well as UI clicks and hovers, and it is never reset during a session. It reaches 2^23 after about 8.4 M sound starts in one long session. The next UI click or hover sound is then UB, and the optimiser may assume counter < 2^22.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_ui_ub/play_shift.cpp: playGeneration = 2^23-1, then ui->Play(0). `fz.sh build ui_play_shift src/engine/ui/userinterface.cpp` compiled the objects but its link failed, so the binary was relinked by hand with the same sanitizer flags plus -no-pie --allow-multiple-definition --unresolved-symbols=ignore-all. Output: `userinterface.cpp:689:67: runtime error: left shift of 8388608 by 9 places cannot be represented in type 'int32_t' ... #0 UI::UserInterface::Play(int)`.
root_cause: The port spelled retail's 32-bit SHL as a C++ signed shift of an int32_t. C++17 leaves that undefined once the result exceeds the unsigned range; retail's instruction simply wraps.
minimal_fix: Shift an unsigned value, as userinterface_close.cpp:371 already does: `(static_cast<uint32_t>(index) * 2u) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(counter) << 9)`, and the same at documenttextelement.cpp:151. To also avoid the increment overflow at 2^31, increment through uint32_t.

title: Video::Device::ValidateConfiguration indexes adapter->multisampleData with the unvalidated settings value VideoMultisample (heap OOB read)
bug_class: UB: out-of-bounds read on unvalidated persisted index
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800f89f3: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX+0x18] (adapter->multisampleData) / MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [RSP+0xa8] (cfg->multisample) / CMP byte ptr [RDX+RCX*1],0x0 / CMOVZ EDX,R10D. There is no compare against multisampleCount (+0x20). The port's banner at device_startup.cpp:150 notes this as retail's.
reachability: "VideoMultisample" comes from the user-editable settings file via Configuration::Startup with no range check. A negative or too-large value reads outside the Array<bool> at boot. When the stray byte is non-zero, the bad index survives and is written back to cfg->multisample, then reaches the renderer's sample-count selection. A wild index far enough out faults. The 8-argument ValidateConfiguration (device.cpp:261, options dialog path) has the same unchecked `adapter->multisampleData[antialias]`.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_graphics_src_engine_video_errors/vcfg_multisample_oob.cpp. The adapter's multisample list is new uint8_t[4]{1,1,1,0} with multisampleCount=4. Configuration has refreshD=1 and multisample=64. Built with `fz.sh build p8vid_msoob src/engine/video/device_startup.cpp` and run with `-runs=1`. Result: `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow src/engine/video/device_startup.cpp:259:9 in Video::Device::ValidateConfiguration()`, which is `if (adapter->multisampleData[msIdx] == 0) msIdx = 0;`.

title: System::Thread::_runFlags is a plain uint32 that the worker read-modify-writes while RequestFirst / RequestPath read it after Unlock (lost Start, data race)
bug_class: C11 lost wake-up / data race on a non-atomic flag
label: retail
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (retail shape, not a port divergence): retail RequestPath 0x1400a6c10: `1400a6cc7: LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x30]` / `1400a6ccb: CALL qword ptr [0x140152550]` (CriticalSection Unlock) / `1400a6cd1: TEST byte ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x1` / `1400a6cda: JNZ 0x1400a6ce5` / `1400a6cdf: CALL qword ptr [0x140152558]` (Thread::Start). The port's line is path_query_first.cpp:45 `pf->lock.Unlock(); if ((pf->_runFlags & 1) == 0) pf->Start();`. The worker side is thread.cpp:205 `self->_runFlags |= 1u` and :210 `self->_runFlags &= ~1u`, both plain RMWs with no lock. Interleaving: the worker finds the queue empty under the lock, unlocks and returns from Run. Main pushes the query at the head under the lock and unlocks. Main reads _runFlags while bit 0 is still 1 and skips Start(). The worker then clears bit 0 and exits. The query stays queued until RunPathQuery's spin (keystone_a_zone.cpp:110-113) re-checks queueCount/_runFlags under the lock. That re-check is a read under a lock the writer never takes, so it is also a race.
root_cause: Retail's Thread::_runFlags (+0x08, Thread.h:259) is a plain field used as a cross-thread 'running' flag: the worker sets and clears it outside any lock, and the enqueuers read it outside or under a different lock. Under the C++ model this is a data race (UB), and a lost Start is possible: the window between the worker's empty-queue check and its clear of bit 0. path_query_first copies the shape for the synchronous road and boat query. Only the YieldToThreads spin recovers it, and DiagThreads also reads the word as const volatile. Retail shares this; the user ruling makes all UB a finding.
minimal_fix: Access _runFlags through std::atomic_ref<uint32_t> (fetch_or/fetch_and release in ThreadFunc, load acquire at the Start() checks). This keeps the +0x08 layout. Optionally do the bit test and Start() under pf->lock in RequestFirst, as the spin loop already does.
module: src/ext threads that run by default (derived_cache writer, path_query_first, create_on_demand / async_gpu_create if on by default: check)

title: P13_OVERLAP claims the steps while the emit is short of BeginCommands: the message pump / options apply write Video::Device::settingsChanged + backBufferWidth/Height that the render thread's BeginCommands reads, so Dx11_DeviceData_Resize (AdjustDisplay/SetWindowPos/ResizeTarget) runs on the render thread (the 32250bb88/744e4345d FAA-MENU deadlock shape)
bug_class: C11 data race / cross-thread deadlock (steps run beside an emit that has not reached BeginCommands)
label: ext
label_evidence: The overlap (pipe_driver.h BeforeSteps -> Handoff::ClaimSteps, handoff.h:96) is NOT RETAIL (docs/android/P13_OVERLAP.md). Retail has no render thread. The racing engine writers are retail bodies used as retail uses them: Video::Device::SizeWindow (device_window.cpp:76, retail 0x1800f7d10 family) and Device::ApplyChangedSettings (device.cpp:298). The port-only SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync (sunlight.cpp:324/345) also writes settingsChanged.
reachability: ext.render_pipe on, with the render thread up (>= 3 physical cores) and the overlap governor switched on. The governor turns on when the frame does not idle (a busy town on desktop or Android) and holds for 120 frames. Then, during the overlapped steps, either the window is resized or moved (MainLoop::Frame's step loop calls Platform::Pump -> WindowProc -> SizeWindow), or the player presses Apply in the Options dialog (Shadow Resolution / resolution) or toggles max_shadow_res in the Extensions tab. Both run inside UpdateLoop::Update, within the steps. The emit is short of BeginCommands while it waits for a swap-chain image; the governor measures exactly this as 'the fence's waits for an emit still short of BeginCommands' (~7 of 11 ms on the S10).
proof:
TSan, using the real src/ext/render_pipe/handoff.h: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_graphics_src_engine_video_concurrency/overlap_settings_race.cpp, built with clang++-19 -fsanitize=thread -I src.

The repro: main calls Publish, then ClaimSteps() (returns 1 with BegunUs=0, i.e. the emit is short of BeginCommands), then the step write settingsChanged=1, backBufferWidth=1920 (SizeWindow), then OpenGate and WaitIdle. The render thread calls WaitJob, waits for the swap chain, reads settingsChanged (ContextData::BeginCommands, contextdata.cpp:441), then NoteBegun, then the Gate.

Output: 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Read of size 1 ... by thread T1 (overlap_settings_race.cpp:26, the BeginCommands read) / Previous write of size 1 ... by main thread (overlap_settings_race.cpp:41, the SizeWindow write) ... ClaimSteps=1 BegunUs=0 ... render thread: settingsChanged=1 backBufferWidth=1920 -> Dx11_DeviceData_Resize on the render thread'.

Why the fences do not cover it: in the real code the sequential decision (pipe_state.h:61, in.settingsChanged read at render_pipe.cpp:674) is taken at the tail, before the packet is published. A flag raised during the overlapped steps reaches the already-published emit's BeginCommands (packet.h:102). That runs Dx11_DeviceData_Resize -> AdjustDisplay (devicedata.cpp:804, SetWindowPos on the main thread's HWND) / ResizeTarget / SetFullscreenState on the render thread. Those calls send messages to the main thread synchronously. The main thread then leaves the steps for Tail -> OpenGate -> FenceReleased/WaitReleased, a condition-variable wait that does not pump, which is the same deadlock commits 32250bb88 and 744e4345d fixed for the non-overlapped path.

P13_OVERLAP.md's read/write table lists only ClearResourcesIfDirty/BeginFailed's MainLoop fields for the E1 span. It omits Device::settingsChanged and the back-buffer size, which BeginCommands reads.
root_cause: Handoff::ClaimSteps (handoff.h:96-101) admits the steps whenever the job is not past its Gate (!_passed && _busy). It does not require the job to be past BeginCommands. The E1 span (FrameTailTime .. Pass2) is assumed to read only the packet, its Renderer slot and the snapshot. But E1's BeginCommands reads live Video::Device state (settingsChanged, backBufferWidth/Height, Configuration) that the steps' message pump and UI apply write with no ordering, and a set flag makes the render thread do the swap-chain/window reset.
minimal_fix: In Handoff::ClaimSteps, also refuse the claim while _begunUs == 0, so the steps keep THE FENCE until the emit's BeginCommands has returned. NoteBegun must then store with release order and ClaimSteps read with acquire, or NoteBegun must be set under _m. Alternatively, have the emit's BeginCommands op treat settingsChanged != 0 as BeginFailed, leaving the resize to the next sequential (main-thread) frame.

bug_class: out-of-range float->int conversion (UB)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail uses CVTTSS2SI, which yields 0x80000000 (defined in x86), and then clamps to 0. In C++ the same conversion is UB. The port's static_cast/(int) is the faithful translation of that instruction, so the behaviour matches only by accident of codegen.
reachability: MoveTo::destination is read from the save by Vector3::Serialize (moveto.cpp:168) with no validation. MoveTo::Execute case 2 (moveto.cpp:383) and PathSetup (via AbstractImpl) convert it on the first tick after the load. A NaN or huge coordinate in a save reaches it. Live play produces in-map positions only.
proof: Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_game_Action_ub/worldtocell.cpp carries WorldToCell / ClampCell verbatim from moveto.cpp:117-131, with worldX = 1e10 (a saved MoveTo::destination.x). clang++-19 -fsanitize=undefined,float-cast-overflow: 'runtime error: 1e+10 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'' at the `(int)(worldX + halfMap)` line. The same pattern is in action_base_move.cpp:385 (PathSetup's clamp lambda `int v = static_cast<int>(f);`) on destination.x/y.

minimal_fix: Clamp in float before converting: `float f = worldX + halfMap; int v = (f >= 0.0f && f < (float)mapSize) ? (int)f : (f >= (float)mapSize ? mapSize - 1 : 0);` (NaN takes the 0 arm, as retail's 0x80000000 -> 0). Apply it in moveto.cpp WorldToCell and action_base_move.cpp PathSetup. This changes no in-range result.

title: CemeteryComponent::EnterBuilt shifts 1u by the saved terrainType byte without the & 0x1f mask (shift exponent up to 255)
bug_class: UB-shift-exponent
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x140047100 MOVZX ECX,byte ptr [RDI+0x29]; 0x140047104 SHL EAX,CL. x86 masks CL to 5 bits, so retail is defined for any byte. Every other port site of this idiom in the module writes `1u << (x & 0x1f)` (pasturecomponent_states.cpp:436, pasturecomponent.cpp:340, citizen_lifeevent_handler.cpp:231, quarrycomponent_deform.cpp:316); this one dropped the mask.
reachability: MapCell::terrainType is restored by Map::Serialize as a raw uchar (Map.h:86), and the cell index comes from the cemetery's saved plot list. Loading a save whose cell byte is >= 32 under a cemetery plot, then finishing (or reloading into) a built cemetery, runs this line. Normal play writes only small values (2..10), so only a corrupt or crafted save reaches it.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x140046fc0 (cemetery state-2 enter):
  1400470f9: ADD RDI,qword ptr [R14 + 0x80]
  140047100: MOVZX ECX,byte ptr [RDI + 0x29]   ; cell->terrainType
  140047104: SHL EAX,CL                         ; EAX=1, CL masked by hardware
  140047106: TEST EAX,0x1e0
  14004710e: OR byte ptr [R14 + 0xa2],AL
port cemeterycomponent.cpp:196-197: `const uint8_t zone = cell->terrainType; const bool walkableZone = ((1u << zone) & 0x1e0u) != 0;`
Sanitizer repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_game_Component_ub/cemetery_shift.cpp (clang++-19 -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined, -runs=1): 'cemetery_shift.cpp:12:36: runtime error: shift exponent 40 is too large for 32-bit type 'unsigned int''.
root_cause: The hardware shift-count mask that retail's SHL relies on was not carried into C++ at this one site. In C++, a shift by 32 or more is UB, and GCC may fold it (for example walkableZone=false for any value, or arbitrary results), which would diverge from retail's bit = 1 << (zone & 31).
minimal_fix: `const bool walkableZone = ((1u << (zone & 0x1f)) & 0x1e0u) != 0;`, the same form as the sibling sites.

title: StatGoal::SumProductionWindow: ((year - statSubType) - 1) * 0x30 is int32 signed overflow for out-of-range serialized statSubType
bug_class: signed overflow (data-driven)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400d8c50 does the same 32-bit wrapping arithmetic: `MOV EAX,dword ptr [RDI]; SUB EAX,dword ptr [RBP+0x7c]; DEC EAX; LEA R8D,[RAX+RAX*0x2]; SHL R8D,0x4; CALL 0x140090f20` (and `LEA R9D,[RBX+RBX*0x2]; SHL R9D,0x4; ADD R9D,-0x30` for hi). reachability: An achievement StatGoal with statType 0x14 whose statSubType comes from modded or crafted .rsc data. The goal is evaluated every tick by CheckGoalState.
proof: UBSan repro scratchpad/p8/src_game_Goal_src_game_Tutorial_src_game_ub/statgoal_window_overflow.cpp (raw GameUpdateLoop/CitizenBehavior/Calendar, statFlags 0x20, statSubType INT_MIN, StatValue(0x14)), built with build.sh statwin ... src/game/Goal/statvaluedispatch.cpp: `statvaluedispatch.cpp:604:28: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1 - -2147483648 cannot be represented in type 'int32_t'  #0 StatGoal::SumProductionWindow() const statvaluedispatch.cpp:604:28`.

title: FormatLocalDateTime ignores both conversion results, so a failed FILETIME conversion leaves the 0x100-wchar buffer uninitialised and WideString(buf) reads it (indeterminate read, possible over-read past the buffer)
bug_class: unchecked return value -> use of uninitialised memory
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Runtime 0x1800c56a0 (DateAsString): 1800c56c9 CALL [0x18014b120] FileTimeToLocalFileTime; 1800c56dc CALL [0x18014b128] FileTimeToSystemTime; 1800c5705 CALL [0x18014b130] GetDateFormatW(0x400,1,&st,0,[RSP+0x50],0x100); 1800c570b MOV [RSP+0x260],0; 1800c5724 CALL 0x1800caf40 (WideString::Set on [RSP+0x50]). No result is tested and nothing stores to [RSP+0x50] beforehand. The port keeps this on purpose (value_types.cpp:382 banner and file_win.cpp:124).
reachability: saveloaddialog.cpp:321 formats `saveInfo.sortKey.AsString()` for every valid save (field44==2). sortKey comes from FileSystem::GetFileTimeStamp (filesystem_timestamp.cpp:119), which returns DateTime{} (FILETIME 0) whenever CreateFileW(GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ) on the save fails, for example while another process holds the save open for writing (a OneDrive-synced Documents folder or an antivirus scan). The probe shows that in any time zone west of UTC, FILETIME 0 fails conversion, which leads straight to the uninitialised read.
proof: I ran the exact call sequence on this machine (Eastern Standard Time) with a 0xCCCC-filled 256-wchar output buffer, using scratchpad ft_probe.py (Python ctypes). Results: FILETIME 0 gives FileTimeToLocalFileTime=1 (local hi=0xffffffd6, negative), FileTimeToSystemTime=0, GetDateFormatW=0, and the buffer is still 쳌... Inputs 0x7fff...ffff and 0x8000...0000 give GetDateFormatW=0 with the buffer untouched; 0xffff...ffff gives FileTimeToSystemTime=0 and GetDateFormatW=0. In every failure case the port's `Platform::PathChar buf[kDateTimeChars]` (value_types.cpp:412, uninitialised) is then handed to `System::WideString ws(buf)` (value_types.cpp:423), which scans for a terminator in indeterminate wchar_t data. That read is UB, and it can run past the 0x100-unit array into the rest of the frame.
root_cause: The return values of FileTimeToLocalFileTime, FileTimeToSystemTime and GetDateFormatW/GetTimeFormatW are discarded, and the output buffer has no defined content when they fail. The port faithfully keeps retail's uninitialised locals.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening, with no behaviour change on success. In FormatLocalDateTime, set out[0] = 0 before the calls (or when GetDateFormatW/GetTimeFormatW returns 0), so a failed conversion yields an empty string. Note it as a fix.* or a divergence row, because the value_types.cpp banner deliberately keeps it uninitialised.
