The record copies BufferRecord::Publish (`*_out = _made`). A reader thread runs the PrefetchGathered pattern: `VertexBufferMade(c)` (`buffer != nullptr`), then `t->Prefetch(c)`. TSan report: "WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 8 by thread T2 (mutexes: write M0): #0 BufferRecordModel::Publish() ... #1 LazyTable::RunClaimed lazy_table.cpp:90 #2 LazyTable::WorkerMain lazy_table.cpp:286 ... Previous read of size 8 by thread T1: #0 VertexBufferMade(void const*) ...". The reader holds no lock (it never takes M0).
root_cause: Record::Publish (lazy_table.cpp:90, inside RunClaimed on a prefetch worker) stores the new handle with a plain write under the table's _mutex. These sites read the same field without that mutex and without any atomic: CreateOnDemandBackend::VertexBufferMade / ImageMade (lazy_create.cpp:369-376, called from ext/create_on_demand/prefetch.cpp:95 PrefetchGathered on the gather thread), and the `if (buffer == nullptr) CreateOnDemand::Ensure(this)` / `if (shaderResourceView == nullptr)` fast paths in buffers.cpp (Bind / Lock / SetData) and imagebufferdata.cpp:855. A UseScope only shuts out Evict (through the UseGate); it does nothing to order Publish against these reads. Evict (sweep, under a closed gate) also nulls the field while PrefetchGathered reads it without the gate.
minimal_fix: Publish the handle with release semantics and read it with acquire, e.g. std::atomic_ref<ID3D11Buffer*>(*_out).store(_made, std::memory_order_release) in Publish and Evict, and atomic_ref loads (acquire) in VertexBufferMade, ImageMade and the slot fast-path null tests. This keeps the field's type and offset unchanged for the binary-compatible header. Alternatively, have VertexBufferMade / ImageMade ask the table for the entry's state under its mutex instead of reading the companion field.

title: create_on_demand: a deferred object's GPU handle is read without synchronisation as the 'made' test while a prefetch worker's Record::Publish writes it under the table mutex
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads / data race (unsynchronised publication)
label: ext
proof: TSan, two standalone repros linking the real src/render/common/create_on_demand/lazy_table.cpp and use_tracker.cpp (clang++-19 -fsanitize=thread). (1) cod_gather_race.cpp copies PrefetchGathered: `if (!VertexBufferMade(c)) table.Prefetch(c)` once per frame. Report: 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Read of size 8 ... by main thread: #0 VertexBufferMade ... Previous write of size 8 ... by thread T1 (mutexes: write M0): #0 FakeRecord::Publish() #1 LazyTable::RunClaimed lazy_table.cpp:90 #2 LazyTable::WorkerMain lazy_table.cpp:286'. (2) cod_handle_race.cpp: Keep(c), then the Bind fast path `Enter(); Use(c); if (c->buffer == nullptr) Ensure(c); read c->buffer; Leave()`. Report: data race between the main-thread read at the handle test and Publish under M0 (RunClaimed:90, WorkerMain:286). With Prefetch instead of Keep and Enter/Use, TSan stays silent: the UseStamps::Touch acquire load pairs with Insert's release store, which follows Publish. So the slots are covered only for tracked objects, and only after Insert.
root_cause: Record::Publish writes the companion's handle fields while holding LazyTable::_mutex: `*_out = _made` (dx11 BufferRecord/TextureRecord), and Vulkan BufferRecord writes `_store->gpu = _made; immutable = true`. The readers never take that mutex and do no acquire before testing the handle. These readers are CreateOnDemandBackend::VertexBufferMade/ImageMade (called by Ext::CreateOnDemand::PrefetchGathered, prefetch.cpp:95, every gathered level every frame, no UseScope) and every slot fast path `if (buffer == nullptr) Ensure(this)` (dx11 buffers.cpp:597/606/626/674/684/716, imagebufferdata.cpp:855/886/919; vulkan companions.cpp:583/621; metal backend.mm). The UseScope's Touch synchronises only through UseStamps::Insert. Keep'd objects are never Inserted (RunClaimed: `e.tracked = !e.kept && ...`); these are UI sprite sheets via SpriteSheet::_extLoaded, and terrain/water/batch materials via WorldGeometry::_extMaterialTaken. So the first Bind of each such object races with the worker's Publish. DX11 has no FinishPrefetches drain at the bracket end, so a worker can publish while the main thread is drawing. On Vulkan, a reader that sees gpu.buffer non-null may still see stale gpu.allocation/size or immutable==false: the struct copy order is unspecified and there is no acquire.
minimal_fix: Publish the handle with release and test it with acquire. Use std::atomic_ref<T*>(field).store(v, release) in Publish/Evict, and an acquire load in VertexBufferMade/ImageMade and the slot fast paths. On Vulkan, write gpu.buffer last, as the release store, after allocation/size/immutable. Alternatively, call Insert (or another release store the reader acquires) for kept objects too, and give PrefetchGathered a UseScope.
module: src/ext threads that run by default (derived_cache writer, path_query_first, create_on_demand / async_gpu_create if on by default: check)

title: Swap-chain rebuild reads refreshData[refreshRateIndex] of a different display mode after an Options resolution change (heap out-of-bounds read)
bug_class: out-of-bounds read / stale index across display-mode change
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Runtime ApplyChangedSettings 0x1800f8110 re-picks Device+0x0c and never touches +0x10. Its disassembly: `MOV R10D,[RDX+0x28]` ... `CMP R9D,[RAX]; JNZ; CMP R8D,[RAX+4]; JNZ; MOV [RDX+0xc],ECX; INC ECX; ADD RAX,0x18; CMP ECX,R10D; JL` ... `MOV AL,1; MOV [RDX+0x9c],AL; RET`. Retail VideoDX11 Resize 0x180004340 reads `local_38 + *(int*)(Device+0x10)*8`, the refresh array of the GetDisplayMode copy for Device+0x0c. The port is faithful on both sides.
reachability: OptionsDialog::ApplyVideoSettings (optionsdialog.cpp:1012): any resolution change on the same renderer and adapter calls ApplyChangedSettings, never Device::Startup, so refreshRateIndex keeps the index chosen at boot for the boot mode. The next frame's BeginCommands runs DeviceData_Resize, which reads the new mode's refresh list at that index. Any monitor whose modes have different refresh-rate counts triggers it, for example a high-refresh native mode next to a 60 Hz-only lower mode. The rate the player picked in the Refresh combo is also silently ignored.
proof:
Repro file: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_dx11_swapchain/refresh_index.cpp. Built with `~/fz.sh build dx11sc_refresh_index src/engine/video/device.cpp` and run with -runs=1.

Setup: mode 0 is 2560x1440 with refresh rates {60,120,144,165}; mode 1 is 1280x720 with {60}. Startup's choice is displayModeIndex=0, refreshRateIndex=3. The repro sets cfg fullscreen 1280x720 and calls the real Video::Device::ApplyChangedSettings, then makes the real GetDisplayMode(displayModeIndex) copy and reads rates[refreshRateIndex], as devicedata.cpp:840-841 (Resize) and 454-455 (FillSwapChainDesc) do.

ASan output: `heap-buffer-overflow ... 0x503000000208 is located 16 bytes after 8-byte region` allocated by `GrowFor<RefreshRate>` <- `RtVideo_ArrayRefreshAssign` <- `Video::Device::GetDisplayMode` (device_enum_types.cpp:737). SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow in the rates[rateIndex] read.
root_cause: Device::refreshRateIndex is an index into one specific mode's refresh array, but only Device::Startup sets it. ApplyChangedSettings changes displayModeIndex without re-resolving the refresh index against the new mode, and dx11 indexes the new mode's array with it unchecked.
minimal_fix: In DeviceData_Resize and FillSwapChainDesc, use the index only when `rateIndex >= 0 && rateIndex < mode.refreshCount`. Otherwise use the entry matching cfg->refreshNumerator/Denominator, or entry 0. Better: re-resolve refreshRateIndex in ApplyChangedSettings when it changes displayModeIndex, as Startup's pass 2 does. Under the fix/ext rules this is a fix.* row.

title: GetPathForReferenceId descends the reference tree with UNSIGNED compares; retail and our InsertCore order it SIGNED, so ids >= 0x80000000 are not found
bug_class: signedness divergence (tree ordering mismatch)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800bf1d0 compares with JL/JGE (signed). The port uses `uint32_t id < n->element.id` (unsigned). The port's own InsertCore (reference_set.cpp:391-394) casts to int32 and matches retail 0x18002d1d9 CMP/JL. So port insert and port lookup disagree, while retail's two bodies agree.
reachability: Save load. SerializeReferenceTable reads (id, path) pairs from the save into _references through InsertCore (signed order). Every ExternalPtr in reference mode then resolves its id through GetPathForReferenceId (external_ptr_serialize.cpp:283). A save carrying a reference id with the top bit set alongside small ids resolves to an empty path, so FindOrLoad("") gives a null resource where retail loads the right one. The game itself writes ids 1..N, so this needs a crafted or corrupted save.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail GetPathForReferenceId 0x1800bf1d0:
 1800bf201: MOV EAX,dword ptr [RBX]
 1800bf203: CMP R8D,EAX
 1800bf206: JL 0x1800bf213      ; signed -> left
 1800bf208: CMP EAX,R8D
 1800bf20b: JGE 0x1800bf219     ; signed -> found
 1800bf20d: MOV RBX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x20]
Retail InsertCore 0x18002d1d7: MOV EAX,[RDI]; CMP ECX,EAX; JL; CMP EAX,ECX; JGE (signed, same order).
Port external.cpp:389-390: `if (id < n->element.id) n = n->left; else if (n->element.id < id) n = n->right;` with uint32_t id (External.h:228).
Repro (ASan+UBSan libFuzzer, real rtrefset::Insert + RtObject_ExternalFactory_GetPathForReferenceId): C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_engine_object_ub/refid_signed_lookup.cpp. It inserts ids 1, 2, 0x80000001. Output:
 id 0x00000001 -> "a.rsc"
 id 0x00000002 -> "b.rsc"
 id 0x80000001 -> "(null)"
 LOOKUP MISS: 1 inserted id(s) not found  (abort)
Retail finds all three.
root_cause: The lookup was written with the uint32 field's natural compare. Retail (and the port's insert) use signed 32-bit compares on the same key. The unused helper detail::ReferenceFind (External.h:873) has the same unsigned descent.
minimal_fix: Compare as int32 in GetPathForReferenceId (and in detail::ReferenceFind): `const int32_t k = static_cast<int32_t>(id); const int32_t nk = static_cast<int32_t>(n->element.id); if (k < nk) left; else if (nk < k) right; else found;`.

title: CleanRemovedDialogs caches the _removedDialogs count, where retail re-reads it every iteration, and stores the null through the re-read array base, where retail uses the base loaded before the delete
bug_class: C1/C12 ownership: dialog queued for removal during the drain is dropped (never unlinked or freed)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x18011f790 bounds the loop with `CMP EBP,dword ptr [RDI+0x20]` (it reloads _removedDialogs._size each iteration). The port reads `const int32_t removedCount = _removedDialogs._size;` once.
reachability: Latent. It needs a destructor run from CleanRemovedDialogs that closes a dialog not already in _removedDialogs. The only such destructor in src/ is ~ComboElement, and its drop-down is normally the dying dialog's own child, so it is already queued (see the first finding). An exe dialog or controller destructor that closes another dialog would trigger it. None was found in src/game.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x18011f790: `18011f7bb CMP dword ptr [RCX+0x20],R15D ; JLE ...` (entry) ... `18011f920 MOV RBX,qword ptr [RDI+0x18] ; 18011f924 MOV RAX,[RBX+R14] ; ... 18011f93d MOV RAX,[RAX] ; MOV EDX,1 ; CALL [RAX] ; 18011f947 MOV qword ptr [RBX+R14],R15 ; 18011f94b INC EBP ; ADD R14,8 ; 18011f951 CMP EBP,dword ptr [RDI+0x20] ; JL 0x18011f7d0 ; ... JMP 0x180079c90`. Port, userinterface.cpp:1001-1033: `const int32_t removedCount = _removedDialogs._size; for (int32_t i = 0; i < removedCount; ++i) { ... delete dlg; _removedDialogs._data[i] = nullptr; } _removedDialogs._size = 0;`. There are two differences. (a) If a deleted dialog's destructor chain calls CloseDialog on a live dialog (~ComboElement does that for its open drop-down), PushRemovedUnlessPresent appends at index >= removedCount. Retail processes that entry in the same loop: it unlinks it from _dialogs, drops its events and deletes it. The port never visits it, then sets _size = 0. The dialog has already had OnClosed run and been unlinked from its parent, but it stays linked in _dialogs and is never freed. It keeps being updated and drawn, and its back-pointers (such as ComboDialog::_combo) point into the freed dialog. That is a leak plus a stale live dialog. (b) Retail writes the null slot through RBX, the array base loaded before the delete. The port re-reads _data after the delete. If the push in (a) reallocated the array, retail writes into the freed old buffer (a retail UAF write), and the port writes into the new one. The port's own banner comment ('RE-READ ... the re-read is free and keeps this body honest against retail's own instruction order') is wrong on both counts.
root_cause: The loop bound was hoisted out of the loop in the port (the comment claims nothing inside moves the array, which is false once a destructor pushes onto it). The null store re-reads the base instead of using the pre-delete base retail used.
minimal_fix: Match retail at this site: `for (int32_t i = 0; i < _removedDialogs._size; ++i)`. Keep the post-delete re-read of _data for the null store and record it as a deliberate deviation, because retail's store through the stale base is a write into freed memory once the array grows.

title: CompleteTask's factory ctor sets taskIndex to 0; retail sets the 'unresolved' sentinel 0x7FFFFFFF, so a version-0 CompleteTask loaded from a save completes or reassigns scheduler task 0
bug_class: C2/C5 wrong default state (port-only ctor value replacing a retail store)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail factory 0x140021fc0 stores the qword 0x7fffffff at +0x30 (taskIndex = 0x7FFFFFFF, taskParam = 0). The port's CompleteTask() initialises taskIndex(0), and CreateNewObject / CreateInPlaceObject build the object with that ctor. The comment at completetask.cpp:157 ('The tree's factory zeroed every field above +0x10; kept') assumed retail zero-fills too. For CompleteTask it does not; the other eleven 'zeroed' Action factories do zero-fill (checked).
reachability: Loading a save whose CompleteTask action block was written at Serializer version 0 (older Banished builds; retail keeps the version-0 read arm on purpose). The action is in a citizen's action stack, so it is restored by every save load that contains a citizen mid-task.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail CompleteTask create factory 0x140021fc0:
  140021ffe: XOR EAX,EAX
  140022000: MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x10],RAX
  140022004: MOV byte ptr [RBX + 0x18],AL
  140022007: LEA RCX,[0x14015fbd0]          ; CompleteTask vtable
  14002200e: MOV qword ptr [RBX],RCX
  140022011: MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x20],RAX ; workEntity = 0
  140022015: MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x28],RAX ; targetEntity = 0
  140022019: MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x30],0x7fffffff ; taskIndex = 0x7FFFFFFF, taskParam = 0
Port (completetask.cpp:159-163):
  CompleteTask::CompleteTask() : workEntity(nullptr), targetEntity(nullptr), taskIndex(0), taskParam(0) {}
The value matters. Retail CompleteTask::Persist 0x1400c5be0 (port completetask.cpp:66-69) reads taskIndex only when ser.GetVersion() > 0. The Serializer's version on read is the version stored in the stream (BinaryReader), so a version-0 record keeps the factory value. Retail AbstractImpl 0x1400c5b40 then does `if ([+0x30] == 0x7fffffff) [+0x30] = citizen[+0x30]; if (-1 < [+0x30]) TryCompleteTask(...)`, and the port has the same logic (completetask.cpp:86-103, CheckEntity :122-129). In retail the version-0 record resolves its task lazily from the citizen. In the port it keeps 0: TryCompleteTask(task 0) / TaskCleanup(0) on completion, and TaskReassign(task 0) on CheckEntity.
root_cause: The B.3.8 ctor rewrite kept the tree's zero-fill for the default ctor instead of the retail factory's inlined stores. CompleteTask is the one Action factory with a non-zero store above +0x18, and it was missed.
minimal_fix: In completetask.cpp, initialise taskIndex(0x7FFFFFFF) in CompleteTask::CompleteTask() (retail 0x140022019), and correct the comment at line 157 to say that retail stores +0x30 = 0x7FFFFFFF.

title: BuildPathGraph stores pairs as {entityCell, buildingCell}; retail stores {max(cell), min(cell)}, so ProcessPaths calls PathDistance with the arguments swapped
bug_class: C5 wrong element order
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400d73d3..0x1400d73e7 orders the two CELL indices by size before the append. The port appends them unordered. git log -L shows the unordered form since the first port (43eeda0ec).
reachability: Every path-graph rebuild (every 300 s of game time) for each (worker-entity, residence) pair where entityCell < buildingCell.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400d70c0:
1400d732a: MOVSXD R11,EAX                 ; entityCell = GetAnchorCell(...)
1400d7363: MOVSXD R10,dword ptr [R15]     ; buildingCell
1400d73d3: MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x7f],R11D   ; pair.a = entityCell
1400d73d7: MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x83],R10D   ; pair.b = buildingCell
1400d73de: CMP R11D,R10D
1400d73e1: JGE 0x1400d73ee
1400d73e3: MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x7f],R10D   ; swap -> {max, min}
1400d73e7: MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x83],R11D
...
1400d7469: LEA RAX,[RBP + 0x7f]           ; the appended element is this qword
1400d7474: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX]
1400d7477: MOV qword ptr [R10],RAX
Port citizenbehavior.cpp:542:
    PathCellPair pairData = { entityCell, buildingCell };   // no max/min ordering
ProcessPaths (0x1400d6f00, port :313-319) then calls map->PathDistance(pairs[idx].cellA, pairs[idx].cellB, 0). The region key is sorted in both, but the cell order passed to PathDistance is not.
root_cause: The port skipped the cell-order normalisation that retail applies to the pair before Array::Add. PathDistance (0x14009f810) passes (regionA, regionB) to RegionGraph::PathLength (0x1400a8ba0), and PathLength runs the region A* (0x14001dc00) from start toward goal, summing truncated centroid distances along the path it finds. A search in the opposite direction can settle on a different equal-cost region path, so the int sum, and with it the cost stored for the region pair and used by AssignCitizens, can differ from retail. Each pair's PathLength run also starts from a different region than retail's.
minimal_fix: Before the append: `PathCellPair pairData = entityCell < buildingCell ? PathCellPair{buildingCell, entityCell} : PathCellPair{entityCell, buildingCell};`

label: port

reachability: Normal play: any slot-9 Update that spawns an entity of the same category while the cursor is near the end of that bucket (forest spread, wildlife population, pasture births, spawners).
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400c4090 bucket loop:
1400c4170: MOVSXD RAX,dword ptr [R13 + 0x8]   ; count, read ONCE per bucket
1400c4188: MOV RDI,RAX
1400c418b: MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],RAX
...
1400c42d8: MOV RDI,qword ptr [RSP + 0x20]    ; restored after the component ticks
1400c4302: INC RSI
1400c4305: INC R14D
1400c4308: INC R15D
1400c430e: CMP RSI,RDI                        ; wrap test against the STALE count
1400c4311: JL 0x1400c4319
1400c4313: MOV R14D,R8D                       ; cursor = 0
1400c4316: MOV ESI,R8D                        ; idx = 0
1400c4319: CMP RSI,RBP
Port entitylist.cpp:971-976:
    // Re-read count (array may have changed size)
    count = bkt->_size;
    if ((int64_t)idx >= count) { idx = 0; cursorVal = 0; }
RegisterEntity (0x1400c48a0, componententity.cpp:705) appends straight to buckets[category]. It is called from component Update bodies that run inside this loop (growthcomponent.cpp:270, populationcomponent.cpp:373, herdcomponent.cpp:312/493, pasturecomponent_spawn.cpp:193/339, spawncomponent.cpp:293 ...), so the bucket can grow mid-loop.
root_cause: The port treats the bucket count as live and lets the walk run into entries appended during this pass. Retail wraps at the old end. Worked example: count 100, processCount 2, cursor 99. A tick of entity 99 appends entity 100. Retail ticks 99, wraps, ticks 0, and saves cursor 1. The port ticks 99, visits 100 (delta 0, so nothing runs), wraps, and saves cursor 0. Entity 0's Update is skipped this frame and later runs with a bigger delta, and the saved cursor[] (serialized by EntityList::Serialize) differs from retail's from then on.
minimal_fix: Read `int32_t count = bkt->_size;` once per bucket and delete the `count = bkt->_size;` re-read at line 972 (keep the per-iteration re-read of `bkt->_data`, which retail also does).
also: Bucket round-robin wraps at the re-read bucket size; retail wraps at the count captured before the loop (tick schedule diverges when an Update registers an entity into the same bucket)

title: Serialize writes an entity's bucket index zero-extended (SHR); retail sign-extends it (SAR), so every category-6 entity saves 0x00FFFFFF where retail saves 0xFFFFFFFF
bug_class: integer sign/width divergence (shift)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400c462c-0x1400c4635 is MOV ECX,[RAX+0x1c]; SHL ECX,8; SAR ECX,8, an arithmetic shift on the signed dword. The port shifts the uint32_t _handle, which is a logical shift. RemoveEntity has the same SHR-vs-SAR difference at line 1424 (retail 0x1400c3934 SHL EBP,8 / 0x1400c3937 SAR EBP,8, then MOVSXD RCX,EBP).
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail EntityList::Serialize 0x1400c44a0:
1400c4629: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX]
1400c462c: MOV ECX,dword ptr [RAX + 0x1c]
1400c462f: SHL ECX,0x8
1400c4632: SAR ECX,0x8
1400c4635: MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x38],ECX
1400c4663: XOR R8D,R8D
1400c4666: LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x38]
1400c466e: CALL qword ptr [0x140152ac8]   ; Serializer::Serialize(int&)
Port line 1611:
  int32_t bucketIdxField = static_cast<int32_t>((masterArray._data[entityIdx]->_handle << 8) >> 8);   // _handle is uint32_t -> SHR
RegisterEntity with category 6 sets the low 24 bits to 0xFFFFFF (componententity.cpp:694, `_handle |= 0xFFFFFF`). For each such entity retail writes the int -1 (FF FF FF FF) and the port writes 16777215 (FF FF FF 00). Saves written by the port therefore differ byte-for-byte from retail's for every no-bucket entity. Load is unaffected, because both mask with 0xFFFFFF. A port-to-port resave gate cannot see the difference. In RemoveEntity the same zero-extension makes `bucketData[entityBucketIdx]` and `bucketData[lastIdx]` (with lastIdx a uint32_t) index +4G elements, where retail indexes a negative element. That only happens for out-of-range values (see the save-trust finding).
root_cause: _handle was typed uint32_t, so the port's `(x << 8) >> 8` became a logical shift. Retail's `(int << 8) >> 8` sign-extends the 24-bit bucket index.
minimal_fix: Sign-extend as retail does. At line 1611: `int32_t bucketIdxField = static_cast<int32_t>(masterArray._data[entityIdx]->_handle << 8) >> 8;`. At line 1424 the same, using `int32_t entityBucketIdx` and an int32_t lastIdx, so indexing matches retail's MOVSXD.

1400ff451: LEA R9,[RSP+0x50]      ; max
1400ff456: LEA R8,[RSP+0x40]      ; min
1400ff45b: LEA RDX,[RSP+0x60]     ; out
1400ff460: LEA RCX,[RSP+0x30]     ; this = target (x,y,z)
1400ff465: MOV dword ptr [RSP+0x58],R12D   ; max.z = 0 (R12 == 0, see CMP [RDI+0xa4],R12B / JZ)
1400ff46a: MOVSS [RSP+0x50],XMM0 ; max.x = h
1400ff470: MOVSS [RSP+0x54],XMM0 ; max.y = h
1400ff476: XORPS XMM0,[0x1401722c0] ; -h

1400ff48e: CALL [0x140152910]   ; Math::Vector3::Clamp
1400ff4a9..4ae: target.z = result.z (0)
The port clamps only x and y (camera_input.cpp:271-272):
    pc->target.x = clampf(pc->target.x, -halfExtent, halfExtent);
    pc->target.y = clampf(pc->target.y, -halfExtent, halfExtent);
and leaves target.z alone. title: MusicPlayer track list is loaded lazily behind a process-wide one-shot static; every game after the first in a session has no music
bug_class: C2 port-only state (one-shot static replacing a per-Load retail find)
label: port
reachability: Play one game, quit to the main menu, then start a new game or load a save in the same process. In-game music never plays again.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail GameUpdateLoop::Load 0x140096b00 finds the track list on every Load, for each new MusicPlayer (0x18 bytes):
1400972a6: LEA ECX,[RDX+0x14] / CALL [0x140152b60]   ; MemAlloc MusicPlayer
1400972bb: LEA RDX,[0x14015e4a8]                      ; "Game/MusicTracks.rsc" (bytes 47616d652f4d75736963547261636b732e727363)
1400972c6: CALL [0x1401516f8]                          ; Filename ctor
1400972eb: MOV RCX,[R15+0x8]
1400972ef: CALL [0x140152160]                          ; resource Find
140097307: CALL [0x140152a98]                          ; IsDerivedFrom MusicList
14009731b: MOV dword ptr [RBX],0xffffffff
140097321: MOV qword ptr [RBX+0x8],RCX                 ; trackList = found list
14009732e: MOV qword ptr [R15+0x80],RBX
The port's Load (gameupdateloop_load.cpp:1003) stores `player->trackList = nullptr; // DEFERRED`. MusicPlayer::Update then calls EnsureTrackList:
    if (mp->trackList) return;
    static bool attempted = false;
    if (attempted) return;   // one shot
    attempted = true;
and then `if (!trackList) return;` (line 176).
root_cause: The deferred Find is gated by a function-local static that survives across games. Each later GameUpdateLoop::Load allocates a new MusicPlayer with trackList null, EnsureTrackList returns at `attempted`, and Update returns before choosing a track.

title: EditTool::Update keeps a dead-pointer range probe and a null-controller bail that retail 0x1400fcda0 does not have
bug_class: C6 port-only guard that skips retail behaviour
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400fcda0 reads the ToolUI controller's pin byte (+0x40) with no null test and has no address-range test. Row 692 removed the same range probe from CloseInfoDialog (0x1400fcc90) only; the copy in Update (0x1400fcda0) is still there. The site's own comment says 'Retail always has both controllers' and 'this guard never triggers' in retail.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400fcda0 decompile: `if (*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x28) != 0) { ...GetController(ToolUI)... (*fn_InternalBasePtr_Ctor)(&local_48,ptr); ...GetController(EntityUI)... (*fn_InternalBasePtr_CheckPtr_slot)(&local_48); if (*(char *)(local_48 + 0x40) == '\0') { ... PlayerScreenRect_EntityRect ...; if (cVar5 == '\0') { EditTool_Deselect_CloseInfoDialog(param_1); return; } ...` The only test is the +0x28 null test. There is no range test on +0x28, and local_48 (the ToolUI controller) is dereferenced at +0x40 untested. Port edittool.cpp:252-261: `if (resolved < 0x10000 || resolved > 0x00007FFFFFFFFFFFULL) { entityRef = nullptr; lastEntityRef = nullptr; return; }`. It also subtracts dialogWidth/dialogHeight, which are in the same space as the screen rect (retail divides (rectX - w/2) by _uiScale), from screenW/uiScale, a layout-unit bound.     if (targetX < 0 || targetX >= cMapSize) {

1400eb2a4: ADD R13D,R14D                  ; x = col + rx
1400eb2a7: ADD ECX,EAX                    ; y = row + ry
1400eb2b6: CMP EAX,dword ptr [RBP + -0x50]
1400eb2b9: JG 0x1400eb280                 ; outside radius -> retry
1400eb2be: TEST R13D,R13D

label: port
reachability: Every planting tick on a crop field whose claimed-cell count equals the cached max.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail PlantArea::Execute 0x1400f4010:
1400f405b: MOV EDI,dword ptr [R15 + 0x50]   ; _cells._count
1400f406d: CMP dword ptr [RBX + 0x30],0x0
1400f4076: CALL 0x14012e5c0
1400f407b: MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0x30],EAX
1400f407e: CMP EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0x30]
1400f4081: JLE 0x1400f4096                  ; count <= max -> continue
1400f4083: MOV EAX,0x1
Port plantarea.cpp:124: `if (treeCount >= workComp->workState) { return 1; }`.
root_cause: Off-by-one compare kept since the first reimplementation. Retail allows one more claimed cell or worker before declining.
minimal_fix: `if (treeCount > workComp->workState) return 1;`

title: PlantArea::Execute packs paired index i+1 for a single-cell plant where retail packs the field size; OnCancel then re-offers and unclaims the neighbouring cell
bug_class: C5 wrong element / C3 state value mismatch (faithfulness drift)
label: port
reachability: Every single-cell planting assignment: the last slot of a field, or a slot whose neighbour i+1 is already planted (validity 0) or claimed by another farmer. A cancel (the farmer is reassigned, the job is interrupted, the field state changes) then runs OnCancel with paired = i+1 < size.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail PlantArea::Execute 0x1400f4010, pairing test and the unpaired arm:
1400f41ad: LEA EBX,[RDI + 0x1]        ; candidate pair = i+1
1400f41b0: CMP EBX,R8D                ; R8D = [R15+0x60] = slot count
1400f41b3: JGE 0x1400f41e0
1400f41b5: CMP byte ptr [R12 + R9*0x1 + 0x1],0x0
1400f41bb: JZ 0x1400f41e0
...
1400f41e0: XOR SIL,SIL                ; not paired
1400f41e3: MOV EBX,R8D                ; paired index := slot COUNT
...
1400f42ed: MOV dword ptr [RBP + -0x25],EBX   ; packedCells[1]
1400f434f: MOV ECX,EBX
1400f4356: SHL ECX,0x10
1400f435f: OR ECX,EDI                 ; packed = EBX<<16 | i
1400f437a: MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x38],ECX
Port (plantarea.cpp:166, 225-226, 238): `int pairedIdx = i + 1;` is never reset when !pairedAvailable, so `packedCells[1] = pairedIdx` and `packedCellInfo = (pairedIdx << 16) | i` carry i+1. Retail OnCancel 0x1400f3ea0 and OnComplete 0x1400f3f60 act on the high word only `if ((int)paired < [this+0x60])`, which is never true for retail's unpaired packing. HarvestArea (harvestarea.cpp:282-284, `cellIdx2 = fieldCellCount`) already has retail's shape; PlantArea lost it.
root_cause: The port computes pairedIdx = i+1 up front and does not replace it with the field size on the unpaired path, as retail's `MOV EBX,R8D` does. OnCancel therefore sets validity[i+1] = 1 and removes cell i+1 from the claim set; OnComplete removes it from the set. Effects: a cell that is already planted is offered for planting again (the 'tile already holds an entity' replant loop seen before with the slot 6/7 swap), and another farmer's in-flight claim on i+1 is dropped, so two farmers can be sent to the same cell.
minimal_fix: In PlantArea::Execute, when !pairedAvailable set pairedIdx = fieldCellCount (retail 0x1400f41e3 MOV EBX,R8D) before building packedCells and packedCellInfo, as HarvestArea does with cellIdx2 = fieldCellCount.

title: TendArea::Execute worker cap uses >= where retail uses > (one tender fewer than retail)
bug_class: C6 port-only cap / off-by-one compare (faithfulness drift)
label: port
reachability: Every tending tick on a crop field or orchard whose tender count has reached WorkComponent+0x30.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail TendArea::Execute 0x1400f5490:
1400f54c2: MOV R14D,dword ptr [RSI + 0x50]   ; _citizens._count
1400f54d4: CMP dword ptr [RBX + 0x30],0x0
1400f54dd: CALL 0x14012e5c0                 ; CalcMaxWorkers
1400f54e2: MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0x30],EAX
1400f54ed: CMP R14D,dword ptr [RBX + 0x30]
1400f54f1: JLE 0x1400f54fd                  ; count <= max -> assign
1400f54f3: MOV EAX,0x1                      ; only count > max returns 1

root_cause: The compare was written as >= in the first reimplementation (7e1d2b80a) and carried through every later pass. Retail proceeds when count == max, so it admits max+1 concurrent tenders; the port stops at max.
minimal_fix: `if (currentWorkers > workComp->workState) return 1;`

title: Font lookup caches the FIRST face asked for and answers every later face with it: the DefaultFaces fallback (Arial, Helvetica) never works on Linux, macOS or Android
bug_class: logic: cache keyed on nothing (face argument ignored after the first call)
label: ext
label_evidence: NOT RETAIL (file banner): ext/resources font rasteriser over FreeType. The identical FacePath body is in src/platform/darwin/font_raster_darwin.cpp:126 and src/platform/android/font_raster_android.cpp:71. The Windows twin (font_raster_win.cpp) looks each face up on every call.
reachability: ext.family_tree's SystemGlyphSource (src/ext/family_tree/family_raster.cpp:82-90) tries DefaultFaces() = {kGameFace "FrancophilSans", "Arial", "Helvetica"} in order, and font_provider.cpp:91 calls FaceAvailable(kGameFace). When FrancophilSans.ttf is absent, the first lookup caches 'absent' and every later face is reported absent even when its file is present, so the family tree has no font. When a face is found first, a later call for a different face rasterises the first face's file.
proof:
Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_platform_posix_src_platform_darwin_s_sdl/font_face_cache.cpp, linked against font_raster_posix.cpp.o from libfuzz_tree.a, with 'DejaVu Sans.ttf' placed beside the binary. Output:
direct lookup: file=1 path=/home/uspc/fz/p8_fontcache/DejaVu Sans.ttf family=DejaVu Sans ok=1
FaceAvailable(NoSuchFaceAtAll)=0
FaceAvailable(DejaVu Sans)=0 why='no NoSuchFaceAtAll.ttf (tried ...)'
BUG: an available face is reported absent (cached answer of the first face)
The reason string even names the wrong face.
root_cause: FacePath() guards the lookup with a single process-wide g_lookedUp flag and one g_facePath / g_faceWhy. The face argument is used only on the first call; later calls return the cached result whatever face they name.
minimal_fix: Key the cache by face name, e.g. std::map<std::string, std::pair<std::string, std::string>> under g_lock: look up `face`, and run FindFaceFile + FamilyName only on a miss. Apply the same change in the darwin and android twins.

title: Windows DX11 build creates the game window with SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN: no Vulkan loader means no window and the game does not start, where retail needs only CreateWindowExW
bug_class: platform init dependency / error handling (graphics-API flag mismatched with the backend)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail Application::PlatformStartup 0x18009fc10 makes only IAT calls (RegisterClassW, CreateWindowExW, UpdateWindow, SetCursor) and loads no Vulkan. The port's src/platform/win/window_win.cpp PrepareCreate returns SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN unconditionally, also in the DX11 build, which never makes a Vulkan surface.
reachability: Any Windows machine or session without a Vulkan runtime (vulkan-1.dll), for example some VMs or drivers without Vulkan, running the default DX11 build. The process cannot open its window at boot.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: Runtime-x64.dll 0x18009fc10 call list: `18009fc39: CALL 0x1800cb110 / 18009fc97: CALL [0x18014b4c8] / 18009fcee: CALL [0x18014b4c0] / 18009fd05: CALL 0x1800c5fa0 / 18009fd12: CALL [0x18014b4a8] / 18009fd20: CALL [0x18014b4b0] / 18009fd42: CALL 0x1800c7ad0`. These are user32 window creation calls only; there is no graphics-API dependency. Port: window_sdl.cpp:337 `SDL_CreateWindow(title, width, height, SDL_WINDOW_HIDDEN | platformFlags)`, where window_win.cpp:19 `return SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN;`. third_party/SDL/src/video/SDL_video.c:2514-2521: `if (flags & SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN) { ... if (!SDL_Vulkan_LoadLibrary(NULL)) { return NULL; } }`. Without vulkan-1.dll, Create logs "SDL_CreateWindow failed" and returns nullptr, and Application::PlatformStartup fails. The window_sdl.cpp banner records this ("a machine with D3D11 but no Vulkan runtime now fails at 'failed to create window'"), but it has no docs/known_port_issues.md row.
root_cause: PrepareCreate on Windows always asks SDL for a Vulkan-capable window, whichever render backend is compiled in. SDL_CreateWindow then hard-fails when the Vulkan loader cannot be loaded.
minimal_fix: Return SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN from the Windows PrepareCreate only when the Vulkan backend is built: make it a per-backend constant from the backend's cmake, not an #if in game code. Or, in the DX11 build, retry SDL_CreateWindow without the flag when the first attempt fails. Record a known_port_issues row either way.

title: LazyTable::Sweep still gives objects back after Pause() returned (the device going away); the paused check runs only once, before the gate wait
bug_class: device-lost / pause race (check-then-act)
label: ext
reachability: ext.create_on_demand with idle_min > 0, and a device-lost recovery, device rebuild or exit while worker 0's sweep waits for a use to leave the gate. On DX11 the late Release is COM-safe, so the impact is a contract violation plus Release/DropBuffer calls racing Shutdown's ShareGpuData::Clear and device teardown. On a backend whose objects may not outlive the device it would be use-after-destroy.
proof: Standalone repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_common_swapchain/sweep_after_pause.cpp, linked with the real lazy_table.cpp and use_tracker.cpp and built with clang++-19 -fsanitize=address,undefined on WSL. It prints 'evictions after Pause() returned: 1'. Sequence: a made record idle past the limit; a use holds the gate (Enter); a thread runs Sweep(), which reads _paused==false, collects the candidate and blocks in _gate.Close(); the main thread calls Pause(), which returns at once because _running==0 (the DeviceData::Shutdown order: Pause, then ShareGpuData::Clear, then the device and context are released); the use Leaves; Sweep takes _mutex and calls Record::Evict without checking _paused again. Code: 'idle = _paused ? 0 : _idleEpochs;' is evaluated in the first locked block only, and the eviction loop under the second lock has no _paused test. This contradicts the contract in CREATEONDEMAND.md section 7: 'A sweep during a pause gives nothing back.'
root_cause: Pause() waits only for running materializations (_running). An eviction in progress is not counted, and Sweep checks _paused before the potentially long Close() wait instead of after it.
minimal_fix: In Sweep's eviction block (under _mutex, after _gate.Close()), add 'if (_paused) { _gate.Open(); return 0; }' before the loop. Or count the sweep in _running, or a separate counter that Pause() waits on, so Pause cannot return while an eviction is pending.

title: LazyTable::Sweep can evict after Pause() has returned: _paused is read once before the gate wait, and Pause does not wait for a sweep that is in flight
bug_class: GPU resource lifetime / TOCTOU between device teardown and deferred eviction
label: ext
label_evidence: lazy_table.cpp is 'NOT RETAIL' ext.create_on_demand code (header banner), with no retail counterpart.
reachability: Worker 0 runs Sweep once a minute whenever ext.create_on_demand is on with idleMinutes>0. Any DeviceData::Shutdown (exit, the device-lost RecoverLostDevice on DX11/Vulkan/Metal) that overlaps a sweep waiting in the gate hits the window. The gate wait lasts as long as any thread is inside a companion slot (Bind/Lock/SetData/Read, including an on-use Materialize), which widens the window.
proof:
Repro: C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_common_gpu_lifetime/sweep_after_pause.cpp, built with ~/fz.sh build rc_lt_sweep_after_pause against the real lazy_table.cpp and use_tracker.cpp in libfuzz_tree.a (ASan+UBSan).

Sequence:
1. Add, then Ensure: the record is made at epoch 1.
2. SetIdleLimit(1, 0ms), then Sweep(): epoch 2, not idle yet.
3. The main thread calls Enter(), standing in for a draw inside a companion slot.
4. A thread runs Sweep() for epoch 3. It reads _paused==false at line 397, collects obj as a candidate, and spins in _gate.Close().
5. The main thread calls Pause(). It returns at once, because it waits only for _running==0.
6. The main thread then deletes the fake device (the backend's DeviceData::Shutdown), then calls Leave().
7. The sweep goes on: at lines 422-428 it takes _mutex and calls e.record->Evict() without rechecking _paused.

ASan output: 'Pause() returned; destroying the device' followed by 'AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... sweep_after_pause.cpp:21:29 in Rec::Evict()' (Evict touches the destroyed device).
root_cause:
Sweep samples `idle = _paused ? 0 : _idleEpochs` under _mutex at line 397. It then drops the lock, waits for in-flight uses in _gate.Close(), which can take any length of time, and retakes _mutex for the eviction loop at line 422 without looking at _paused again. Pause() (lines 477-482) sets _paused and waits only for _running==0, which counts materializations and not an in-flight sweep. The header promises that Pause is 'the device going away', after which backends tear down (dx11 devicedata.cpp:1048, vulkan device.cpp:1218 then ResourcesShutdown / vkDestroyDevice, metal backend.mm:992). A sweep that started before Pause can therefore still run Record::Evict on handles of a device that is being or has been destroyed.

The shipped Evicts are latent today. Vulkan's only pushes a RetireBuffer closure: g_retired is swapped out by ResourcesShutdown, and DestroyBufferNow later looks the handle up in g_liveBuffers, so a recycled non-dispatchable handle value could destroy a new device's buffer. DX11 and Metal Release refcounted objects. OnVideoError normally Forgets every companion first. Any backend Evict that touches the device turns this into a use-after-free.

title: Dxbc::ParseProgram customdata length wraps `at + in.length` (uint32), so the parser loops forever and grows instrs until OOM
bug_class: 32-bit offset overflow in a length check (hang / unbounded allocation)
label: ext
label_evidence: dxbc.h: 'NOT RETAIL. ... parses whatever blob it is handed (the user's installed shaders, at run time)'. Retail hands byte code to D3D unparsed.
reachability: Every shader blob goes through it while a DXBC rewrite row is on: SmokeVs::Analyse on every vertex program variant (src/render/dx11/draw_batch/smoke_vs_stage.cpp:88), FaaRewrite::Analyse (dx11 foliage_aa_stage.cpp:209, vulkan shader_rewrites.cpp:239), and natural_growth / edge_dither / receiver_rewrite Analyse. A shader resource (for example from a mod) whose SHDR contains a customdata token (opcode 53) at dword at>0 with length word 2^32-at+k (k <= n) makes the check pass and moves `at` backwards. With k <= at the loop re-reaches the same customdata forever.
proof:
Repro C:/Users/USPC/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/f1762c107073ce1b/9ab6db73-5aa8-4544-a435-76b2cbc4daf1/scratchpad/p8/src_render_common_layout/dxbc_customdata_wrap.cpp. The SHDR is {0x40 ps_4_0, 5, nop len1, 53 customdata, 0xFFFFFFFF}; the call is ParseProgram. At at=1, length=0xFFFFFFFF gives 1+0xFFFFFFFF = 0 <= n, so the check passes; then at += length gives 0, and the loop restarts. libFuzzer (fz.sh run rc_layout_dxbcwrap):
==805== ERROR: libFuzzer: out-of-memory (malloc(3221225472))
    #8 std::__new_allocator<Dxbc::Instr>::allocate ...
(instrs.push_back in the endless ParseProgram loop)
root_cause: `in.length = t[at + 1]` is an unbounded 32-bit value from the blob, and `if (in.length == 0 || at + in.length > n)` is evaluated in uint32_t, so it wraps. `at += length` (line 266) then wraps too, so the parser makes no forward progress.
minimal_fix: Test without overflow: `if (in.length == 0 || in.length > n - at)`. Equivalently, compute in uint64_t: `static_cast<uint64_t>(at) + in.length > n`.

title: EventNotifyDialog_RemoveEntry destroys only the removed entry's String, so every later entry's String is copy-constructed over a live String and the last slot is never released (refcount leak on every ribbon expiry)
bug_class: refcount imbalance / lifetime (C1-family ownership)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x140011670 calls ~String (CALL [0x140152af0] at 0x1400116c7) at the top of every loop iteration for slots removeIndex..count-1, and only then copy-constructs slot i from slot i+1 (CALL [0x140151428] at 0x140011712). The last slot is destroyed and not rebuilt. The port calls ~String once, before the loop.
reachability: Every game session. EventNotifyDialog::OnUpdate (0x140067c30) calls RemoveEntry each time a shown ribbon notification's timer runs out (eventnotifydialog.cpp:193-194). Each expiry with n entries shown leaks n-1-removeIndex String buffers, for the life of the process.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF + RUN. Retail 0x140011670:
1400116b0: MOVSXD RAX,ESI
1400116b3: LEA RCX,[RAX + RAX*0x2] ; SHL RCX,0x4 ; ADD RCX,[RBX]
1400116c3: ADD RCX,0x20
1400116c7: CALL qword ptr [0x140152af0]   ; ~String(slot i)  <- inside the loop
1400116cd: INC ESI
1400116cf: CMP ESI,dword ptr [RBX + 0x8] ; JGE 0x140011721
...
14001170e: LEA RCX,[RDI + 0x20]
140011712: CALL qword ptr [0x140151428]   ; String(const String&) slot i <- slot i+1
140011725: CMP ESI,dword ptr [RBX + 0x8]
140011728: JL 0x1400116b0                   ; back to the ~String
Port (eventnotifydialog.cpp:109-118): `entries._data[removeIndex].text.~String();` once, then `for (i = removeIndex+1; i < count; i++) { ... new (&dst.text) System::String(src.text); }`. Slots removeIndex+1..count-2 are overwritten without a destructor, and slot count-1 is never destroyed.
Repro run (WSL, clang-19, ASan+UBSan, the real static function via #include of the TU): scratchpad/p8/src_game_Dialog_lifetime/evnotify_remove.cpp builds 3 entries and calls EventNotifyDialog_RemoveEntry(entries, 0). Output: `after removing [0] of 3: size=2 refcount(second)=2 refcount(third)=2 (each has ONE live holder)` followed by `REFCOUNT IMBALANCE: string buffers leak` (abort by the repro's check). Retail's sequence leaves both at 1.
root_cause: The transcription moved retail's per-iteration ~String out of the loop, so its comment 'kept exactly' is wrong. The copy-construct is retail's, but retail destroys each destination slot just before it builds it, and destroys the vacated last slot.
minimal_fix: Match 0x140011670: for (int i = removeIndex; i < count; ++i) { entries._data[i].text.~String(); if (i + 1 < count) { copy timer/eventIndex/icon/color from [i+1]; new (&entries._data[i].text) System::String(entries._data[i+1].text); } } then entries._size = count - 1.

title: The video-interface sentinel module takes one reference but is stored in two slots and released twice at Engine shutdown (cleanup runs twice)
bug_class: cleanup runs twice (refcount over-release)
label: ext
label_evidence: SentinelModule and the cutover DX9 placeholder exist only in OpenBA. Retail LoadLibraryW's each plugin once per slot, so its per-slot FreeLibrary at Shutdown (0x1800db5e8) is balanced.
reachability: Every boot, with the release at every clean Engine shutdown. Today it has no visible effect because both OSes pin the main executable.
proof: SentinelModule() caches one LoadLibraryW(self) (Windows) or dlopen(nullptr) (POSIX). Video::Device::InitializeInterfaces (src/platform/win/video_interfaces_win.cpp:225/276, src/platform/posix/video_interfaces_posix.cpp:64/74) stores it in dllSlots[1] (FillDx11Slot) and dllSlots[0] (FillDx9Placeholder). Engine shutdown then calls Platform::ReleaseLibrary on every non-null slot (src/engine/engine/engine_lifecycle.cpp:765 and src/game/Game/game_main.cpp:219), which is 2 releases for 1 reference. Repros: scratchpad/p8/src_app_errors/sentinel_release.cpp (WSL, clang++-19 ASan+UBSan) printed 'dlclose(0x78403d6712e0) = 0' twice. scratchpad/p8/src_app_errors/sentinel_win.cpp (WinLibs g++) printed FreeLibrary -> 1 four times with the exe still mapped. Neither OS shows a visible effect today, because the main image is pinned and never unloaded. The pairing that the comment at video_interface.cpp:76-79 claims ('an extra reference taken for the purpose') does not hold.
root_cause: The function-local static caches the handle, so the second fill takes no new reference, while the engine shutdown body faithfully releases each populated slot.
minimal_fix: Take one reference per fill: drop the static cache and call LoadLibraryW(self) / dlopen(nullptr) in each of FillDx11Slot and FillDx9Placeholder. Alternatively, have SentinelModule() add a reference on every call (LoadLibraryW again, or dlopen again).

title: CitizenComponent::ShowTool / HideTool carry port-only guards: a GameUpdateLoop::_singleton test around Scene::AddObject/RemoveObject and a null-mesh test before GetNodeIndexFromName
bug_class: C6 port-only guard that skips retail behaviour
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1401173b0 calls GraphicsMesh::GetNodeIndexFromName(model->meshInstance._mesh, "tool") with no null test. It then calls Scene::AddObject([g_pGameWorldSingleton]+0x60) and stores +0x1d8/+0x1dc unconditionally. Retail HideTool 0x1401176e0 calls Scene::RemoveObject on [0x1401c3dd8]+0x60 with no test. None of these guards carries a retail-address justification.
reachability: Inert in normal play: the singleton and the model mesh are always present when a citizen shows a tool. It only changes behaviour where retail would crash (no world, or a model with no mesh), and there it hides the upstream fault the project rules require surfacing.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail HideTool 0x1401176e0:
  140117738: CALL qword ptr [0x140152978]   ; Geometry::Detach
  14011773e: MOV RCX,qword ptr [0x1401c3dd8] ; g_pGameWorldSingleton, no test
  140117745: MOV EDX,dword ptr [RDI + 0x1dc]
  14011774b: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x60]
  14011774f: CALL qword ptr [0x140151360]   ; Scene::RemoveObject
  14011775a: MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x1d8],-0x1
Retail ShowTool 0x1401173b0 (decompile): `this = *(GraphicsMesh**)(model+0xe8); iVar6 = GetNodeIndexFromName(this,"tool"); Attach(...); ...; uVar7 = Scene::AddObject(*(Scene**)(g_pGameWorldSingleton+0x60), tool); [+0x1d8] = toolId; [+0x1dc] = uVar7;` with no conditionals.
Port: action_base_complete.cpp HideTool `if (GameUpdateLoop::_singleton) { scene->RemoveObject(...) }`. ShowTool has `int nodeIdx = graphicsMesh ? graphicsMesh->GetNodeIndexFromName("tool") : -1;` and `if (GameUpdateLoop::_singleton) { AddObject; this->toolId = toolId; toolSceneId = objId; }`. When the singleton test fails, the port also skips recording toolId/toolSceneId, which retail always writes.
root_cause: Standalone-era defensive tests, left in place when the B6 guard sweep removed the ShowTool call-site guards (G73/G74).
minimal_fix: Remove the three tests so the calls run unconditionally as in retail: AddObject plus the toolId/toolSceneId stores in ShowTool, RemoveObject in HideTool, and GetNodeIndexFromName called on the mesh as is.

title: StorageDisplayComponent slot 9 (Update) runs the slot-6 layout (OnAdded) before Refresh every tick; retail slot 9 is Refresh alone
bug_class: port divergence: wrong slot body (C4 shape, found during the lifetime sweep; outside the assigned class)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail vtable slot 9 0x1400566a0 is a single `JMP 0x1400563e0` (Refresh). The port's Update calls StorageDisplayComponent::OnAdded() (retail slot 6, 0x140056730) and then Refresh(). The extra call has no retail counterpart.
reachability: Every tick of every storage-yard or stockpile entity in a running game. The visible result should match retail because the layout is idempotent for a fixed footprint. The cost is per-tick terrain queries and scene transform writes that retail does not make. Each tick also runs an Array<Pile>::SetSize on an array whose elements the scene holds by address (AddObject(&pile.mesh)). That call copies and frees the elements if the footprint size ever changes while meshes are registered; no reachable trigger was found.
root_cause: The port's slot-9 body was written as 'Draw + Refresh', which is the shape of slot 11 (0x140056940). It is not the retail slot 9, which jumps straight to Refresh.
minimal_fix: Make StorageDisplayComponent::Update call Refresh() only, as retail 0x1400566a0 does. The layout stays with slot 6 (OnAdded) and slot 11 (Slot11), as in retail.

title: ToolUI::OnUpdate keeps a port-only per-frame pinOnDrag = 1 stand-in, now that EntityUI slot 8 (0x140066ad0) is wired and does the same
bug_class: C2 port-only state write / stale stand-in
label: port

title: ForceVideoContextReset (WM_ACTIVATE observer) resets Video::Context on the main thread while ext.render_pipe's render thread emits with it
bug_class: data race: context reset off the emitting thread
label: ext
label_evidence: WndMsgObserver / ForceVideoContextReset are NOT RETAIL focus diagnostics in main.cpp (installed by Init step 8). Retail had no render thread, so the race needs ext.render_pipe.
reachability: DX11 exclusive fullscreen (the default on first run) + ext.render_pipe on + its overlap governor engaged (desktop at high speed or a heavy town) + alt-tab back to the game during an overlapped frame.
proof: main.cpp:652-662: ForceVideoContextReset does ml->_contextDirty = 0; ctx->Reset(); and Context::Reset (src/engine/video/context.cpp:480) memsets several thousand bytes of the Context (+0x208.., _viewProjection.., _transforms, _lightStaging) and nulls every image and vertex binding, with no lock. It runs from WndMsgObserver, which Platform::Pump calls inside MainLoop::Frame's fixed-step loop (mainloop_frame.cpp:418). render_pipe.cpp's Emit (line ~580) uses the same Video::Context* (loop->_context) on the render thread, and the file banner (THE OVERLAP) says an overlap packet's pass 2 'runs beside the next Frame's steps' and is not waited for at the fence. So the pump, and with it this Reset, runs concurrently with pass 2's context reads and writes. The guard g_bootedExclusiveFullscreen is true on DX11 exclusive fullscreen, which known_port_issues row 1334 says is the default for an empty settings.cfg.
root_cause: The observer assumes the Context is owned by the pumping thread, which was true with the faithful single-threaded draw. With render_pipe's overlap the emitting thread owns it during the steps.
minimal_fix: Do not touch the Context from the pump. Latch a flag in the observer and run ctx->Reset() at the Frame tail after render_pipe's join (or have render_pipe force a join before Platform::Pump when a reset is pending). Alternatively skip the reset while MainLoop::_extFrame is installed.

title: MaterialInstance::Setup indexes _textures/_constants with a FindTexture/FindConstant result of -1 and writes Context slots at an unbounded shader 'dest'
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (negative index, out-of-range slot write)
label: retail
label_evidence: GHIDRA-DIFF (no divergence): retail Setup 0x180102c90: 180102cd7 MOVSXD RCX,[R8+RDX] (sourceIndex) ; 180102cdb ADD RCX,RCX ; 180102cde MOV R11,[RAX+RCX*8+0x8] (_textures[src].image, no sign test) ; 180102ce3 MOVSXD RCX,[R8+RDX+0x4] (shaderSlot) ; 180102ce8 CMP R11,[RBX+RCX*8+0x30] ; 180102cfd MOV [RBX+RCX*8+0x30],R11 (Context::_imageBuffers[slot], no bound against 16). Constants arm: 180102d28 MOVSXD RDX,[R11+RCX+4] ; 180102d89 MOV [RBX+RDX*8+0x208],EAX (staging + slot*16, no bound against 4). Port lines 312-318 and 328-336 are the same operations. FindByName (0x180102f40 / 0x180103020) returns -1 ('OR EAX,0xffffffff') on a miss, and BuildParameters (0x1801033e0) stores that -1 unchecked (wave27_lane_gfxbig.cpp:634/675).
reachability: A mod material whose texture/constant list omits a name the pass's pixel shader declares, or a mod shader resource with an out-of-range dest. Setup runs on every draw of that material.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x180102c90 disassembly quoted in label_evidence, beside port wave21_lane_gfxbody.cpp:312 `const Video::ImageBuffer* image = _textures._data[b.sourceIndex].image;`, :318 `context._imageBuffers[slot] = image;` and :328 `float* dst = &context._pixelConstantStaging.material[0][0] + b.shaderSlot * 4;` followed by memcpy(dst, src, 16). With sourceIndex == -1, _textures._data[-1].image is the qword 8 bytes before the heap block (allocator header), which is then bound as an ImageBuffer* and dereferenced by BindResources. With shaderSlot >= 16, the write lands past Context::_imageBuffers[16] into _vertexBuffers and the fields after it. With shaderSlot >= 4 in the constants arm, it writes past material[4][4] into the rest of PixelConstantStaging and Context. No sanitizer run: building a Material / PixelProgram / Context fixture needs the video module, which is not in the fuzz archive.
root_cause: BuildParameters pairs each non-internal sampler/constant of the pass's PixelProgram with the material instance's entry of the same name. On a name miss FindTexture/FindConstant return -1, and the -1 is stored as MaterialBinding::sourceIndex. The shader slot is ShaderProgram::Parameter::dest, read from the shader resource (shaderprogram.cpp:170). Neither value is range-checked before Setup uses it as an array index every draw.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening in BuildParameters, which runs once per instance: skip (do not append) a binding whose sourceIndex < 0, or whose shaderSlot is outside [0,16) for textures or [0,4) for material constants. Setup's per-draw loop then needs no change.

title: SaveLoad teardown frees the embedded SavedState buffer that a queued Persistence job is still reading (save) or writing (list metadata load), without waiting for the worker
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads: buffer handed to the worker freed by its owner while the job runs
label: retail
label_evidence: Ghidra Runtime-x64.dll ??1SaveLoad 0x1800c3c90: `1800c3ca6 MOV qword ptr [0x1801fc6f0],0x0`, the String release at +0x70, `1800c3cdb LEA RCX,[RBX+0x50] / CALL 0x1800329c0` (~Array<SaveInfo>), `1800c3ce5 MOV RCX,[RBX+0x30] / TEST RCX,RCX / JZ / CALL 0x180006a10` (frees _embeddedState._data), the String release at +0x20, RET. There is no read of Persistence+0x48 (status) and no wait. RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor (saveload.cpp:400-418) transcribes exactly this. It also never frees the heap _saveState at +0x40, so a teardown mid-save leaks that block.
reachability: (1) An autosave starts; AutoSaveDialog does not pause the game, so the player can press Esc and choose Main Menu (ReturnToMenu) or Quit while state 2 is still writing. The worker reads freed blocks[0] after the CRC pass over the large blocks[1]. (2) In the front-end Load or Save dialog, UpdateList loads one row's metadata per cycle into _embeddedState through LoadJob. A menu-loop teardown during that window (Quit from the main menu while the list fills) frees the buffer the worker writes into. Timing-dependent: the window is the duration of one job.
proof: UpdateSaveTail (saveload_update.cpp:1055-1077) builds blocks[0].data = _embeddedState._data and blocks[1].data = _saveState->_data and enqueues them (RtIo_PersistenceWorker_EnqueueSave stores them in _blockPtrs, persistence_worker.cpp:450). SaveJob then reads blockPtrs[i] on the worker thread for the CRC pass and the WriteFile loop (persistence_worker.cpp:602-630). UpdateList state 3 (saveload_update.cpp:1586-1597) hands _embeddedState.SetupLoad()'s buffer to BeginLoad, and LoadJob writes into it (closure_batch2b.cpp:166-182, fs->ReadFile(st._file, size, dst)). The only wait for the job is SaveLoad::Update's `if (p->_worker._status == 0) return;` (saveload.cpp:799-800), which gates the state machine and not the destructor. RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor, reached from MainMenuDialog::ReturnToMenu (mainmenudialog.cpp:203/211), GameUpdateLoop teardown (gameupdateloop.cpp:2280) and MenuDialogLoopT teardown (menudialogloopt_stubs.cpp:301), frees _embeddedState._data at saveload.cpp:415-416 with no check of _worker._status. The tree already records the hazard at background_save.cpp:312-316: 'the teardown about to run frees the SaveLoad and with it the embedded metadata block the write reads'. Only the ext path waits.
root_cause: SaveLoad lends raw buffers (_embeddedState._data, _saveState->_data) to the Persistence worker through SaveBlock without any ownership transfer. Its destructor frees the embedded one unconditionally and never checks that the worker finished the job that borrowed it.
minimal_fix: At the top of RtSave_SaveLoad_Dtor, wait for an outstanding job when one may hold SaveLoad's buffers. If IO::Persistence::_singleton exists, (_worker._runFlags & 1) == 0 and _worker._status == 0, call _worker.WaitForFinish() before freeing _embeddedState._data. Optionally free _saveState after that wait to stop the leak. Same hardening shape as the background_save Join, applied to the faithful path.

title: CreateNaturalResource's saved cellIndex indexes Map::cells unbounded (reads, then PlaceAtCell / RegisterEntity claim the cell)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound (OOB read, then OOB cell claim)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400c6650 reads [R14+0x30] (the persisted cell) as the cell index with no compare. The port matches it.
reachability: Loading a save with a pending CreateNaturalResource action (a forester or orchard planting) whose cellIndex is outside [0, size*size). The checks read 0x30-byte records outside the cell array. If they pass (occupant 0, blocker equal to the action's parent, which is null when the parent is null), the new entity is placed at, and its MapComponent claims, the out-of-range cell.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (identical, faithful): retail 0x1400c6650: 'MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0xf8] / MOVSXD R8,dword ptr [R14 + 0x30] / LEA RDX,[R8 + R8*0x2] / ADD RDX,RDX / MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x80] / CMP qword ptr [RAX + RDX*0x8 + 0x8],0x0 / JNZ 0x1400c686d / ... MOV RBX,qword ptr [RAX + RBX*0x8] / ... CMP RBX,qword ptr [R14 + 0x28]'. Port: createnaturalresource.cpp:61 'ser.Serialize(cellIndex, nullptr);' then :105 'if (cells[cellIndex].occupant != nullptr)', :110 'cells[cellIndex].blocker', :115 CheckCellTerrain(cellIndex) (action_base_cnr.cpp:100 'cells.GetData()[cellIndex]'), :121 '.footprintCount', :138 'naturalResource->PlaceAtCell(cellIndex)'.
