title: Status-bar status-icon click with zero citizens reads citizens._data[0] past _size (stale InternalPtr: use-after-free of the last dead citizen, or null deref)
bug_class: array index without bound (OOB read / UAF)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x14007a120 has the same control flow. INC [R15+0x100] / JS reset / CMP [R15+0x100],R13D(count) / JL read, and otherwise MOV [R15+0x100],0 and fall into the read, with no count==0 test anywhere before MOV RCX,[RAX+RCX*8]. The port comment itself says 'no test of the town or of the count'.
reachability: An unmodded game: let the whole population die (starvation, freezing or disease; Banished has no game-over, so play continues in an empty town), open the toolbar's town status utility dialog (StatusBarUI), and click any of the six status icons (element ids 100..105). The icons stay clickable whatever their count, and OnElementEvent (0x14007a3a0) forwards every click with eventType 2 and id 100..106.
proof:
Retail disassembly at 0x14007a120 (faithful; there is no port diff):
14007a164: MOV R13D,dword ptr [RAX + 0xa8]   ; citizenCount = town->citizens._size
14007a17b: INC dword ptr [R15 + 0x100]       ; statusCitizenIndex++
14007a18c: JS 0x14007a197
14007a18e: CMP dword ptr [R15 + 0x100],R13D
14007a195: JL 0x14007a1a0
14007a197: MOV dword ptr [R15 + 0x100],R14D   ; index = 0, with no size test
14007a1a0: MOVSXD RCX,dword ptr [R15 + 0x100]
14007a1a7: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX + 0xa0]     ; citizens._data
14007a1b2: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + RCX*0x8]   ; _data[0] read with _size == 0
14007a1be: CALL CheckPtr ; 14007a1cc: MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x10] ; citizen->_entity

Port, statusbarui.cpp:404-437: `self->statusCitizenIndex++; if (>=0) goto bound_test; for(;;){ statusCitizenIndex = 0; do { citizen = town->citizens._data[statusCitizenIndex].Get(); icons = citizen->_entity->FindComponent<StatusIconComponent>(); ... } while (idx < citizenCount); }`. With citizenCount == 0 the bound test fails, the outer loop resets the index to 0, and the loop reads _data[0] anyway.

What is in _data[0]: citizens are removed through Array::Remove -> rtcoll::ArrayRemove8 (src/engine/collection/array.cpp:2429). It shifts later elements down and decrements _size, and it never clears or frees the vacated slot (capacity never shrinks). After the last citizen dies, _data[0] therefore still holds the InternalPtr of the freed CitizenComponent. InternalPtr::Get / CheckPtr is a bare RET, so the pointer comes back unchanged and is dereferenced (citizen->_entity, then FindComponent and the activeMask read). If the mask bit happens to be set, CenterOnEntity runs on the freed entity. If _data were ever null, the read is a null-plus-0 dereference. Either way it is an out-of-bounds index that is undefined behaviour.
root_cause: StatusBarUI_StatusIconHandler (0x14007a120) wraps statusCitizenIndex to 0 and reads citizens._data[index] before it checks that the array has any element. The loop's only exit before the read depends on the element it reads.
minimal_fix: Add a fix.* row (retail behaviour) under src/ext that returns early when town->citizens._size == 0 (`if (citizenCount <= 0) return;` before the increment), with the faithful arm kept as is. Do not use a silent guard in game code.

title: Loaded per-entity metadata (master index, bucket index, bucket id) is stored unvalidated; RemoveEntity then writes through it out of bounds (buckets[int8] past EntityList, bucketData[idx], masterData[idx])
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Serialize 0x1400c44a0 stores the three ints back into +0x18 / +0x1C (low 24 bits) / +0x1F with no test (0x1400c46b9-0x1400c46dd). Retail RemoveEntity 0x1400c38e0 indexes with them, also untested: MOVSX RCX,byte [RAX+0x1f]; CMP ECX,6; ... MOV RDX,[RDI+R8*8+0x18]; MOV RAX,[RDX+RAX*8]; MOV [RDX+RCX*8],RAX. The port mirrors this, so it is faithful.
proof:
Retail RemoveEntity 0x1400c38e0:
1400c390a: MOVSX RCX,byte ptr [RAX + 0x1f]   ; bucket id from the save
1400c390f: CMP ECX,0x6
1400c3912: JZ 0x1400c398d
1400c3921: MOV R15D,dword ptr [RDI + RAX*0x8] ; size of buckets[id] (id up to 127 -> past the 0xE8 EntityList)
1400c3931: MOV EBP,dword ptr [RAX + 0x1c]
1400c3937: SAR EBP,0x8                        ; bucket index from the save
1400c394b: MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDI + R8*0x8 + 0x18]
1400c3954: MOV qword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x8],RAX  ; WRITE bucketData[idx]
Port: Serialize lines 1608-1630 store masterIdxField / bucketIdxField / bucketId back into _entityId / _handle / _handleBytes[3] unchecked. RemoveEntity line 1416 then does `&buckets[bucketIdx]` (int8, any value but 6), and lines 1429 / 1453 do `bucketData[entityBucketIdx] = bucketData[lastIdx]` and `masterData[entityMasterIdx] = masterData[lastMasterIdx]`. A save whose entity has bucketId 40 or masterIdx 0x10000000 corrupts memory the first time that entity is removed: it is demolished, dies, or runs through FlushForSerialize on the next save. bucketId 40 reads a fake Array at EntityList+0x298 and SetSize's it. A null master slot also faults immediately at line 1608: the slot is nulled by the IsDerivedFrom filter at line 1588, then dereferenced with no test (retail 0x1400c4610 also has no test).
root_cause: The save is trusted. The per-entity bucket and master indices are persisted and restored verbatim, and every later consumer indexes with them, assuming the invariants _entityId == position in masterArray and bucket[id][low24] == entity.
minimal_fix: After the metadata loop in EntityList::Serialize, on load, validate each entity: require bucketId in 0..4 or == 6, bucketIdx < buckets[bucketId]._size with buckets[bucketId][bucketIdx] == entity, masterIdx == entityIdx, and a non-null slot. Otherwise fail the load, or rebuild the fields from positions. This is a fix.* row, because retail has no check.

title: CitizenBehavior::PostLoad files each saved residence cell into the coarse grid with no bound: AddCellEntry indexes field_0x140 with (mapW>>3)*(y>>3)+(x>>3) (heap OOB write)
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x14008f580: `iVar10 = *(int*)(lVar11 + *(this+0x130)); CitizenBehavior_AddCellEntry(this, iVar10 % iVar9, iVar10 / iVar9, iVar7);` with no range test. The port adds only an fprintf diagnostic for an out-of-range cell and then still calls AddCellEntry.
reachability: Loading a save: CitizenBehavior::Serialize reads the +0x130 pair array raw, and PostLoad runs on load when +0x148 < 1.
proof: Port lines 713-726: `int cell = residenceCells[idx].cellA; if (cell < 0 || cell >= mapWidth*mapWidth) { fprintf(...) } AddCellEntry(cell % mapWidth, cell / mapWidth, idx);`. wellcomponent.cpp:158-160: `cellIdx = (mapW >> 3) * (y >> 3) + (x >> 3); Collection::Array<int32_t>& rec = field_0x140._data[cellIdx];`, after which it reads and writes rec._size, rec._capacity and rec._data, and stores `value` through rec._data. field_0x140 has (size>>3)^2 entries. A saved cellA of -9 or >= size*size gives a negative or past-the-end cellIdx, so a 16-byte header outside the array is treated as an Array and written (count increment, MemAlloc'd pointer store, element write through its data pointer). A mapWidth of 0 from a crafted Map makes `cell % mapWidth` a division by zero (UB).
root_cause: The saved residence and water pair cells are never checked against the map size before they are used as grid coordinates.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening at the root cause in CitizenBehavior::Serialize or PostLoad: drop (or reject the save for) any pair whose cellA is outside [0, size*size), and require size > 0.

title: Minimap::Serialize reads the edge size independently of the two pixel arrays; CopyToTexture, ClearTerrain and the terrain repaint then use size*size elements
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400a57f0 does the same: SetSize(+0x28, n1) and SetSize(+0x18, n2) from separate counts, then Serialize(int* +4), then CopyToTexture(+0x18, size, size) and CopyToTexture(+0x28, size, size), with no consistency check.
reachability: Loading a save: GameUpdateLoop serializer -> Minimap::Serialize; then any building placement or removal on the minimap, or a terrain repaint.
proof: Retail 0x1400a57f0: `Collection_Array_SetSize_Int32_21d0(param_1 + 0x28, local_res8[0]); ... SetSize(param_1 + 0x18, local_res8[0]); Serialize(param_1 + 4); ... CopyToTexture(*(+8), *(+0x18), *(+4), *(+4))`. Port: Minimap::Serialize -> CreateAndUpload -> CopyToTexture(pixels, size, size) reads size*size*4 bytes from arrays sized by the saved counts. Minimap::ClearTerrain (mapcomponent.cpp:57-61) writes `cells[(width - y - row - 1) * width + x + col]` into overlayPixels for every building footprint, and minimap_paint.cpp:223-226 CopyFromTexture writes width*width pixels into terrainPixels. A save with size 768 and pixel counts of 1 gives a heap over-read on load and a heap overflow write on the first ClearTerrain or repaint.
root_cause: Same shape as F-026 (Map::Serialize), but in a different function: an edge length and an element count both come from the save, and nothing checks that count >= size*size.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening in Minimap::Serialize on load: require size > 0 and both arrays sized to size*size (SetSize(size*size), zero-filled, or reject the save).

title: With ext.render_pipe threaded, WM_ACTIVATE runs DeviceData_Resize on the main thread while the render thread is in EndCommands/Present (immediate context and swap chain used from two threads)
bug_class: data race on ID3D11DeviceContext / IDXGISwapChain / DeviceData::colorBuffer during fullscreen focus change
label: ext
label_evidence: Retail has no render thread: Resize from the WM_ACTIVATE callback 0x1800042d0 ran on the only thread that touches the immediate context. The concurrency comes from ext.render_pipe (src/ext/render_pipe). The handler itself is a faithful copy and takes no device lock (retail 0x180004340 calls no Lock).
reachability: ext.render_pipe on (opt-in, default false in registry.h:108) on a machine where Cpu::RenderThread is true, the game in fullscreen (retail's default for an empty settings.cfg), and the player alt-tabs or the window loses focus during a pipelined frame. SizeWindow is safe because it only raises settingsChanged, which makes the pipe sequential. WM_ACTIVATE is the one window message that rebuilds the swap chain synchronously from the pump.
proof:
(1) packet.h Emit: `ops.PostDraw(); ops.Released(p); ops.EndCommands(); ops.FrameUpdateTime(); ops.IncFrameIndex(); ops.Finish();`. Per the comment, Released 'may let the steps run from here', and render_pipe.cpp's banner says the steps overlap 'EndCommands, the frame index and Present'. With P13_OVERLAP even pass 2 runs beside the steps (pipe_driver.h BeforeSteps: `if (_handoff && _held.overlap && _handoff->ClaimSteps()) { _overlapping = true; return; }`).
(2) The steps contain the message pump: mainloop_frame.cpp:418 `Platform::Pump(&Application::WindowProc)` inside the `while (_accumulator >= _deltaTime._ticks)` loop, after the kExtBeforeSteps fence at :363.
(3) The pump dispatches WM_ACTIVATE to DeviceData_OnActivate. When cfg->fullscreen or wasFullscreen is set, it calls DeviceData_Resize (devicedata.cpp:928/935). Resize runs `ctx->OMSetRenderTargets(0,..); ctx->ClearState(); dev->ReleaseDynamic(); Dx11Release(self->colorBuffer); self->colorBuffer = nullptr; ... sc->ResizeTarget / ResizeBuffers / SetFullscreenState`, with no device lock or Present mutex.
(4) Meanwhile the render thread holds the device lock in ContextData::EndCommands: `IUnknown* color = dd->colorBuffer; color->AddRef(); dd->swapChain->GetBuffer(...); d3dContext->ResolveSubresource(backBuffer,0,dd->colorBuffer,...)`, then FinishPresent `dd->swapChain->Present(sync,0)`.
Interleavings: color read as null (null AddRef), or released and freed between the read and ResolveSubresource (use-after-free); ClearState concurrent with ResolveSubresource on the non-thread-safe immediate context; ResizeBuffers while the render thread holds a back-buffer reference or is inside Present (DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL).
(5) src/app/main.cpp:690 ForceVideoContextReset also runs `ctx->Reset()` and `ml->_contextDirty = 0` on the Video::Context from the same pump, concurrent with the render thread's Emit, which writes that Context.
root_cause: DeviceData_OnActivate mutates the swap chain, the immediate context and DeviceData's buffers directly from the window callback. render_pipe's fence (Released, overlap) lets the pump run while the render thread still owns those objects, and nothing makes the pump join the render thread first.
minimal_fix: Under render_pipe, make the activation rebuild deferred, as SizeWindow is: in OnActivate, set wasFullscreen/fullscreen and raise dev->settingsChanged instead of calling DeviceData_Resize; BeginCommands then runs the Resize sequentially. Alternatively, have render_pipe join the render thread before Platform::Pump when a WM_ACTIVATE is pending. Apply the same to ForceVideoContextReset in main.cpp.

title: Resources referenced only through the SM50 argument table (gpuResourceID/gpuAddress + useResource) are released before the GPU runs: ASSAO mip input views, and zeroConstants in Shutdown before the in-flight drain
bug_class: gpu-lifetime: object destroyed while in flight
label: ext
label_evidence: ext.ambient_occlusion Metal pass and the Metal backend's Shutdown; no retail counterpart.
reachability: Every frame with ext.ambient_occlusion on and qualityLevel > 1 (mip views). Device shutdown or rebuild with frames in flight (zeroConstants). SUSPECTED: depends on Metal's useResource retention semantics.
proof: assao_pass.mm:404-417: each mip level builds `inputs[i] = [d newTextureViewWithPixelFormat:... levels:NSMakeRange(level - 1, 1) ...]`. The views reach the shader only as `args[off] = t.gpuResourceID._impl` plus `[enc useResource:t ...]` (Bind, :241-250). They are never set as attachments or with setFragmentTexture, and ARC releases them at the end of each loop iteration, long before `commands` is committed in Present. backend.mm Shutdown (:1004-1023) likewise sets `zeroConstants = nil`, clears retiredBuffers / bufferUses, and drops ShareGpuData's references BEFORE the `dispatch_semaphore_wait` drain of in-flight frames. zeroConstants is referenced by in-flight frames only via `b.gpuAddress` in setVertexBytes + useResource (Resources, :409-416). If a retained-references command buffer does not retain resources passed only to useResource (Metal's bindless model leaves argument-buffer lifetime to the app), the GPU reads freed texture views or freed buffer memory. Not verifiable on this machine (no macOS/Metal).
root_cause: Lifetime of indirectly referenced (argument-table) resources rests on an unverified assumption that useResource retains. The code comment at backend.mm:107 ('the command buffer itself retains its encoded resources') covers only directly bound resources.
minimal_fix: Keep indirectly referenced objects alive until the command buffer completes: capture them in an addCompletedHandler block (e.g. an NSArray of the ASSAO views per frame), or cache the per-level views in `state` next to the depth textures. In Shutdown, move `zeroConstants = nil` and the retired/bufferUses clears after the semaphore drain.

title: Android background teardown races the render thread's BeginCommands: the swap chain, surface and per-image vectors are destroyed between the render thread's `backgrounded` check and its acquire
bug_class: data race / use-after-destroy (C10 lifecycle)
label: ext
reachability: Android with ext.render_pipe's render thread up (the Android settings profile): press Home or switch apps while a frame is being begun. The window is the whole of steps 2-4 above, which includes a blocking fence wait, so it is hit regularly. Desktop platforms never send the event.
proof:
LifecycleWatch (device.cpp ~171-190, main thread inside the SDL event pump) on SDL_EVENT_WILL_ENTER_BACKGROUND does three things. First, it waits only for `framesOpen == 0`. Second, it calls vkDeviceWaitIdle. Third, it calls DestroySwapchainObjects() (which clears swapImages / swapViews / renderFinished), vkDestroySwapchainKHR(swapchain), `swapchain = VK_NULL_HANDLE`, SDL_Vulkan_DestroySurface and `surface = VK_NULL_HANDLE`. framesOpen is only incremented by FrameOpened() AFTER a successful vkAcquireNextImageKHR (BeginCommands ~1448).

With ext.render_pipe threaded (the Android profile), BeginCommands runs on the render thread (render_pipe.cpp: 'BeginCommands takes it and FinishPresent drops it, both on the render thread'). Its order is:
1. `if (backgrounded.load()) return false;` (~1401)
2. `if (!surface) ...` and `if (swapchainDirty) { vkDeviceWaitIdle; CreateSwapchain(...) }`
3. `vkWaitForFences(f.done, UINT64_MAX)` (blocks for a GPU frame)
4. `vkAcquireNextImageKHR(device, swapchain, ...)`
5. `FrameOpened()`

If the event arrives while the render thread is anywhere in steps 2-4, framesOpen is 0, so the watch tears down at once. The render thread then acquires on a destroyed VkSwapchainKHR, or on VK_NULL_HANDLE (both are VU violations / UB), or runs CreateSwapchain on a destroyed surface. If the acquire 'succeeds', it indexes `swapImages[imageIndex]` / `swapViews[imageIndex]` (~1468-1479) and later `renderFinished[imageIndex]` (PresentFrame ~1531/1537), all on vectors the main thread just cleared: an out-of-bounds read of a std::vector.

The globals `swapchain`, `surface`, `imageAcquired`, `swapchainDirty` and the three vectors are plain (non-atomic, unlocked), and the watch writes them while the render thread reads them. That is a C++ data race (UB) independent of the Vulkan misuse. The watch's own 2 s timeout ('a frame is still open after 2 s; tearing down anyway') deliberately takes the same teardown with a frame open.
root_cause: The background teardown synchronises only with frames that have already acquired (framesOpen). It does not synchronise with a BeginCommands that has passed the `backgrounded` check but not yet acquired, and the shared swap-chain globals have no lock.
minimal_fix: Make 'begun' cover the whole of BeginCommands: take frameLock (or bump framesOpen) before the `backgrounded` check and re-check `backgrounded` under it, then drop the count on every early return. Alternatively, have the watch hand the teardown to the render thread (set backgrounded, then wait on a 'render thread parked' flag) instead of destroying the objects from the main thread. Drop the 2 s 'tear down anyway' path, or make it skip the teardown rather than destroy objects in use.

title: Retire stamp can miss an upload recorded between PresentFrame's FlushUploads and NoteFrameSubmitted: GPU use-after-free of a retired buffer/image
bug_class: GPU resource lifetime / deferred deletion
label: ext
label_evidence: src/render/vulkan is the replacement backend with no retail counterpart (retail is VideoDX11).
proof:
Retire (resources.cpp:677-680) stamps e.frame = FramesSubmitted(). CollectRetired (:660-675) destroys an entry once FramesCompleted() > e.frame, so the destroy waits only for the frame-N submission. PresentFrame (device.cpp:1524-1534) runs `dev->Unlock(); FlushUploads(); serial = SubmitCommands(frame N); NoteFrameSubmitted(serial);`. The device lock is dropped on purpose before the flush ('a loader thread linking a new resource never waits out the presentation').

Interleaving: the render thread runs FlushUploads (batch X submitted). A loader or AsyncCreate worker then calls UploadBuffer/UploadImage (resources.cpp:712/858), which opens a NEW batch Y and records vkCmdCopyBuffer/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage into the object. The same thread then retires that object, and FramesSubmitted() is still N, so the stamp is N. The render thread then submits frame N and NoteFrameSubmitted makes the count N+1. Batch Y is submitted at frame N+1's FlushUploads, with a serial greater than frame N's. At BeginCommands of frame N+2 the slot fence covers only frame N, and CollectRetired runs vkDestroyBuffer/vmaDestroyImage on the object while batch Y may still be pending or executing. Batch Y may even still be open, never submitted.

The upload-then-retire pair happens on worker threads in share_create.cpp:104-106 and :163-165, where the lost race of ext.share_gpu_data runs RetireBuffer(out)/RetireImage(out). Its comment states the assumption this breaks: 'its upload may still be queued: retired, not destroyed'. It also happens on any ImageBufferData::Create / CreateBuffer of an object whose previous contents were just uploaded (ReleaseStore / ReleaseImage then Retire).
root_cause: The retire queue's lifetime rule assumes every GPU use of an object retired at stamp N is in a submission no later than frame N's. The open upload batch breaks that rule: a batch opened after PresentFrame's FlushUploads is submitted after frame N, but FramesSubmitted() still reads N until NoteFrameSubmitted. Nothing orders the stamp against batch membership: Retire holds g_frameLock/g_retireLock, uploads hold g_uploadLock.
minimal_fix: Stamp the retire conservatively: e.frame = FramesSubmitted() + 1. Alternatively, make FlushUploads + SubmitCommands + NoteFrameSubmitted atomic with respect to uploads, by holding g_uploadLock across them or by bumping the frame count before FlushUploads. A third option is to record the open batch's future serial in the entry and destroy only once CompletedSerial() reaches it.

title: SPIR-V cache decode accepts any CombinedPair binding/texture byte; StageImages then writes views[]/samplers[] out of bounds and MasksOf shifts by >=32
bug_class: unchecked input -> stack out-of-bounds write / oversized shift
label: ext
reachability: A crafted or foreign record in the derived-data cache under <Documents>/Banished/Cache whose key matches a game shader, loaded by LoadOrConvert on the Vulkan backend. The encoder never produces such values, so this needs a hostile or cross-build file.
proof: DecodeEntry (shader_convert.cpp:629-637) only checks extras <= kMaxSamplers. It then copies p.binding = r.U8(); p.texture = r.U8(); p.sampler = r.U8(); with no range check. The consumers assume binding is in [BindingOfSampler(0)=24, 40) and texture < 16. draw.cpp:873-877 StageImages: `const uint32_t i = kTextureSlots + (p.binding - Shaders::BindingOfSampler(0)); views[i] = view(p.texture); samplers[i] = sampler(p.sampler); mask |= 1u << i;`. views/samplers are VkImageView[kImageBindings=32] arrays: on the stack in PushPixelSet, or inside SetKey/VertexSetKey. binding=255 gives i=247 and binding=0 gives i=0xFFFFFFF0: both write out of bounds, and 1u<<i is a shift >= 32 (UB). view(p.texture) indexes g_bound.textures[16] with t up to 255 (out-of-bounds read) and evaluates textureCubeMask >> t (UB for t >= 32). pipelines.cpp:447 MasksOf: `m.smp |= 1u << (p.binding - Shaders::BindingOfSampler(0));` is UB for binding < 24 or > 55. shader_cache.cpp's own contract says a damaged entry that the store's hash does not catch 'is a miss'. The store hash is an unkeyed FNV-style Hash64, so a crafted entry with a correct hash decodes successfully.
root_cause: DecodeEntry checks the extraPairs count but not the fields of each pair, and the reflection is then trusted as converter output.
minimal_fix: In DecodeEntry, reject the entry (so it becomes a cache miss and is reconverted) unless every pair has binding >= BindingOfSampler(0), binding - BindingOfSampler(0) < kMaxSamplers, texture < kMaxTextures and sampler < kMaxSamplers. Also reject masks with bits above kMaxConstantBuffers / kMaxTextures and textureSampler bytes other than kNoSampler or < kMaxSamplers.

title: Picking::Scene::AddMesh uses the mesh file's SubMesh::_parent as an unbounded index into the transform scratch array
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail ?AddMesh@Scene@Picking@@ (0x1801252e0): `this_00 = (Quaternion*)(puVar11 + (longlong)*(int*)(*(longlong*)(param_2+0x38) + 8 + lVar14) * 7);` reads the parent's world transform at scratch + parent*0x1c with no range check. Port: `const ::Transform* parent = &dst[node->_parent];`.
reachability: A PickingMesh resource in a mod package (or a damaged .rsc) with an out-of-range parent index, placed by any building or object that AddMesh registers.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (identical, retail-faithful UB): 0x1801252e0 loop body `puVar11 + (int)[nodes + 8 + i*0x80] * 7` (dwords) versus port scene.cpp:285 `&dst[node->_parent]`. PickingMesh::Serialize (pickingmesh.cpp, SerializeInt(s->_parent)) stores the int straight from the resource. A _parent < 0 or >= nodeCount reads up to 2^31*0x1c bytes outside the heap scratch. A _parent >= i reads a not-yet-computed identity entry, which is defined behaviour. No sanitizer run: building a PickingMesh needs the External/Serializer stack.
root_cause: The sub-mesh parent index read from the PickingMesh resource is trusted.
minimal_fix: fix.* row: in AddMesh (or at PickingMesh load), treat _parent outside [0, i) as 0 (the root), or reject the mesh.
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: Picking::Scene::Intersect reads verts[i0/i1/i2] with triangle indices from the mesh file, unchecked against the vertex count
bug_class: array index from data without a bound
label: retail
label_evidence: The port comment states a faithful transliteration of retail 0x1801246c0's per-triangle loop. The disassembly was not quoted in this pass; the triangle loop is the one documented at 0x180124B56-0x180124EF5.
reachability: A mod PickingMesh with a triangle index >= its vertex count. The read is reached by Intersect from mapquery.cpp, edittool.cpp and pathtool.cpp on mouse picking.
proof: pickingmesh.cpp SerializeTrianglesBody stores u16 i0..i2 from the resource, and the vertex array size is a separate serialized count. scene.cpp:466-480 reads `verts[i0].x/y/z`, `verts[i1]`, `verts[i2]` with no comparison to node->_vertices._size. An index >= vCount (up to 65535*12 bytes past the array) is a heap OOB read on every ray cast (mouse picking each frame). Not sanitizer-run.

minimal_fix: fix.* row: validate at PickingMesh load that every triangle index is < the sub-mesh's vertex count (reject or drop the triangle).
module: src/engine/math + volume + pathfinding + picking + collision2d + achievement + input

title: GameUpdateLoop::Load's build-owner and world-built latches are keyed by the loop's address and never cleared: a new loop at the freed loop's address skips the whole world build and is reported built at once
bug_class: C1 cache keyed by object pointer with no Forget (ABA on a freed address)
label: port
reachability: Play a game, quit to the main menu, start New Game or Load a save. Whether it fires depends on the allocator returning the same 0x160 block. That is likely given the LIFO bin head, but not deterministic, which also explains why the quit-to-menu runs logged so far did not show it.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail GameUpdateLoop::Load 0x140096b00 has no ownership test; its first stores are
  140096b27: MOV R15,RCX
  140096b2a: XOR R14D,R14D
  140096b35: MOV qword ptr [0x1401c3dd8],RCX     ; _singleton = this
  140096b3c: LEA RDX,[0x14015e428]                ; step 1 resource name
  140096b47: CALL qword ptr [0x1401516f8]
Port, gameupdateloop_load.cpp:715-721:
  static std::atomic<void*> s_loadingLoop{nullptr};
  if (s_loadingLoop.exchange(loopVoid) == loopVoid) { fprintf(..."redundant dispatch"...); return; }
and :684 / :1496: `static std::atomic<void*> s_worldBuiltLoop` is stored with `loopVoid` at the end of Load. splash_loop_stubs.cpp:456 gates the loading screen on `GameUpdateLoop_IsWorldBuilt(_nextLoop)` (== s_worldBuiltLoop). Nothing resets either value. ~GameUpdateLoop (gameupdateloop.cpp:2413-2429) clears only _singleton, and grep finds no other writer. Quit to menu frees the 0x160 block. The next New Game (newgamedialog.cpp:689) or main-menu Load (worldsetup_reload.cpp:96) does MemAlloc(0x160, 8). The engine allocator pushes freed blocks onto the head of their size bin (allocator.cpp LinkFreeTag) and returns the first fit (GetFreeTagForSize), so the new loop can land at the freed address. When it does: (1) Load returns at the exchange without building the world (m_game, m_entityList, scene and every other subsystem stay null); (2) IsWorldBuilt is already true, so the splash fades into GameUpdateLoop::Update/Draw on an unbuilt loop and the first unguarded deref of m_game crashes.
root_cause: Two port-only (NOT RETAIL) guards identify 'this loop' by its raw address and survive the object. Once the loop is destroyed the address is free for reuse, and a new loop at that address inherits the dead loop's 'owned' and 'built' state.
minimal_fix: Clear both on destruction: in ~GameUpdateLoop (or GameUpdateLoop::Shutdown) do `s_loadingLoop.compare_exchange_strong(this, nullptr)` and the same for s_worldBuiltLoop. Hoisting s_loadingLoop out of Load to file scope makes that possible. Better, replace the address identity with a per-object flag (a non-retail bool on the loop is not possible because the 0x160 layout is fixed, so use a generation counter stored with the pointer).

title: PreloadRefs skips the highest reference id (ids run 1..N, loop runs 0..N-1), so one save-only resource is still parsed with reference mode ON
bug_class: off-by-one in a port-only failure workaround (the preload that prevents the wrong-shape parse)
label: port
label_evidence: The whole PreloadRefs block is NOT RETAIL (the comment says retail preloads its resources up front). The id base comes from the object module: SerializeReferenceTable's write path numbers the tree from ONE (external_reftable.cpp:303 `uint32_t id = 1;`, retail 1800bcdf4), and GetPathForReferenceId(0) misses and returns an empty Filename (external.cpp, the null-temporary arm).
reachability: Every save load. It bites when the resource whose path sorts last in the save's reference table has not already been loaded by the time the reference-mode window opens.
proof: external_reftable.cpp:303 `uint32_t id = 1; // 1800bcdf4, ids start at ONE` ... `++id` per node, so a save holds ids 1..N with N = _references count after load. gameupdateloop_serialize.cpp:612-614: `const int refCount = extFactory->_references.GetCount(); ... for (int id = 0; id < refCount; ++id) { ... GetPathForReferenceId((unsigned int)id)); if (!path->_data) continue;`. id 0 always misses and is skipped (`continue`), and id N (the last resource in path order) is never preloaded. If that resource is referenced only by the save, its first parse happens later inside the reference-mode window. Its nested ExternalPtrs then read a uint id instead of bool+string (external_ptr_serialize.cpp mode 2 vs 3), come out null, and shift every later field. This is the exact SoundBuffer-null XAudio2 crash the block's own comment describes for RiverEffect.rsc.
root_cause: The preload loop assumes 0-based reference ids, but the reference table is 1-based.
minimal_fix: Iterate `for (int id = 1; id <= refCount; ++id)`. Alternatively walk `_references` in order and preload every node's path, which does not depend on the id base.

title: fix.boot_device_lost recovery runs CreateDevice on a minimized window; AdjustDisplay latches 0x0 and the recovery dies with a fatal 'D3D11 Error' box
bug_class: device-lost recovery on a zero-extent (minimized) window
label: port
label_evidence: Both halves are port-only. (1) Retail Resize 0x180004340 has no IsIconic test; only IsWindowVisible gates it: `18000435f MOV byte ptr [RAX+0x9c],0x1 / 18000436a MOV RCX,[RAX+0x90] / 180004371 CALL [0x1800134e0] ;IsWindowVisible / 180004377 TEST EAX,EAX / 180004379 JZ 0x1800044f7 / 18000437f MOV RCX,[RBX+0x28] ... CALL [RAX+0x108] ;OMSetRenderTargets`. The port adds `if (Platform::Window::IsIconic(dev->windowHandle)) return 0;` at devicedata.cpp:740. (2) Retail BeginCommands 0x180001650 discards Resize's result: `180001693 CMP byte ptr [RDI+0x9c],SIL / 18000169a JZ 0x1800016ba / 18000169c MOV RCX,[RDI+0x100] / 1800016a3 CALL 0x180004340`, then returns false. The port's seam (contextdata.cpp:458-467) calls RecoverLostDevice whenever resized==0 and GetDeviceRemovedReason()!=0.
reachability: Default configuration: fix.boot_device_lost is on (registry.h:67). Steps: a windowed game is minimized, then a GPU TDR, driver update or adapter reset occurs before the player restores it. The next frame after the removal takes the recovery path while the window is still iconic.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: see label_evidence for the retail sequences at 0x180004340 and 0x180001650.

The port path:
- Minimizing a windowed game: SizeWindow (device_window.cpp:72-78) stores GetClientRect=0x0 and raises settingsChanged.
- Every frame BeginCommands -> DeviceData_Resize -> devicedata.cpp:740 `IsIconic -> return 0`.
- With the row on (the default) and a removed device (a TDR or a driver update while the game is minimized), contextdata.cpp:459 `GetDeviceRemovedReason() != 0` -> RecoverLostDevice -> Shutdown -> CreateDevice.
- CreateDevice step 8 calls Video::Device::AdjustDisplay. Its windowed branch ends with `GetClientRect(hwnd,&client); backBufferHeight = ch; backBufferWidth = cw; cfg->windowWidth = cw; cfg->windowHeight = ch;` (device_adjustdisplay.cpp:206-213). There is no degenerate-size guard on this path; that guard exists only in Resize. On an iconic window this gives 0x0.
- FillSwapChainDesc gets Width=Height=0, and then CreateAttachment builds D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC with Width=0, which CreateTexture2D rejects.
- CreateDevice returns false ('Failed to create color buffer ... [0x0 ...]').
- RecoverLostDevice then runs `System::Error::SetText(msg, true); System::Error::Display();`, which exits through DisplayStopIfRequested -> ExitProcess(-1).

Retail and the faithful profile never run a recovery while minimized: they spin in the reset until restore. The fix row added to recover therefore turns 'GPU reset while minimized' into a fatal exit.

In exclusive fullscreen the same seam runs CreateDevice with cfg->fullscreen forced back to 1 by Shutdown (wasFullscreen) on an inactive window. CreateSwapChain(Windowed=FALSE) then returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED, which the `!= 0` test treats as failure: the same fatal box.
root_cause: The seam treats every failed reset on a removed device as 'recover now'. The port's own IsIconic early-out makes a failed reset the normal state while minimized, and CreateDevice/AdjustDisplay cannot build a swap chain for a zero client area.
minimal_fix: In the BeginCommands seam, defer the recovery while `Platform::Window::IsIconic(dev->windowHandle)` (or while !IsVisible): leave settingsChanged set and run RecoverLostDevice on the first frame the window is restored. Alternatively, have RecoverLostDevice skip CreateDevice until the client rect is non-degenerate.

title: RenameBuffer copies into an unchecked NewBuffer result: a failed rename allocation null-derefs in SetData
bug_class: unchecked result (allocation) -> null write
label: ext
label_evidence: src/render/metal is the Metal backend, with no retail counterpart (retail ships only VideoDX11).
reachability: Any SetData (UpdateSubresource-style write) on a vertex/index buffer the GPU is still reading, when Metal cannot allocate a same-size buffer (memory pressure or a buffer above maxBufferLength). Lock is safe by accident: cursor is reset to 0, so it returns NULL+0 and BeginVertices fails.
proof: backend.mm:247-251: `} else { fresh = NewBuffer(previous.length, "rename"); } if (preserve) { memcpy(fresh.contents, previous.contents, previous.length); }`. NewBuffer (154-161) returns the raw `[gpu newBufferWithLength:...]`, which is nil on allocation failure or above maxBufferLength, and `nil.contents` is NULL. The preserve path (VertexBufferData/IndexBufferData::SetData, 1853-1855 and 1934-1936) memcpys previous.length bytes to NULL. Even without preserve, line 258 stores `buffer = fresh` (nil), so the caller's next line `memcpy(static_cast<uint8_t*>(buffer.contents) + offsetBytes, src, sizeBytes)` writes to NULL+offset. The busy buffer has also been retired, so the owner is left with no buffer.
root_cause: The new-buffer result in the dynamic-buffer rename is used without a nil check. TakeRetiredBuffer may return nil (handled), but the NewBuffer fallback is assumed to succeed.
minimal_fix: After `fresh = NewBuffer(...)`, `if (!fresh) return;`: keep the busy buffer and write in place, or let the caller fail. In SetData, re-check `buffer` after RenameBuffer and return false when it is nil.

title: Int4 vertex expansion writes through an unchecked NewBuffer result (memset/loop on nil.contents)
bug_class: unchecked result (allocation) -> null write
label: ext
label_evidence: The Metal backend's UChar4->Int4 widening for DXBC int4 inputs has no retail counterpart.
reachability: Every draw whose vertex shader declares an int4 input fed by a UChar4 layout element (the skinned/bone-index path), on a cache miss. Crashes only when the Metal allocation fails.
proof: backend.mm:569-583: `size_t expandedBytes = std::max(size_t(16), n * 16); ... if (!inlineBytes) { expanded = NewBuffer(expandedBytes, "expanded-vertex"); dst = static_cast<int32_t*>(expanded.contents); } memset(dst, 0, expandedBytes); ... dst[v * 4 + k] = ...`. Nothing checks for nil. n is (source.length - begin) / stride over the whole remaining source buffer, not the draw's vertex count, so expandedBytes can be several times a large stream's size. A static source above 4 KB always takes this path, and so does a dynamic one above 4 KB, which allocates a new buffer on every draw. A failed allocation gives memset(NULL, 0, expandedBytes) on the render thread.
root_cause: The NewBuffer result is not checked before its contents pointer is used. The allocation size scales with the whole source buffer, not with the draw.
minimal_fix: `if (!expanded) continue;` (skip the widened stream for this draw) right after NewBuffer. Optionally bound n by the draw's maximum vertex index to shrink the allocation.

title: ASSAO init marks the pass ready without checking the constant ring allocation; WriteConstants memcpys to nil.contents
bug_class: unchecked result (allocation) -> null write
label: ext
label_evidence: ext.ambient_occlusion Metal pass (src/render/metal/passes); retail has no AO.
reachability: ext.ambient_occlusion on with the Metal backend, only when the 1 MB shared buffer allocation fails at first use (device under memory pressure). Low likelihood, but a deterministic crash on the first AO frame when it happens.
proof: assao_pass.mm:118-121: `state.triangle = [device newBufferWithBytes:...]; state.constantRing = [device newBufferWithLength:kSlotBytes * kRingSlots ...]; state.constantNext = 0; state.ready = true;`. Neither buffer is checked. Then lines 128-131 (WriteConstants, called by every Fullscreen): `std::memcpy(static_cast<char*>(state.constantRing.contents) + offset, &c, sizeof(c));`. If the 1 MB ring allocation failed, this writes 240 B to NULL + slot*256. Ready() and AoBackend::Supported() report true, so the extension stays on.
root_cause: InitLocked sets ready = true after shader conversion only. The two buffer allocations are discarded results.
minimal_fix: `if (!state.triangle || !state.constantRing) { return false; }` before `state.ready = true` (ready stays false, so Supported() answers no).

title: Device-lost recovery while the window is minimised (or the Android app is in the background) always fails CreateDevice and stops the application
bug_class: device-lost recovery: partial-failure path during re-init
label: ext
reachability: A GPU reset / TDR or driver update while the game is minimised (alt-tab plus minimise during a long background save, a laptop sleep), or an Android driver that loses the device on backgrounding. BANISHED_FORCE_DEVICE_LOST=bgsave reproduces it if the window is minimised before the injected present.
proof:
In BeginCommands, `if (lost.load()) return BeginLostFrame(dev, ctx);` (~1399) comes BEFORE the minimise / background handling. A loss noted by any thread (an upload submit or a fence wait on the loader thread; NoteResult sets `lost`) is therefore recovered even while the window is minimised or backgrounded.

RecoverLostDevice (~1564-1571) runs `ddBase->Shutdown(); const bool created = ddBase->CreateDevice(); if (!created) { System::Error::SetText("Vulkan Error: VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST!", true); System::Error::Display(); return; }`. SetText's `true` is stopApplication; Display ends in DisplayStopIfRequested.

CreateDevice step 11 (~1171) is `if (!CreateSwapchain(w, &why)) return Fail("Vulkan: " + why);`, and CreateSwapchain (~436-438) is `if (extent.width == 0 || extent.height == 0) { *why = "the window has no pixels (minimised)"; return false; }`. On Windows a minimised window's surface currentExtent is 0x0, so the swap-chain step always fails. On Android in the background, CreateDevice's SDL_Vulkan_CreateSurface (~1061) has no native window and fails too.

BeginCommands itself treats both states as transient ('minimised, or the surface is gone: try again next frame'), but the recovery has no such retry, so a recoverable device loss becomes a fatal error box and exit. The DX11 backend's recovery recreates the device without a client-sized back buffer.
root_cause: Device creation couples device creation to a presentable swap chain. Neither the recovery nor BeginCommands defers the recovery until the window has pixels or a surface.
minimal_fix: In BeginCommands, check minimised (SDL_WINDOW_MINIMIZED / zero surface extent) and `backgrounded` before entering BeginLostFrame, so the recovery waits until the window is back. Alternatively, let CreateDevice succeed without a swap chain (leave swapchainDirty = true and treat the minimised CreateSwapchain answer as non-fatal) so that BeginCommands builds it once the window has pixels.

title: Unchecked VkResult on command pool / command buffer creation passes VK_NULL_HANDLE command buffers to vkBeginCommandBuffer / vkCmd*
bug_class: discarded VkResult -> null dispatchable handle
label: ext
reachability: Device or host out-of-memory during an upload or an in-frame read-back (large towns on low-memory mobile GPUs, which this backend targets). Not reachable on a healthy device.
proof: resources.cpp:211-224 OpenBatchLocked: the return values of `vkCreateCommandPool(Dev(), &pi, nullptr, &b->pool);` and `vkAllocateCommandBuffers(Dev(), &ai, &b->cb);` are discarded, then `vkBeginCommandBuffer(b->cb, &bi); MemoryBarrier(b->cb, ...)`. On VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_*_MEMORY, b->cb is VK_NULL_HANDLE: the spec sets the array to NULL on failure, and b->cb is value-initialised anyway. The loader trampoline then dereferences the null dispatchable handle's dispatch table, which crashes. Every later UploadBuffer/UploadImage/ClearImage records into it. device.cpp:735-747 SubmitFrameSoFar (the in-frame DrawReadImage path: minimap, save thumbnail, screenshot) has the same shape: `VkCommandBuffer cb = VK_NULL_HANDLE; vkAllocateCommandBuffers(device, &ai, &cb); f.extra.push_back(cb); f.commands = ...; vkBeginCommandBuffer(f.commands, &bi);`. The null cb is also cached in f.extra and reused on every later read. Related discards: device.cpp:663/665 vkCreateFence / vkCreateSemaphore for the frame slots (a null fence is later waited on and reset), and device.cpp:521/523 swapchain image views and renderFinished semaphores.
root_cause: Creation calls whose failure is assumed impossible. The surrounding code checks VkResult elsewhere (e.g. FrameSlots at device.cpp:657, DrawReadImage's own between-frames allocate).
minimal_fix: Check each result. In OpenBatchLocked, return nullptr on failure and make StageLocked/UploadBuffer/UploadImage/ClearImage/CreateStaticBuffer treat a null batch as a failed upload. In SubmitFrameSoFar, do not push a null cb: report failure so DrawReadImage returns false. Fail device or swapchain creation when a fence, semaphore or view cannot be made.

title: A failed frame submit leaves the slot fence unsignalled: the next BeginCommands on that slot waits forever (and imageAvailable is left signalled)
bug_class: frame-in-flight synchronisation / hang
label: ext
label_evidence: Vulkan backend frame loop, no retail counterpart.
proof: SubmitCommands (resources.cpp:578-584) returns 0 when vkQueueSubmit2 fails. The frame's fence f.done is then never signalled. The 1.1 path does the same: SubmitCommands11 returns 0 without submitting when vkCreateFence fails (:513-518), and when vkQueueSubmit fails (:529-535). Its second empty submit that signals the caller's fence can also fail (:540-545). NoteResult flags only VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, so a VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY or VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY failure does not start the recovery. PresentFrame (device.cpp:1532-1552) then presents with a wait on renderFinished[imageIndex] that nothing signals, and advances frameSlot. vkResetFences(f.done) already ran in BeginCommands (device.cpp:1450). kFramesInFlight frames later, BeginCommands calls vkWaitForFences(device, 1, &f.done, VK_TRUE, UINT64_MAX) (device.cpp:1430), which never returns. Also, f.imageAvailable was signalled by the acquire and never waited, so a later vkAcquireNextImageKHR on that semaphore is invalid usage (pending signal).
root_cause: The frame's fence and acquire semaphore are consumed only by a successful submit. The failure arm treats a non-device-lost error as 'nothing ran' (serial 0) but does not restore the per-slot sync objects.
minimal_fix: When the frame submit fails without a device loss, signal f.done and consume imageAvailable with an empty vkQueueSubmit (wait imageAvailable, signal f.done), or escalate to the device-lost recovery. Treat any submit failure as fatal by calling NoteResult(VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) so the recovery path rebuilds the frames.

title: Stream worker reads AudioChannel::source before the main thread has stored it (data race; a lost race leaves a streamed track silent and its channel never reaped)
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads: data race on a field published after the consumer thread is woken
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail order is identical. Scene::Update calls PlayPlatform at 0x1800dfb17. For a streamed buffer PlayPlatform ends in Stream::Play (0x1800de9e4), which does SetEvent(hStart) and wakes the worker. Only after PlayPlatform returns does Scene::Update store the flags and the source: 0x1800dfb39 `OR dword ptr [R15+RAX*8],0x1` and 0x1800dfb3e `MOV qword ptr [R15+RAX*8+0x8],RBX`. Stream::Run reads that same field with no lock at 0x1800a0fb7 `MOV RBX,qword ptr [RCX+0x8]` and returns at 0x1800a0fc2 `TEST RBX,RBX / JZ 0x1800a1654` when it is null. The port reproduces both sides (audio_scene_update.cpp:510-511 after the PlayPlatform call at :502; audio_stream_run.cpp:269-270).
reachability: Every streamed SoundBuffer start (music, soundType 2) goes through Scene::Update -> PlayPlatform -> Stream::Play. No crafted input is needed; it depends on timing (thread wake against 3-4 instructions on the main thread).
proof:
GHIDRA (retail-faithful, no diff). Writer, Scene::Update 0x1800df6c0:
  1800dfb17: CALL 0x1800de7a0            ; Device::PlayPlatform -> Stream::Play -> SetEvent(hStart) wakes the worker
  1800dfb23: TEST AL,AL / JNZ 1800dfb30
  1800dfb39: OR dword ptr [R15 + RAX*0x8],0x1
  1800dfb3e: MOV qword ptr [R15 + RAX*0x8 + 0x8],RBX   ; channel->source = buffer  (AFTER the wake)
  1800dfb4a: MOV qword ptr [R15 + RAX*0x8 + 0x20],RCX  ; onComplete
Reader, Stream::Run 0x1800a0f60 (stream thread):
  1800a0f84: MOVSXD RCX,dword ptr [RCX + 0x7c]   ; _channel
  1800a0faa: LEA RCX,[RDX + RAX*0x8]             ; &Device->_channels[slot]
  1800a0fb7: MOV RBX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x8]       ; source, unsynchronised
  1800a0fc2: JZ 0x1800a1654                      ; null -> return
Port: audio_play_platform.cpp:426 `_stream.Play(slot, bytePos);` runs inside PlayPlatform. audio_scene_update.cpp:502-511 then stores `s->flags |= 1u; s->source = bufferRef;` on the main thread. audio_stream_run.cpp:269 `const SoundBuffer* const buf = chan->source; if (!buf) return;` runs on the Stream thread. No lock or fence orders the two, so this is a C++ data race (UB). If the worker wins (main thread preempted right after SetEvent, more likely on few-core devices such as Android), Run returns at once. The voice is then started with no buffer submitted, OnStreamEnd never fires, Device channel flags stays 1, the Scene channel never reaches endedCount == sampleCount, and the track stays 'playing' and silent until something stops it explicitly.
root_cause: The consumer is woken (Stream::Play's SetEvent) inside PlayPlatform, before the caller publishes channel->source, and the field is a plain pointer with no synchronisation.
minimal_fix: This changes retail behaviour, so it is a fix.* row with a settings switch (AGENTS.md §2). Store `s->source = bufferRef` (and flag bit 0) before the PlayPlatform call, so the store happens-before Stream::Play's EventSet; on PlayPlatform failure, clear it again. Alternatively, pass the buffer to Stream::Play and have Run read it from the Stream, under the Stream lock.

title: A streamed SoundBuffer can be freed while Stream::Run still reads its seek table outside the lock (use after free across threads)
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads: a buffer freed while a worker thread still holds a raw pointer into it
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail Stream::Run caches buf->_wmaData once (0x1800a0fd4 `MOV R9,[RBX+0x48]`, spilled to [RBP-0x60]) and dereferences it between the locked regions: 0x1800a11f9 `MOV R9D,[R8+R12*4-0x4]` and the cumulativeBytes loop at 0x1800a1230 `MOV ECX,[R10+RDX]`. ~SoundBuffer (0x1800e03b0) calls Device::OnSoundBufferDeleted and then MemFree(_wmaData). Device::OnSoundBufferDeleted (0x1800de0e0) and Device::Stop (0x1800de200 -> StopPlatform 0x1800dea20) only set _stopping, SetEvent the wake handle and destroy the voice under the Stream lock. Neither waits on the worker's _hFinished; only Stream::Play and ~Stream wait on it. The port adds more reads of the same pointer: XwmaDecoder::Open(segTable) and DecodeChunk.
reachability: Requires a streamed (music) SoundBuffer to be destroyed (ExternalFactory Clean when an UpdateLoop is deleted, or an External reload) within the few milliseconds the worker spends reading and decoding one 16-packet chunk after the stop. That is a narrow timing window, not shown in a run; SUSPECTED.
proof:
GHIDRA (retail-faithful). Stream::Run 0x1800a0f60:
  1800a0fd4: MOV R9,qword ptr [RBX + 0x48]     ; segTable = buf->_wmaData, cached
  1800a0fd8: MOV qword ptr [RBP + -0x60],R9
  ... per chunk, NOT under the Stream lock (the lock is taken later at 1800a124b):
  1800a11e7: CALL 0x1800ace00                  ; FileSystem::ReadFile into the block
  1800a11ec: MOV R8,qword ptr [RBP + -0x60]
  1800a11f9: MOV R9D,dword ptr [R8 + R12*0x4 + -0x4]   ; segTable[curSeg-1]
  1800a1230: MOV ECX,dword ptr [R10 + RDX*0x1]         ; segTable[curSeg+k]
Device::Stop 0x1800de200: CALL 0x1800dea20 (StopPlatform: _stopping=1, SetEvent wake), CALL 0x1800de6f0 (FreeChannelPlatform), clear flags/source, fire the callback, RET. There is no wait for the worker.
Port: audio_stream_run.cpp:276 caches `segTable = buf->_wmaData`. Lines 361-375 (ReadFile, `base = segTable[curSeg64 - 1]`, the cumulativeBytes loop) and the port-only `decoder.DecodeChunk(...)` (the decoder holds segTable from Open) run before the MutexLock at the voice test. batchc_audio_leaves.cpp:139-144: ~SoundBuffer -> OnSoundBufferDeleted (destroys the voice) -> MemFree(_wmaData) with no join. If the last reference to a playing streamed buffer is dropped while the worker is between ReadFile and the next MutexLock, the worker reads freed memory. The port also reads buf->_loopForever after the wait (line ~389).
root_cause: Ownership of the SoundBuffer is not shared with the Stream worker. Nothing on the free path waits for Stream::Run to leave its pass, and the worker uses raw pointers into the buffer outside the Stream lock.
minimal_fix: In ~SoundBuffer (or OnSoundBufferDeleted, for a channel whose source is _streamed), after the voice is destroyed, wait on the Stream's _hFinished when _runFlags bit 0 is set, as Stream::Play's mid-pass arm already does (set _stopping, EventSet(_wakeEvent), EventWait(_hFinished)). This adds a wait retail does not have, so it is a fix.* row (AGENTS.md §2).

title: SunLight::ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync rewrites the live sun map's _depthTarget/_colourTarget descriptors during the overlapped steps while the render thread's pass 2 reads _depthTarget->Width() (SunLight::DrawLight / DrawShadowMap)
bug_class: C11 main-thread mutation of a render-thread-read object (SunLight) under ext.render_pipe
label: ext
label_evidence: ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync / ExtSyncMaxShadowRes(true) are marked NOT RETAIL (ext.max_shadow_res, SunLight.h 'called by the registry between frames on the main thread'). The pass-2 readers are retail bodies: lights_vtable.cpp:583 and :655 (SunLight slots, retail 0x1801067e9.. and 0x180106bc0).
reachability: ext.max_shadow_res and ext.render_pipe on, with the overlap governor on (busy frame). The player presses Apply in the Options dialog (optionsdialog.cpp:1007) or toggles the max_shadow_res / max_shadow_size row (registry_boot.cpp:307/322). Both run in UpdateLoop::Update inside MainLoop::Frame's steps. Under P13_OVERLAP those steps run beside the previous packet's E1, which includes Pass2. Pass2 draws the live SunLight: snapshot.cpp only admits a SunLight drawable and does not copy it.
root_cause: The seam assumes that 'between frames on the main thread' means the render thread is idle. Under P13_OVERLAP, Update runs while the previous packet's Pass2 is in flight on the render thread. The seam does not check RenderPipe pending/overlap state as fixes 4 and 5 do for SunLight::Set and PlayerController::UpdateCamera.
minimal_fix: Make ExtRequestMaxShadowResSync only latch a main-thread request flag (no descriptor or settingsChanged writes). Consume the flag in the pass-1 call (SunLight::AddDrawItems -> ExtSyncMaxShadowRes), which runs in the main half after the join. Alternatively, have the request call into render_pipe to WaitIdle (settle the tail) before rewriting the descriptors.

title: Port-only counter `++g_fcc.closeFile` in FileSystem::CloseFile races across every thread that closes a file
bug_class: data race on shared global (port instrumentation)
label: port
label_evidence: RtIO::g_fcc (FsCreateCounters, filesystem_createfile.cpp:158-164) is port-only. The banner gives retail CloseFile 0x1800accc0 as starting with PlatformCloseFile (1800accde) and has no counter. The same file's g_fcc.platClose (line 411) and closeRenamed (line 422) are on the same path.
proof:
Same pattern as the TSan-confirmed g_fsc race (file_stream.cpp:729). It was not run separately. Exact interleaving:
1. The Audio::Stream worker finishes a track and calls `fsys->CloseFile(st._file)` (audio_stream_run.cpp:491), which runs `++RtIO::g_fcc.closeFile` (filesystem_createfile.cpp:467).
2. Concurrently, the Persistence worker's GetSaveInfoJob calls `fs->CloseFile(bfs._file)` (persistence_saveinfo_job.cpp:298/309) during the in-game load dialog's save-list scan, or the Loader thread closes a resource stream during world load.
3. Both run a plain non-atomic RMW on the same uint64_t: a data race, which is UB.
CloseFile also runs from ~FileStream (file_stream.cpp:730) on each of those threads.
root_cause: A plain global counter is added to a FileSystem member that the main, Loader, Persistence and Audio::Stream threads all call.
minimal_fix: Remove the g_fcc counters (createPath..fsDtor) along with their reporter, or make the fields std::atomic<uint64_t> with relaxed increments.

title: Explicit `~Array()` on live PersistenceWorker members followed by SetSize/reuse and a second implicit destruction: object used after its lifetime ended
bug_class: UB: use of an object after its destructor ran ([basic.life]); double destruction
label: port
label_evidence: Retail calls the out-of-line Array clear/free routines 0x180024aa0 / 0x18002a930 as ordinary functions on live members, and the object keeps living. The port spells those calls as C++ destructor calls `w->_blockPtrs.~Array();` (persistence_worker.cpp:335, 420, 421; persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:82-83) and then calls SetSize on the same object (persistence_worker.cpp:336, 435-436). ~PersistenceWorker later runs ~Array on these members a second time. The UB comes from the C++ spelling, not from retail's bytes.
reachability: Every save, load, delete and save-info request on the persistence worker: EnqueueSave, EnqueueLoad and BeginGetSaveGameInfo run each time the save or load dialog is used and on every autosave.
proof: persistence_worker.cpp:335-336: `w->_blockPtrs.~Array();  w->_blockPtrs.SetSize(w->_blockDescs._size);`. persistence_worker.cpp:420-436: `w->_blockDescs.~Array(); w->_blockPtrs.~Array(); ... w->_blockDescs.SetSize(blockCount); w->_blockPtrs.SetSize(blockCount);`. persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:82-83: the same two explicit destructor calls, after which LoadJob/GetSaveInfoJob use the arrays. Under [basic.life]/6-7, calling a non-static member function (SetSize) on an object whose destructor has run, without a new object having been constructed in its storage, is undefined. The member is destroyed again at ~PersistenceWorker (class.dtor/19: destroying an object whose lifetime has ended is UB). It works today only because ArrayDtorImpl re-zeroes {data,size,capacity} and the build passes -fno-lifetime-dse. That flag is mandatory for this reason (memory reference_lifetime_dse_deletes_dtor_null_stores), so an optimiser treating the post-destructor stores as dead would leave a dangling _data that the next SetSize frees again.
root_cause: The port mapped retail's call to the Array destroy-and-zero routine onto the C++ destructor, which ends the object's lifetime, instead of onto the non-destructor member that does the same work.
minimal_fix: Replace each explicit `X.~Array()` on a live member with `X.DestroyAndFree()` (Collection.h:557, the same ClearCallback + ArrayDtorImpl body and the same calls, frees and stores) at persistence_worker.cpp:335/420/421 and persistence_begin_saveinfo.cpp:82/83.

title: External::Load compares uninitialised `magic` and `version` locals when a truncated resource makes the reader's Read fail
bug_class: read of uninitialised local
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail reads [RSP+0x34] (magic) and [RSP+0x30] (version) after the SerializeInt calls and never initialises them. The port leaves both uninitialised on purpose (comment at :289-291). BinaryReader::SerializeInt ignores Stream::Read's result (serialize_family.cpp:291-294), and CompressedStream::Read returns false without writing once SetWindow fails past the end (compressed_stream_read.cpp:439-441).
reachability: Any resource load whose compressed stream ends early: a valid container shorter than 4 bytes (magic), or one that ends after magic+typeId (version). Mod packages supply these bytes. The comparison then reads an indeterminate stack value, so whether the load proceeds into GetFileVersion and Serialize on a truncated stream depends on stack garbage.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (faithful): retail 0x1800bc620:
 1800bc6da: LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x34]
 1800bc6df: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xa0]   ; SerializeInt(magic), result ignored
 1800bc6e5: CMP dword ptr [RSP + 0x34],0x5412a91f
 1800bc772: LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x30]
 1800bc777: CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xa0]   ; SerializeInt(version)
 1800bc786: CMP dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],EAX
No store to [RSP+0x30]/[RSP+0x34] before either call. Port :292 `int32_t magic; SerInt(rw, &magic); if (magic != kCompiledMagic)` and :347 `int32_t version; SerInt(rw, &version); if (version != objVersion)`.
root_cause: Retail never initialises the out-parameters of SerializeInt, and the reader's short-read failure is silently dropped.
minimal_fix: Initialise both locals (`int32_t magic = 0; int32_t version = -1;` or 0). Valid files behave the same, and a short file then deterministically takes the bad-magic or bad-version exit.

title: UpdateList state 4 runs LoadMetaData on an empty embedded SavedState when state 3 skipped BeginLoad: memmove(dst, nullptr, 0) and a serializer over a failed Open
bug_class: UB (null pointer to memmove) via an unawaited worker status
label: retail
label_evidence: The port transcribes retail UpdateList: state 3 has the guard inside the state but advances unconditionally (port banner: 'The guard is INSIDE the state; the transition is not'). LoadMetaData 0x1800c1b30 copies [this+0x30] for [this+0x2c] bytes with no null test, and its tail zeroes both fields (0x1800c1d98..db5), so the embedded state is {null, 0} after any earlier row.
reachability: Opening the Load or Save dialog with several saves, when an info job (open, header read and whole-file CRC) takes longer than one frame and finishes within the next.
proof: saveload_update.cpp:1602-1615 (state 3): BeginLoad is issued only when `(_runFlags & 1) == 0 && _status == 1`, but `_progress = 4` is set unconditionally. :1621-1624 (state 4): `if ((_runFlags & 1) == 0 && _status == 1) LoadMetaData(...)`. If the info job from state 2 is still busy at state 3 and has finished (status 1) by state 4, LoadMetaData runs with no load issued. saveload_loadmeta.cpp:268-271: `_memoryStream.Open((int)_embeddedState._size); std::memmove(_memoryStream._data, _embeddedState._data, _embeddedState._size);` runs with _embeddedState = {nullptr, 0}: the previous call ended with `_data = nullptr; _size = 0;` (:367-369) and SetupLoad was not run. memmove with a null source is UB even for n == 0 (C17 7.1.4; glibc nonnull, which UBSan's nonnull-attribute check flags). CompressedStream::Open then fails (len < 4), and the Serializer, description and width/height reads all run over a stream whose reads fail, so the row is filled from failed reads instead of the 'no metadata' arm.
root_cause: State 3 advances whether or not it issued the load, and state 4 decides from a status word shared with the previous (info) job.
minimal_fix: In state 3, return without advancing while the worker is busy (`if (_worker._runFlags & 1) return;`). Or take state 4's 'no metadata' arm when `_embeddedState._data == nullptr`.

title: fix.save_failure_notice: state 2 polls the persistence worker's plain int32 _status through a volatile cast while the worker thread writes it (data race), and then frees the saved state on that unsynchronised read
bug_class: C12 ownership across threads (data race / missing release-acquire)
label: ext
label_evidence: The read is inside the EXT SEAM block `if (_extFixSaveResult != nullptr && *_extFixSaveResult && _extSaveResult != nullptr)` (NOT RETAIL, docs/retail_bugs.md §27). The comment says retail finishes state 2 without reading the worker's status. The writer is the seam's own NOT RETAIL viaTemp arm in persistence_worker.cpp SaveJob (`_status = wroteAll ? 1 : 2;`, with the comment 'The status is stored last, so a reader that sees 1 finds the save in place').
reachability: On every in-game save with the default-ON row: state 2 of SaveLoad::UpdateSave polls each frame while the PersistenceWorker thread runs SaveJob.
proof: Reader, main thread, saveload_update.cpp:999: `const int32_t status = *static_cast<const volatile int32_t*>(&persistence->_worker._status); if (g_extSaveQueued && status == 0) return; _extSaveResult(g_extSaveQueued && status == 1);`. The SavedState is freed right after (`MemFree(heap->_data); MemFree(heap);`). Writer, worker thread, persistence_worker.cpp SaveJob: `_status = wroteAll ? 1 : 2;` (plain store), then `Fs()->CloseFile(bfs._file)`. Declaration, Persistence.h:415: `int32_t _status; // +0x38`, which is neither std::atomic nor accessed through atomics. A plain write on one thread and a concurrent read on another is a data race under [intro.races]. volatile adds no synchronisation, and the comment's 'a reader that sees 1 finds the save in place' (the FileReplace finished, and the worker is done with the block buffers the main thread then frees) has no release/acquire pair behind it. No TSan run was made.
root_cause: The seam turns the worker's status word into a cross-thread completion flag that orders the main thread's free of the SavedState after the worker's writes and its file move. The field is a plain int, read through a volatile cast, so there is no happens-before edge.
minimal_fix: Do the seam's accesses with atomics without changing the struct layout: on the worker, `__atomic_store_n(&_status, wroteAll ? 1 : 2, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)` (or std::atomic_ref<int32_t>); in state 2, `__atomic_load_n(&persistence->_worker._status, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)` instead of the volatile cast. Also make EnqueueSave's `_status = 0` store (saveload_update.cpp:1462) atomic.
module: src/ext fix.* rows (default ON: read src/ext/registry.h / registry_boot.cpp for which rows are fixes)

title: System::Thread hands &_runFlags of a heap Thread object to the DiagThreads registry, which never forgets it; the sampler can read it after the object is freed
bug_class: C12 cross-thread lifetime: cached pointer outlives its object
label: ext
label_evidence: The DiagThreads::RegisterNamed call in Thread::ThreadFunc is marked 'NOT RETAIL (block LOADSTAMP)'. Retail 0x1800ca440 is only the two waits and two virtual calls quoted in the banner above it.
reachability: Only with the sampler on (BANISHED_SAMPLE, diag builds and perf runs) while a System::Thread subclass is destroyed; the race window is narrow.
proof: Static reading only. thread.cpp:200 runs `DiagThreads::RegisterNamed(typeid(*self).name(), &self->_runFlags)` from the worker. diag_threads.cpp stores that pointer in g_slots[i].busy and has no Unregister. diag/win/sampler.cpp copies it into Tracked::busy (RefreshTracked) and later, in WantSample, does `if (WaitForSingleObject(t.h,0) != WAIT_TIMEOUT) {dead}` and then `... (*t.busy & 1u)`. Thread::ReleaseFields does EventSet(_hStop), ThreadJoin, and then the owning subclass (Engine::Loader, Audio::Stream, IO::PersistenceWorker, PathfinderThread) frees its storage. If the sampler's liveness probe passes just before the join completes and the object is deleted before the next line runs, *t.busy reads freed heap. That is a TOCTOU use-after-free on the sampler thread whenever BANISHED_SAMPLE is on and a System::Thread subclass is destroyed mid-run (for example the loader at the end of a world build, or audio streams).
root_cause: The busy word is owned by the Thread object, but the registry and the sampler treat it as living as long as the OS thread id. Thread exit is checked separately from the read, and nothing clears the slot before the object is freed.
minimal_fix: In Thread::ReleaseFields, after ThreadJoin, clear the registry slot for that thread: add DiagThreads::Forget(tid) or a Forget(busy) that stores nullptr into the slot. The sampler must also re-load the busy pointer from the registry (an acquire load) each tick instead of caching it in Tracked. A simpler alternative: register a pointer to a thread_local or static busy word that the worker mirrors, so the sampler never dereferences object storage.

title: ComboElement::_openDialog dangles after its parent dialog closes with the drop-down still open; ~ComboElement then reads and closes the freed ComboDialog (heap use-after-free)
bug_class: C1 stale cached pointer / use-after-free
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail behaves the same way. ~ComboElement 0x180112490 reads +0x120 and, when it is non-null, calls CloseDialog through [open+0x10]. ~ComboDialog 0x180111cd0 only restamps the vptr and JMPs to ~DialogInstance, and the inherited OnClosed 0x180115330 only walks the controllers. No retail path clears the combo's +0x120 when the popup is closed by its parent.
reachability: Plausible in game: a dialog that hosts a ComboElement (CropUI's selectResource combo in the crop-field info panel, ConsumeProduceUI, Options, NewGame, Help) is closed by code rather than by a click while its drop-down is open. Example: the port's EntityList_CloseDialogsForDyingEntities closes the info panel when the field is removed, or a hotkey or tool closes the panel. A click outside the drop-down does not trigger it, because ComboDialog::OnUpdate nulls _openDialog first.
proof: GHIDRA-DIFF (retail and port match; the defect is retail's own): ~ComboDialog 0x180111cd0: `LEA RAX,[0x1801590e0] ; MOV [RCX],RAX ; ADD RSP,0x38 ; JMP 0x180114d40`. It does not clear _combo->_openDialog. OnClosed 0x180115330: `CALL 0x180114240 ; ... MOV RAX,[RSI+0x78] ; MOV RCX,[RDI+RAX] ; CALL [RAX+0x30]` loops over the controllers only. ~ComboElement 0x180112490: `MOV RCX,[RCX+0x120] ; TEST RCX,RCX ; JZ ; MOV [RSP+0x48],RCX ; LEA RDX,[RSP+0x48] ; MOV RCX,[RCX+0x10] ; CALL 0x180120f20`. The port matches at comboelement.cpp:205-208: `ComboDialog* const open = _openDialog; if (open != nullptr) { ...; open->_ui->CloseDialog(&slot); }`. Sequence: (1) ComboElement::Update creates the popup with parent = the owning dialog (combodialog_ctor.cpp:417 links it into the parent's _children) and sets _openDialog. (2) Something closes the parent while the popup is open. CloseDialog Block A (userinterface_close.cpp) first closes the child popup, which pushes it to _removedDialogs[0], then pushes the parent to [1]. (3) CleanRemovedDialogs deletes [0], freeing the ComboDialog. It then deletes [1], whose root element tree runs ~ComboElement. _openDialog still points at the freed ComboDialog, so the code reads open->_ui (+0x10). CloseDialog then reads the freed dlg->_children._count (+0x48) in Block A. Under the BANISHED_SANITIZE=asan engine heap this is a heap-use-after-free read. On the retail arena the stale bytes usually still hold valid-looking values, which is why it goes unnoticed.
root_cause: The drop-down's lifetime is owned by the UserInterface (the child-of-parent close plus CleanRemovedDialogs), but the ComboElement keeps a raw back-pointer to it. That pointer is cleared only on the drop-down's own close routes (OnUpdate, OnElementEvent, SetCurrentItem, RemoveAllItems), not when the parent closes it in CloseDialog Block A.
minimal_fix: Plain hardening, at the root-cause site: clear the back-pointer when the drop-down goes away. In ComboDialog::~ComboDialog (or an OnClosed override), do `if (_combo && _combo->_openDialog == this) _combo->_openDialog = nullptr;`. Retail has the same defect, so this would be a fix.* row or a documented retail_bugs.md entry under the faithful-first rule.

title: ProfessionUI::OnOpened allocates the BST node before the search, frees it on a duplicate key, then reads newNode->parent from the freed block and still bumps the count
bug_class: use-after-free (read) / count drift
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x140076ca0 walks the tree first and allocates (CALL [0x140152b60]) only at a null child. On an equal key it jumps from 0x14007707b (JNC 0x140077131) past both the rebalance (0x140077128) and the `INC dword ptr [R14 + 0x68]` count at 0x14007712d. The port allocates first, MemFrees on a duplicate, reads the freed node, and always increments professionIndexCount.
reachability: Needs the same Profession* twice in GameUpdateLoop::m_professionList->professions. ProfessionList::Startup fills it from distinct ExternalFactory entries, so the stock game and the current loaders do not produce a duplicate. The UAF is latent (a second Startup on the same list, or a future loader that appends) and was not reproduced.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x140076ca0 duplicate arm:
140077070: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]        ; node key
140077073: CMP RBX,RAX ; JC 0x140077094   ; less -> left
140077078: CMP RAX,RBX
14007707b: JNC 0x140077131                ; equal -> skip alloc, rebalance and count
...
14007711f: LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x38] ; LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x60]
140077128: CALL 0x140013480               ; rebalance (insert path only)
14007712d: INC dword ptr [R14 + 0x68]     ; count (insert path only)
140077131: LEA R8,[RBX + 0x30]            ; duplicate lands here
Port professionui.cpp:385-430: `ProfNode* newNode = MemAlloc(0x30, 8);` before the walk; on a duplicate `System::MemoryAllocator::MemFree(newNode); inserted = true;` (line 420), then `if (newNode->parent != nullptr)` (line 424) reads the freed block, and `professionIndexCount = professionIndexCount + 1;` (line 430) runs for the duplicate too.
root_cause: The tree was ported as allocate-then-insert with a free-on-duplicate fallback, instead of retail's search-then-allocate. The rebalance guard and the count increment were then placed after the merge point that both arms share.
minimal_fix: Search for the key first and allocate only when a null child is reached (retail's order). On an equal key, skip the allocation, the rebalance and the professionIndexCount increment. As the smallest change: on the duplicate arm, set newNode = nullptr after the MemFree, skip the parent test, and do not increment the count.

title: BuildPathGraph zero-extends the entity anchor cell before indexing map cells; retail sign-extends (MOVSXD)
bug_class: C7 wrong width/sign in an index
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400d732a MOVSXD R11,EAX on GetAnchorCell's result, then [RCX+RDX*8+0x18] with RDX = R11*6. The port writes `cells[(int64_t)(uint32_t)entityCell]`.
reachability: Low: only if an entity in a CitizenBehavior +0x100 profession bucket has no InteractComponent nodes and no MapComponent.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail 0x1400d70c0:
1400d7325: CALL 0x140087fb0            ; EntityAnchorCell -> int (may be -1)
1400d732a: MOVSXD R11,EAX
1400d7331: LEA RDX,[R11 + R11*0x2]
1400d7335: ADD RDX,RDX
1400d733c: MOV RCX,qword ptr [R8 + 0x80]
1400d7343: MOV ESI,dword ptr [RCX + RDX*0x8 + 0x18]   ; cells[(int)cell].regionId
Port citizenbehavior.cpp:515:
    int entityRegion = cells[(int64_t)(uint32_t)entityCell].regionId;
EntityAnchorCell (action_pf_road.cpp:503) returns -1 when the entity has neither an InteractComponent with nodes nor a MapComponent.
root_cause: The wrong cast width. For -1, retail reads cells[-1] (0x30 bytes before the array: an out-of-bounds read, UB in both binaries). The port reads cells[0xFFFFFFFF], about 192 GiB past the array, which is a guaranteed access violation. The other three cell indexings in this function and in ProcessPaths sign-extend correctly.
minimal_fix: `int entityRegion = cells[(int64_t)entityCell].regionId;` (matching retail's MOVSXD). The -1 itself is a separate retail out-of-bounds read.

title: Signed 64-bit overflow in the bucket tick delta (currentTime - _lastUpdateTime) with save-supplied times
bug_class: signed integer overflow (UB)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail computes the same subtraction as a wrapping SUB (decompiled `local_58[0] = *param_1 - *(longlong *)(local_res18 + 0x20); if (0 < local_58[0])` at 0x1400c4090). The port's int64_t subtraction is C++ UB when it overflows. The arithmetic is faithful; the UB comes only from C++.
proof: Port line 916: `int64_t delta = currentTime - entIBP->_lastUpdateTime._ticks;`. Both operands are serialized: EntityList::accumulatedTime through Time::Serialize at line ~1577, and each entity's _lastUpdateTime at line ~1621. A save with accumulatedTime = INT64_MAX - k and an entity whose _lastUpdateTime = -1 makes the subtraction overflow on the first Update. -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow reports it. Without the sanitizer, GCC may assume no overflow for the `delta > 0` test that follows. `*this += *time` in Update's step 1 (System::Time operator+=, accumulatedTime._ticks) has the same exposure once accumulatedTime is near INT64_MAX.
root_cause: Retail's two's-complement wrap on 64-bit tick values is ported as signed C++ arithmetic, with operands that come straight from the save.
minimal_fix: Do the subtraction in unsigned and convert: `int64_t delta = (int64_t)((uint64_t)currentTime - (uint64_t)entIBP->_lastUpdateTime._ticks);`. This keeps retail's wrap exactly. Or bound both times at load.

title: PathTool::BuildRoutes calls ~Array() on three live members, then keeps using them (use after end of lifetime)
bug_class: UB: object used after its destructor ran (basic.life)
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x1400dd770 inlines the free-and-zero body (MemFree, then zero _data and the size/capacity qword); it has no C++ destructor. The port spells it as an explicit `routes.~Array(); points.~Array(); segments.~Array();` and then calls routes.SetSize, points.SetSize and segments.SetSize on the same objects with no new construction. tool_base_highlight_tess.cpp does the same job correctly with DestroyAndFree().
reachability: Runs every time the path tool's selection changes (BuildRoutes, from SetSelected).
proof: pathtool_setselected.cpp:330-332 calls `routes.~Array(); points.~Array(); segments.~Array();`. Later lines use the same objects: 386 reads `routes._data[r]`, PushRoute calls `routes.SetSize(...)`, and 436-440 call `points.SetSize(points._size + 1, ...)` and `segments.SetSize(...)`. Array::~Array (src/engine/Collection/Collection.h:563) only calls DestroyAndFree(). After an explicit destructor call the object's lifetime has ended, so the stores the destructor made (zeroing _data) are dead to the optimiser. CMakeLists.txt:78-91 documents that GCC's lifetime DSE deletes exactly these stores, and the build relies on -fno-lifetime-dse to survive it (memory reference_lifetime_dse_deletes_dtor_null_stores). Without that flag, the next SetSize reallocates from a freed _data, which is a use-after-free.
root_cause: The ENDGAME B.3.2 cleanup replaced the inlined free-and-zero body with an explicit destructor call instead of the non-destructor DestroyAndFree().
minimal_fix: Replace the three `X.~Array();` calls with `X.DestroyAndFree();`. The bytes are the same and the objects stay alive.

title: The tutorial highlight's world-entity target (+0xE8) is a raw entity pointer with no Forget; if that entity is removed while the step is active, OnUpdateLayout reads the freed entity every frame
bug_class: C1 side pointer outlives the entity (use after free)
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail OnUpdateLayout 0x1400dffe0 is `CMP [RCX+0xe8],0; JNZ 0x1400dfda0; JMP 0x1400dfac0`. 0x1400dfda0 passes [RBP+0xe8] straight to 0x140100380, which runs FindComponent<ModelComponent> on it, with no validity test. The port mirrors this exactly. No code in src references TutorialHighlightDialog outside src/game/Tutorial, so no entity-removal path closes the highlight or clears +0xE8.
reachability: SUSPECTED. It needs a tutorial step whose TutorialSetupDialog points at a building through toolbarRef/toolbarIndex, and the player removing that building (demolish, or the building burning down) before the step ends. TutorialSetupRestrictPlayer may disable the demolish tool during such steps, and the tutorial data was not inspected, so reachability on shipped content is unproven.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF (faithful, not a diff): 0x1400dfda0:
1400dfdd9: MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBP + 0xe8]   ; targetEntity, untested
1400dfde0: LEA R8,[RSP + 0x30]
1400dfde5: LEA RDX,[RSP + 0xa0]
1400dfded: MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0xa0],RAX
1400dfdf5: CALL 0x140100380                ; FindComponent on the entity
Port: `ComponentEntity* entityIBP = targetEntity; bool ok = PlayerScreenRect_EntityRect_0380(&rect, &entityIBP, &rect)`, followed by the port-only TutHLDiag(entityIBP, ...), which walks entity->_components as well. The entity is taken in OpenHighlightDialog (0x1400e2700) from CitizenBehavior +0x160 bucket[toolbarIndex] and stored by value. TutorialSetupDialog::Update calls OpenHighlightDialog(1), which returns while a highlight exists, so the stored pointer is never refreshed for the life of the step.
root_cause: InternalPtr in this engine is a plain pointer (AssignId / CheckPtr are bare RETs), so the highlight keeps no reference on the entity, and nothing removes the highlight or clears the target when the entity is removed.
