minimal_fix: Hardening as a fix.* row (retail shares the defect): in PlaceOnEntity, re-resolve the target each frame from the owning TutorialSetupDialog (bucket[toolbarIndex] of CitizenBehavior +0x160), or close the highlight from the entity-removal path when the removed entity is its target.

title: Android ReapplyPreferredFrameRate runs on the render thread (CreateSwapchain under ext.render_pipe): it calls SDL_GetWindowProperties, documented main-thread-only, and uses the ANativeWindow pointer without holding a reference while the Java UI thread may release it
bug_class: SDL video call off the main thread / native handle lifetime
label: ext
label_evidence: NOT RETAIL (P12 preferred frame rate; Android only). The call site is src/render/vulkan/device.cpp:544, at the end of CreateSwapchain, reached from ContextData::BeginCommands (device.cpp:1416), which runs on the render thread under ext.render_pipe. window_android.cpp:38-39 itself notes that the swap chain is rebuilt on the render thread.
reachability: Every swap-chain rebuild on Android with render_pipe on: back from the background, a rotation or a resize. SDL's onNativeSurfaceDestroyed (third_party/SDL/src/core/android/SDL_android.c:1337-1340) runs on the Java UI thread. Under SDL's private Android_ActivityMutex, which the app cannot take, it clears SDL_PROP_WINDOW_ANDROID_WINDOW_POINTER and calls ANativeWindow_release.
proof: window_android.cpp:124-130: `SDL_Window* window = Sdl::GameWindow(); void* native = SDL_GetPointerProperty(SDL_GetWindowProperties(window), SDL_PROP_WINDOW_ANDROID_WINDOW_POINTER, nullptr); ... g_setFrameRate(native, g_preferredFps, kFrameRateCompatibilityFixedSource);`. SDL_video.h documents SDL_GetWindowProperties as `\threadsafety This function should only be called on the main thread.` g_frameRateLock serialises only this file's two callers, not SDL's Java-thread release, so `native` can be released between the property read and ANativeWindow_setFrameRate. A second problem: the `native == g_frameRateWindow` short-circuit (line 129) compares raw addresses, so a new ANativeWindow allocated at the released one's address is never told the rate. No sanitizer run is possible: this needs an Android device.
root_cause: A main-thread SDL query and an unowned native-handle use were placed in a hook that the Vulkan backend calls from its render thread.
minimal_fix: Do not touch SDL or the native window from the render thread. Have ReapplyPreferredFrameRate set an atomic 'reapply pending' flag, and run ApplyFrameRateLocked from the main thread: the frame limiter's per-frame path, or the DID_ENTER_FOREGROUND / SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_RESIZED handling. Wrap the native pointer in ANativeWindow_acquire / ANativeWindow_release around setFrameRate, and drop the address-equality cache (or reset it on WILL_ENTER_BACKGROUND).

title: RenderStateData::Create indexes the blend/compare/stencil/cull/fill tables with serialized RenderState fields (out-of-bounds read)
bug_class: unchecked serialized index / layout table OOB
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail 0x1800037c0-0x180003990 indexes stack-built tables with each field and no bounds check: 1800037d3 movslq 0x6c(%rdi),%rax (fillMode) ; 1800037f0 mov 0x100(%rbp,%rax,4),%ecx ; 180003801 movslq 0x68(%rdi),%rax (cullMode) ; 180003816 mov -0x58(%rbp,%rax,4),%ecx ; 180003914 movslq 0x24(%rdi),%rax (srcBlend) ; 180003918 mov 0x20(%rsp,%rax,4),%ecx ; 18000392a movslq 0x2c(%rdi),%rax (blendOp) ; 18000392e mov 0x78(%rsp,%rax,4),%ecx ; 180003977 movslq 0x38(%rdi),%rax (depth func) ; 18000397b mov -0x78(%rbp,%rax,4),%ecx.
reachability: Any RenderState resource read from a .rsc (material render states in a mod package or a corrupted resource) whose enum field exceeds its table.
proof: Retail sequence quoted in label_evidence: every index is movslq'd from the RenderState and used directly in a scaled load. Port lines 345-394 do the same: kBlendFactor[10][srcBlend/dstBlend], kBlendOp[3][blendOp], kFillMode[2][_fillMode], kCullMode[3][_cullMode], kCompareFunc[8][depth.func / stencil.func], kStencilOp[8][fail/depthFail/pass and back*]. All of these fields come from Video::RenderState::Serialize (src/engine/video/renderstate.cpp:136-150, 165-176, 296-297) as raw uint32 reads with no range check. Example: blendOp = 3 reads kBlendOp[3], one past the 3-entry table, and fillMode = 2 reads kFillMode[2]. The port's fields are uint32_t while retail sign-extends them, so a negative value lands on opposite sides in the two builds; both are out of bounds.
root_cause: The engine enum values are used directly as D3D11 translation-table indexes, and nobody validates them after the serializer reads them.
minimal_fix: Range-check each field against its table size in RenderStateData::Create, falling back to the RenderState constructor default (srcBlend 1, func 4, ...) or failing the create. Validating in RenderState::Serialize would also work.

title: VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate indexes the 9-entry kElementFormat table with the serialized element format (out-of-bounds read)
bug_class: unchecked serialized index / layout table OOB
label: retail
label_evidence: Retail VideoDX11-x64.dll 0x180003ff0 has the same unchecked index. It builds the 9-dword table on the stack (movl $0x2,0x30(%rsp) ... movl $0x1c,0x50(%rsp)) and indexes it with the sign-extended element format: 180004095 movslq -0x8(%rax,%rdx,1),%rcx ; 1800040a4 mov 0x30(%rsp,%rcx,4),%eax ; 1800040a8 mov %eax,0x4c(%rsp,%rdx,1). There is no compare on rcx anywhere in the loop.
reachability: Any vertex layout loaded from a resource file: a mod package's MeshLayout .rsc, or a corrupted one, with an element format of 9 or more.
proof: Retail disassembly (objdump VideoDX11-x64.dll), no range check on format: 180004073 mov 0x20(%r9),%rax ; 180004077 lea 0x20(%rdx),%rdx ; 180004095 movslq -0x8(%rax,%rdx,1),%rcx (element+0x18 = format) ; 18000409a mov %rdi,0x40(%rsp,%rdx,1) ("TEXCOORD") ; 1800040a4 mov 0x30(%rsp,%rcx,4),%eax ; 1800040a8 mov %eax,0x4c(%rsp,%rdx,1) (desc.Format). Port line 198: descs[i].Format = kElementFormat[elems[i].format]; with static const DXGI_FORMAT kElementFormat[9]. Source of format: src/engine/video/vertexlayout.cpp:137-139 reads it with rw->SerializeUInt(format) from the MeshLayout*.rsc stream and stores it unvalidated. A format value >= 9 reads past the 36-byte table (the port's table is static; retail's is on the stack). D3D11 then gets an arbitrary DXGI_FORMAT, and CreateInputLayout fails, leaving inputLayout null.
root_cause: The engine element format (0..8) is used directly as a table index. Neither the serializer nor the backend validates it.
minimal_fix: In PlatformCreate, treat format >= 9 as invalid: skip the layout and leave inputLayout null, as the signature-size-0 early return does. Range-checking at VertexLayout::Serialize would also work.

title: Metal BeginCommands clears Device::settingsChanged without checking whether a rebuild ran: a resize, DPI or shadow-map request raised meanwhile (render_pipe) or while minimised is lost, so the back buffer is never rebuilt (black frames, viewport past the attachment)
bug_class: C10 swapchain/resize: lost settingsChanged; data race on a non-atomic flag
label: ext
label_evidence: src/render/metal is the macOS backend with no retail counterpart; retail renders through VideoDX11-x64.dll only.
reachability: Shape 1: any request that raises settingsChanged while the macOS window is minimised (a sun-map or AO request, a fullscreen chord). Shape 2: ext.render_pipe on, with a drag-resize, a display-scale change or an Options Apply in the built game; the final resize event of a drag can be the one lost.
root_cause: The flag is cleared as a separate, unconditional store after the size read, not consumed atomically where it is applied. The clear also runs on the minimised early return, where nothing was rebuilt.
minimal_fix: Consume the flag where it is applied: under dev->Lock(), copy it and reset it to 0 only when ApplyEngineSettingsChange actually rebuilt (return a bool; leave the flag set when the window is minimised or mainColor is nil). Delete the unconditional store at line 1178. Make the cross-thread access atomic (std::atomic_ref<uint8_t> exchange) or keep every writer and the consumer under the device lock.

title: Swap-chain rebuild destroys renderFinished semaphores that pending presents may still wait on (vkDeviceWaitIdle does not cover present)
bug_class: GPU resource lifetime (present semaphores)
label: ext
label_evidence: Vulkan backend swap chain, no retail counterpart.
proof: BeginCommands (device.cpp:1413-1415) runs vkDeviceWaitIdle(device) and then CreateSwapchain. CreateSwapchain calls DestroySwapchainObjects() (:504), which runs `for (VkSemaphore s : renderFinished) vkDestroySemaphore(device, s, nullptr);` (:372). It then destroys the old swapchain. Each renderFinished[i] is the wait semaphore of the last vkQueuePresentKHR on image i (:1537-1542). The rebuild is reached right after a present that returned VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR or VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR, and after an acquire that reported SUBOPTIMAL (swapchainDirty). Device idle covers queue submissions, not the present engine's semaphore waits. Without VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 present fences, nothing establishes that those waits completed before the destroy. This is the destroy-in-use case of VUID-vkDestroySemaphore-semaphore-05149 that the Khronos swapchain-semaphore guidance warns about.
root_cause: The lifetime of the present-wait semaphores is tied to the swapchain rebuild instead of to proof that the present engine consumed them.
minimal_fix: Do not destroy renderFinished on rebuild. Keep the semaphores (one per image is enough to reuse across swapchains), or retire them until their image has been re-acquired from the new or old swapchain. Where available, use VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 present fences and destroy the semaphores after those fences signal.

title: A failed vkCreateSwapchainKHR leaves the retired old swap chain in `swapchain`, and the retry passes it again as oldSwapchain
bug_class: Vulkan valid-usage violation (UB) on a swap-chain rebuild failure
label: ext
reachability: Any vkCreateSwapchainKHR failure after the first swap chain, for example a resize, fullscreen toggle, OUT_OF_DATE / SUBOPTIMAL rebuild, or an Android rotation that hits VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR, VK_ERROR_NATIVE_WINDOW_IN_USE_KHR or an out-of-memory error. The code already special-cases DEVICE_LOST here (swapchainLost), which shows that failure occurs.
root_cause: The failure path does not account for the old swap chain being retired by the failed call.
minimal_fix: On a failed vkCreateSwapchainKHR with a non-null oldSwapchain, wait for idle, call DestroySwapchainObjects(), vkDestroySwapchainKHR(device, swapchain) and set `swapchain = VK_NULL_HANDLE` before returning false. The retry then creates from VK_NULL_HANDLE, and no acquire or present can reach the retired chain.

title: Null index buffer is emulated with the 64 KiB zero buffer and no robustBufferAccess: a draw past 32768 indices reads out of bounds
bug_class: emulated D3D11 defined-OOB read without robustness
label: ext
reachability: Only when the engine issues an indexed draw with no index buffer bound and more than 32768 indices. The P6 Vulkan GPU-AV run (7 min) and the DX11 debug layer reported no such draw, so it is not observed in normal play.
proof: draw.cpp:1445-1452: `if (!buffer) buffer = ZeroBuffer().buffer;   // D3D11 reads zeros from a null index buffer` then `vkCmdBindIndexBuffer(cb, buffer, 0, VK_INDEX_TYPE_UINT16); vkCmdDrawIndexed(cb, count, instances, first, baseVertex, 0);`. ZeroBuffer is kZeroBufferBytes = 64ull << 10 (resources.cpp:26), i.e. 32768 uint16 indices. D3D11 defines every fetch from a null or short index buffer as 0. Vulkan defines an index fetch past the bound buffer only under robustBufferAccess, and device.cpp never enables it: want2.features has no robustBufferAccess (device.cpp:1143-1152). So `first + count > 32768` with no index buffer bound is UB. The same holds for any real index or vertex buffer fetched past its end, which D3D11 also defines as 0.
root_cause: The D3D11 'null buffer reads 0' rule is emulated with a fixed-size buffer, and robustness is not requested.
minimal_fix: Skip (count as failed) an indexed draw with a null index buffer and first + count > kZeroBufferBytes / 2, or request robustBufferAccess when the device supports it so out-of-bounds index and vertex fetches are defined as on D3D11.

title: Weather effects never spawn or retire their ambient-audio entity (no rain sound); the SetEffectEnabled audio arm and the Update emitter-volume/removal arm are missing
bug_class: C4 retail body never wired (missing call arm)
label: port
reachability: Any rain in any game (state 0, temperature > 34). Also any save loaded while it is raining.
root_cause: The audio half of 0x1400942c0 and the matching emitter arm of 0x1400944e0 were scoped out when the particle half was ported and never wired. AmbientEmitterComponent (MoveTo, PlaySlot) and FindComponent<AmbientEmitterComponent> are ported now (KPI rows 1286/1288), so nothing blocks it.
minimal_fix: In SetEffectEnabled's enable arm, when `arrayBase[slot]` has an audio template (+8), clone and register the entity into emitters[slot], MoveTo (0,0,0) and set volume 0, as retail does. In Update's per-effect loop, set the emitter volume from the effect's intensity, and on removal MarkForRemoval, append to entityList->+0xd0 and null emitters[i], as at 0x1400944e0.

title: FreeType font twins (posix/darwin/android) cache one lookup for whichever face is asked first, so the Arial/Helvetica fallbacks in DefaultFaces can never succeed when the game face is missing
bug_class: error-path: a failure is cached and returned for unrelated requests
label: ext
label_evidence: NOT RETAIL (file banner): font rasterisation for ext.sharp_ui / ext.family_tree. The same body is copied in src/platform/darwin/font_raster_darwin.cpp:259 and src/platform/android/font_raster_android.cpp:60.
reachability: Linux, macOS or Android with ext.family_tree (or ext.sharp_ui) on and no game TTF beside the exe: the family tree renders with 'no font' although a fallback face is installed.
root_cause: A process-wide single-entry cache keyed on nothing: g_lookedUp, g_facePath and g_faceWhy are shared by all face names.
minimal_fix: Key the cache by face, for example `std::map<std::string, std::pair<std::string,std::string>> g_faces;` under g_lock, and look up `g_faces[face]`. Alternatively cache only kGameFace and resolve other names on each call. Apply the change to all three twins.

title: LoadPrivateFace's 'tried once' flag is process-wide, not per face, so a failed private load of one face blocks the shipped game font's private load
bug_class: logic / platform error handling
label: ext
label_evidence: The file banner says NOT RETAIL (KITFREE RSCFONT, ext/resources/font_raster.h). It is the ext rasteriser used by ext.sharp_ui (font_provider.cpp) and ext.family_tree (family_raster.cpp).
reachability: Only when the first face tried is not installed system-wide and the private file of a later face is the one that exists. Most likely on Wine or a stripped Windows install with ext.family_tree on and ext.sharp_ui's FaceOk not yet run (or with sharp_ui off). On a stock Windows install Segoe UI is present and the path is not taken.
proof: Static only, not run. LoadPrivateFace(face) opens with `if (g_privateTried) return g_privateLoaded; g_privateTried = true;` (lines 76-77). The flag and result are single globals (lines 35-36), but the file it tries depends on the face: `<exe dir>/<face>.ttf` (lines 84-85). family_raster.cpp:83-88 (SystemGlyphSource::Glyphs) calls RasterizeFont in order for DefaultFaces() = {"Segoe UI", "Arial", kGameFace}. On a host where Segoe UI is not installed (e.g. Wine), AcquireFace("Segoe UI") calls LoadPrivateFace("Segoe UI"). That finds no Segoe UI.ttf beside the exe and sets g_privateTried = true, g_privateLoaded = false. Every later LoadPrivateFace call then returns false at once, including the one for kGameFace, whose FrancophilSans.ttf the release package ships beside the exe (comment at line 73). The family tree therefore gets 'no font'. Later, FaceAvailable(kGameFace) for ext.sharp_ui (font_provider.cpp:91) also fails, so sharp_ui turns itself off for the session, although the private file exists. The opposite order is also wrong: once the game face has loaded, a later call for a missing face returns true, and the caller gets a misleading 'private <face>.ttf loaded but GDI selected ...' reason.
root_cause: A cache meant to stop repeating AddFontResourceEx for the one shipped font is keyed on nothing, while the function takes the face name as input.
minimal_fix: Key the attempt on the face, e.g. a small std::map<std::wstring, bool> (or set) of faces already tried / loaded under g_lock, or keep the global but only for kGameFace and try other faces' files each time.

title: LoadPrivateFace records 'tried' process-wide for whichever face asks first, so a failed private load of one face stops the bundled FrancophilSans.ttf from ever loading (and a success for one face is reported as a success for every other face)
bug_class: swallowed failure cached as global state
label: ext
label_evidence: The file banner says NOT RETAIL (KITFREE RSCFONT); it is the ext.sharp_ui / ext.family_tree GDI rasteriser.
reachability: This needs a host where an earlier DefaultFaces entry is missing and the family-tree raster runs before the sharp_ui FaceOk check, or any caller that passes a face other than kGameFace first. It is unlikely on stock Windows 10/11 but reachable on Wine/Proton.
proof: `if (g_privateTried) return g_privateLoaded; g_privateTried = true; ... path = <exe dir>\<face>.ttf ...`. The guard ignores `face`. SystemGlyphSource::Glyphs (family_raster.cpp:82-86) tries DefaultFaces in order {"Segoe UI", "Arial", kGameFace}. If the first face is not installed (Wine, a stripped image), LoadPrivateFace("Segoe UI") looks for Segoe UI.ttf, fails and sets g_privateTried. Every later AcquireFace(kGameFace) then returns g_privateLoaded=false without trying FrancophilSans.ttf, which the release package ships beside the exe. FaceOk() (font_provider.cpp:91) caches that false for the session, so ext.sharp_ui's variants stay off. The opposite order is also wrong: after a successful load of FrancophilSans.ttf, a missing "Segoe UI" makes LoadPrivateFace return true, and AcquireFace reports the misleading 'private Segoe UI.ttf loaded but GDI selected ...'.
root_cause: The once-per-process latch (g_privateTried / g_privateLoaded) is one global bool pair, but the work it guards depends on its `face` argument.
minimal_fix: Key the latch by face: keep a small std::map<std::wstring,bool> of attempted faces under g_lock. Or only set the latch when face == kGameFace (the one file the package ships).

title: Port-only IsIconic early-out makes WM_ACTIVATE(WA_INACTIVE) skip SetFullscreenState(FALSE) when a fullscreen game is minimized
bug_class: fullscreen focus-loss path diverges from retail
label: port
label_evidence: Retail 0x180004340 tests only IsWindowVisible (`180004371 CALL [0x1800134e0] / 180004377 TEST EAX,EAX / 180004379 JZ 0x1800044f7`). An iconic window is visible, so retail proceeds to `swapChain->SetFullscreenState(Configuration+0x40 != 0, 0)` (vtable +0x50) with +0x40 just cleared by OnActivate. The port returns 0 before that call.
reachability: Any exclusive-fullscreen session (the default with an empty settings.cfg) that the player minimizes rather than alt-tabs: Win+D, Win+M, or a minimize command. Whether Windows or DWM forcibly revokes exclusive mode on minimize was not verified, so the visible impact (output held in the game's mode, or a black screen until restore) is SUSPECTED.
proof:
GHIDRA-DIFF: retail Resize head `18000435f MOV byte ptr [RAX+0x9c],0x1 / 180004366 MOV RAX,[RCX+0x8] / 18000436a MOV RCX,[RAX+0x90] / 180004371 CALL [0x1800134e0] (IsWindowVisible) / 180004377 TEST EAX,EAX / 180004379 JZ 0x1800044f7 / 18000437f MOV RCX,[RBX+0x28] / 18000438e CALL [RAX+0x108] (OMSetRenderTargets)`, continuing to ResizeTarget(+0x70), ResizeBuffers(+0x68) and SetFullscreenState(+0x50). Port: devicedata.cpp:740 `if (Platform::Window::IsIconic(dev->windowHandle)) return 0;` runs before the ClearState / SetFullscreenState chain.

Sequence on minimize from exclusive fullscreen (Win+D, Win+M, or SC_MINIMIZE): SDL delivers FocusLost through the pump, after the window is already iconic. DeviceData_OnActivate then sets wasFullscreen=1 and cfg->fullscreen=0 and calls Resize, which returns 0. Retail would have dropped DXGI exclusive mode. The port leaves the swap chain in exclusive fullscreen on an iconic window. CreateDevice step 13 passes DXGI_MWA_NO_WINDOW_CHANGES, so DXGI's own focus monitoring does not undo this. Every later BeginCommands retries and early-outs until restore.
root_cause: The IsIconic guard was added for the windowed minimize case, so that a 0x0 size is not latched. It also short-circuits the fullscreen to windowed transition that OnActivate relies on Resize to perform.
minimal_fix: Before the IsIconic early-out, when `cfg->fullscreen == 0 && self->wasFullscreen != 0`, call `self->swapChain->SetFullscreenState(FALSE, nullptr)`. Alternatively, apply the IsIconic early-out only after the fullscreen state has been brought in line with cfg->fullscreen.

title: ImageBufferData::Update writes a texture in place with replaceRegion while up to 3 in-flight frames still sample it (no versioning/staging)
bug_class: gpu-lifetime: resource reused while in flight (dynamic texture versioning)
label: ext
label_evidence: The Metal backend has no retail counterpart. It implements retail VideoDX11 slot 5 (0x180002e10), whose port in src/render/dx11/imagebufferdata.cpp:883 uses Map(WRITE_DISCARD) for a dynamic owner and UpdateSubresource otherwise. Both are versioned/ordered by the driver. The Vulkan twin (companions.cpp:517 UploadImage) also goes through a recorded upload.
reachability: Every gameplay frame where the minimap overlay is dirty, and every ext.terrain_edit brush stroke. macOS Metal build only.
root_cause: The backend treats CopyToTexture like a CPU memcpy into a shared texture. It does not reproduce D3D11's DISCARD/ordered-update semantics, and texture uses get no completion ticket, so frames still executing read texels being overwritten (torn or wrong minimap / ground texture). A call made inside a frame also changes what draws already encoded earlier in the same uncommitted command buffer see.
minimal_fix: Record the update in the command stream: copy the rows into an upload-arena block (Upload()) and encode a blit copyFromBuffer:toTexture: on `commands` (or a private command buffer committed before the frame's when commands is nil). Alternatively, keep per-texture uses with completion tickets as bufferUses does and rename (allocate or recycle a fresh texture, re-point the aliases) when the current texture is busy.

title: Pipeline fast cache evicts an owner's address BEFORE the object dies; a pipeline inserted after the eviction survives address reuse (stale blend/layout/function)
bug_class: gpu-lifetime: address-keyed cache, evict-then-release ordering (ABA)
label: ext
label_evidence: The FastPipelineCache and the EvictPipelineOwner scheme are Metal-backend only. Retail D3D11 binds state objects by COM reference and has no address-keyed pipeline cache.
reachability: A RenderState / VertexLayout / program re-created or destroyed while it is still bound, followed by a draw before the rebind, then an ObjC allocation landing at the freed address. Mostly a device-restore / options-apply / render_pipe loader-thread interleaving.
proof:
Order in backend.mm: RenderStateData::Create (2134-2135) calls EvictPipelineOwner((__bridge void*)blend) and only afterwards replaces `blend = [MTLRenderPipelineColorAttachmentDescriptor new]`. The destructor (2132) likewise evicts while the object is still alive. The old descriptor is NOT freed at that point: RenderStateData::Bind stored it strongly in the global `bound.blend` (2192), and the render thread keeps drawing with it until the next RenderState bind. Pipeline() (backend.mm:315-399) keys on the raw address `blendKey = (__bridge void*)bound.blend` and calls pipelines.Insert(key, state, {vf, pf, layout, blendKey}) at line 399, after the eviction already ran. When bound.blend is later rebound, the old descriptor is released. A new descriptor allocated at the same address then matches the stale entry, and the draw uses a pipeline with the wrong blend factors / write mask. The same order applies to VertexLayoutData::PlatformCreate (evict, then `descriptor = [MTLVertexDescriptor vertexDescriptor]`) and to Vertex/PixelProgramData::PlatformCreate (EvictShaders, then shaders.clear()). With ext.render_pipe the loader thread's Create/destructor and the render thread's Pipeline() run concurrently. CachedPipeline compiles synchronously between the key computation and the Insert, which widens the window.
Model run (clang++-19 -fsanitize=address,undefined, scratchpad p8/src_render_metal_gpu_lifetime/fastcache_evict_order.cpp, which includes the real fast_pipeline_cache.h): Evict(A) then Insert(key{A}) then Find(key{A}) prints `evicted=0 found=1 value=111 (stale pipeline for a different blend state)`, exit 1.
root_cause: Eviction is tied to the owner's destructor or re-create rather than to the moment the address can actually be reused. bound.* holds extra strong references that outlive the eviction, and Pipeline() can insert under the old address afterwards.
minimal_fix: Key the cache on something that cannot be recycled: a monotonically increasing id stored in RenderStateData/VertexLayoutData/Shader at create. Alternatively, have Insert retain the owners (store the id<> objects in the entry so the address cannot be reused while the entry exists) and Evict by identity.

title: Metal command-buffer error handler writes an uncapped stderr line every frame once the GPU faults or the queue is refused (no device-lost route, per-frame log spam in shipped builds)
bug_class: C10 device lost: no recovery route plus hot-path log output
label: ext
label_evidence: Metal backend, no retail counterpart.
reachability: macOS: an eGPU unplug, a GPU fault from a bad draw, or the GPU watchdog timing out a long frame.
root_cause: The completion handler is the backend's only reaction to a command-buffer error, and it logs without a cap. The backend has no device-lost state that would stop submission or start a rebuild.
minimal_fix: Cap the line (e.g. the first 8 errors, then one summary), and on a removed or blacklisted error set a device-lost flag that BeginCommands checks to refuse frames and request the engine's device restart (as DX11 does through OnVideoError).
